# agent-director — Architecture

## What it is

A Go binary (plus an off-PATH operator tool, `agent-director-admin`) that:

- Spawns agent instances (Claude Code, Codex or Cursor, chosen per Spawn) inside tmux sessions.
- Tracks agent state and transcripts through hooks; Cursor uses an owned ACP gateway with correlated reports and protected transcripts. All three agents share request inspection and decisions; Cursor validates ACP permissions/plans and denies questions before admission.
- Reports experimental context fullness through the shared read surfaces using qualified structured evidence; unsupported or unreliable sources return explicit nulls.
- Exposes a CLI for humans and a stdio MCP server for LLM callers — both implemented by the same binary in different modes.

## Surfaces

- **CLI** — `agent-director <verb> ...` for every verb in
  `pkg/api/manifest`. See `docs/cli-reference.md` for the canonical
  list.
- **Internal Cursor gateway** — `agent-director cursor-host`, the direct pane process for a fresh, reused or resumed Cursor row; CLI-only launch plumbing, excluded from MCP discovery and dispatch.
- **Hook entrypoint** — the same binary invoked by the agent on hook events (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostToolUseFailure, Stop, Notification, SessionEnd, PermissionRequest, SubagentStart, SubagentStop).
- **Stdio MCP server** — same binary invoked as `agent-director serve --stdio`. Stdio transport, lifetime scoped to a single agent session.
- **Operator tool** — a second binary, `agent-director-admin`, for the two
  operator-only actions (the finished-row kill, `kill-finished`, and
  `delete`). It is not an agent surface: install.sh puts it at
  `~/.config/agent-director/admin/agent-director-admin`, never on PATH, and no
  manifest text, `help`, MCP tool or client library names it. See
  [Operator tool `agent-director-admin`](#operator-tool-agent-director-admin)
  and `docs/admin-reference.md`.

## Data

- SQLite at `~/.config/agent-director/state.db` for spawn state, parent/child links, permission requests, subagent records, and labels.
- TOML config at `~/.config/agent-director/config.toml`.
- Templates as plain files in `~/.config/agent-director/templates/`.
- Private launch diagnostics, input attempts and transcript proof under
  `~/.config/agent-director/input/<store_id>/<launch_token>/`; see
  [Ordinary input delivery](#ordinary-input-delivery).

Nothing in that directory may rely on a file or directory named `.git`,
`.agents`, `.codex` or `.aws`: Codex mounts those names read-only beneath a
writable root, and a Codex agent's sandbox may name that directory as one (see
[Usage](usage.md#drive-a-spawn-from-another-agent)).

See the SRD (Ideas hive: `t1.jus.x5`) for the full design.

## Supported platforms (v1)

The supported install hosts are **`linux/amd64`** and **`darwin/arm64`**.
`install.sh`'s pre-flight host check (`uname -s` / `uname -m`) admits
only `Linux/x86_64` and `Darwin/arm64` and exits 2 on any other host,
`Linux/aarch64` included, before it downloads or writes anything. The
release builds the CLI for three targets, those two and
**`linux/arm64`** (see [Build paths](#build-paths)), but no installer
admits a `linux/arm64` or `darwin/amd64` host. The
TS Client's npm package ships no CLI binary: it drives the CLI installed
on the host (see
[System-install discovery pipeline](#system-install-discovery-pipeline-bw3q)),
and its `package.json` declares `"os": ["linux", "darwin"]` and
`"cpu": ["x64", "arm64"]`. That pair also admits `linux/arm64` and
`darwin/x64`, where the package installs but `install.sh` installs no
CLI for it to drive.

Each target gets two binaries, `agent-director` and `agent-director-admin`
(six in all). All are pure `CGO_ENABLED=0` cross-compiles (pure-Go
SQLite via `modernc.org/sqlite`). There is no FFI / shared-library
build path. The TS Client spawns the CLI binary per verb call.

Cursor's protected gateway currently runs on Linux only and refuses other
platforms before starting a runtime. The generic build/install targets above
do not establish Cursor support. Darwin cross-compilation and synthetic
Linux fixture passes are not authenticated runtime/platform acceptance.
The recorded native Linux candidate `2026.10.12-d47ca18`, wire protocol ACP1
and SDK `0.14.1` are distinct evidence. None supplies a minimum Cursor release
date or establishes earlier-version, macOS, account-model or trust equivalence.

## What a new agent reuses

The agent-specific parts of agent-director are small, named seams. A future
agent plugs into each one and never assembles an argv, classifies an event or
branches on the agent anywhere else. Each seam's own section states its rule
(its **Must use** entry); this list only points to them.

- **Launch.** The agent's program, argument check, settings, environment and
  pre-trust live in its one composition, entered through `ComposeLaunch` and
  `ComposeRelaunch`: [Per-agent launch
  composition](#per-agent-launch-composition). The agent's program is chosen by
  its `...Program` function and the agent's words in advice come from the
  agent helpers: [The agent: resolution, ownership and
  checks](#the-agent-resolution-ownership-and-checks).
- **Hooks.** The event-to-write decision comes from the classifier: [The
  agent-aware hook classifier](#the-agent-aware-hook-classifier). Its output
  gates subagent capture: Claude's table enables it, Codex's and Cursor's never do. A
  Codex launch stores `subagent_tracking` 0, an independent store guard. The
  close of a row's subagent entries when its agent is gone is [The liveness
  close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries).
- **The permission relay.** Claude/Codex relay proof and hold contracts: [The
  relay on Codex rows](#the-relay-on-codex-rows-bssz), checked by the models in
  [`spec/tla/codex/`](../spec/tla/codex/README.md) (see [Model check (`make
  tla`)](#model-check-make-tla)).
- **Cursor gateway.** Fresh/load protocol, input, transcript and runtime proof use
  [the shared gateway components](#cursor-gateway-and-current-launch-binding);
  tests use [cursorfix](#cursorfix-synthetic-acp-runtime-reusable-test-fixture).
- **Test components.** A test of a launch's argv or an agent's own files uses
  [codexfix](#codexfix-codexs-own-files-and-launch-command-reusable-test-fixture)
  and, in `pkg/api`, the [Codex-folder
  fixture](#pkgapi-codex-folder-fixture-package-internal-test-fixture). A test
  that needs a real pane process as the agent uses the stand-ins and, for the
  agent's end and the launcher case, the `/exit` stand-in and the forking
  launcher: [Docker hook
  pattern](#docker-hook-pattern-the-stand-in-claude-and-pane-hooksh) and [the
  stand-in `codex`](#testrealtmux-real-tmux-proof-of-the-client-reusable-test-fixtures).
  Hook-trust data comes from [Hook-trust golden
  data](#hook-trust-golden-data-reusable-test-data).

## Cursor gateway and current-launch binding

`internal/cursorhost` implements fresh, finished-id reuse and latest-only
resumed Cursor routes.
`internal/spawn.ComposeLaunch` and `ComposeRelaunch` use `composeCursorCommand` to select the
current whole-path `cursor_path` (default `agent`) and compose the actual AD
executable plus `cursor-host`. `installedGatewayBinary` uses build identity to
permit self-exec only for the actual `cmd/agent-director` main package. Embedded
Go applications instead require the existing canonical installed binary at
`$HOME/.config/agent-director/bin/agent-director`, resolve symlinks and verify a
regular executable before mutation. Fresh, reused and resumed launches MUST
reuse this
selection; a library caller's executable is not a gateway dispatcher.
The runtime path travels as one private `--runtime` value. Selection uses the
current loaded config on every spawn, reuse and resume; resume retains saved
cwd, arguments, environment, group and latest session. An unset path selects
`agent` on PATH. A configured path gets no executable/directory prevalidation
or PATH fallback: startup uses the existing process launch, with inherited
asynchronous failure and process-backed missing detection. Installed-gateway
validation above is a separate dependency check. Installer presence discovery
below must never change this runtime selection or rewrite launch config.
`ReadCursorArgs` is the shared, I/O-free Cursor token reader for validation,
composition, private gateway parsing and selector extraction. Its `ArgOption`
metadata preserves original indices, spellings and owned values, including
dashed required values; unknown options are valueless and still refused.
`CursorLaunchArgs` validates that reading and separates canonical model runtime
argv, one exact initial prompt and requested mode. `CursorArgs` is its existing
validation wrapper. Model identifiers remain opaque, without a catalog or
substitution. Supported modes are `agent`, `plan` and `ask`, including `--plan`;
all unsupported/malformed arguments fail before row writes. A prompt is the
sole final operand or exactly one element after an unowned `--`; an operand
before a trailing delimiter cannot bypass validation. Original saved arguments
remain unchanged except deliberate switching sanitization.
`pkg/api` retains all public control operations. Cursor reuse and agent switches
MUST use the shared fresh composition and finished-row lifecycle below. No
generic ACP framework,
public control plane or arbitrary wrapper adoption is introduced.

**Cursor environment authority.** `internal/cursorenv` is the stdlib-only,
I/O-free selection owner. Future Cursor selection consumers MUST reuse
`Validate`, `Selectors`, `WithoutSelection` and `Runtime`, rather than add
selector lists or environment policies. Fresh/reuse use resolved request/template
`ExtraEnv`; resume uses the saved protected row, while runtime executable
selection still uses current config. Both composition entry points defensively
validate Cursor selection. `ValidateExtraEnv` keeps HOME, reserved AD-prefix,
then malformed-key precedence before `ValidateCursorEnv` wraps shared policy
with `ErrReservedEnvKey`. Generic templates defer Cursor policy until effective
agent resolution. Resume retains its HOME/malformed checks and historical saved
AD-variable compatibility, then validates Cursor selection before transcript
lookup or lifecycle mutation.

Each directory selector is independently optional. Explicit `CURSOR_CONFIG_DIR`
and `CURSOR_DATA_DIR` must be nonempty, `filepath.IsAbs`, equal to
`filepath.Clean` and free of ASCII 0x00–0x1f/0x7f; accepted bytes remain unchanged.
No expansion, stat, symlink resolution or mkdir occurs. Explicit
`CURSOR_API_KEY` or `AGENT_CLI_CREDENTIAL_STORE` presence, even empty/incomplete,
is refused before transport/start. Fixed checks are API key, credential store,
config directory, data directory; diagnostics name keys without values.
Directory-only selection remains compatible with personal login and provides
no credential/account isolation. No credential transport or account framework
is introduced; the profile remains unreleased pending external acceptance.
Protected `ExtraEnv`, public omission and plaintext template visibility retain
their existing owners and protections.
Directory selection supplies no policy isolation. Handling structured rejection
does not prove AD can reliably detect native malformed-policy repair or silent
fallback in the permitted personal-login route. The unreleased profile and
second-account, key-exchange/renewal, expiry, personal-auth preservation,
cross-account worker and macOS acceptance remain independently conditional and
unmeasured by synthetic fixtures.

For each Cursor create, `tmux.NewSession` uses `invokeEnv` with
`WithoutSelection` applied to the create client's environment. `createCommands`
adds bare `-e NAME` for every absent selector, removing existing-server inheritance
for this session; explicit directories retain ordinary exact `-e NAME=value`.
This changes neither server globals nor unrelated sessions. The gateway first
uses `waitForOwnedPane` to verify the protected pending row and direct pane
identity, then validates that row's selection. `Runtime` strips all ambient
selectors and overlays only saved explicit directories into a non-nil environment
passed to `startProcess`/`exec.Cmd.Env`. HOME, store/AD identity routing, ordinary
environment, direct ownership, parent-loss protection and existing deadlines
remain intact. A parent's, client's, server's or gateway's ambient selection
cannot supply an unselected child's intent. The existing non-Linux unsupported
lifetime boundary is unchanged; this is no platform-parity claim.

**Must use:** initialization uses `initializeCapabilities` in
`internal/cursorhost/capabilities.go`, not another handshake validator or a
version-string comparison. It reads exact JSON `protocolVersion` and
`agentCapabilities` keys from raw-message maps: integer protocol 1 and a
non-null capability object are required. Known optional booleans, nested
groups, nullable support markers and reserved `_meta` containers are shape
checked. Omitted optional features remain valid; unknown extension values,
including `sessionCapabilities.fork` and `systemPrompt`, remain opaque.
Case aliases cannot supply missing exact keys or overwrite real values;
the existing framing validator still refuses duplicate exact keys.
Baseline `session/new` and text prompts require no optional capability.
Only load requires `loadSession: true`; its existing response/session checks
and latest-only no-fresh-fallback path remain authoritative. Requested mode
must still pass the existing advertised-state/selection acknowledgement gate
for fresh, loaded and rotated conversations before publication or prompt.

`protocol.response` retains the correlated `pendingMethod` before retirement.
`acpResponseFailure` and `acpOperation` are the shared failure boundary:
future response handling MUST reuse them. Only host-owned operation names
(`initialize`, `session/new`, `session/load`, `session/set_mode`,
`session/prompt`, otherwise `request`) and static cause text are rendered.
Exact `code` and `message` keys require non-null int32 and string values;
case aliases remain opaque. Codes -32601, -32700/-32600/-32602, -32800,
-32000 and -32002 establish unsupported, format/parameter rejection,
cancellation, authentication-required and missing-resource causes respectively.
-32603 is internal-error/unknown; other codes remain rejection/unknown.
Malformed errors remain malformed, with no authentication/configuration
inference from message, data, stderr or exit. Runtime-supplied secrets,
paths, environment and control text never enter these diagnostics.
Exact structured -32601 also carries the private `errACPOperationUnsupported`
marker. Future consumers MUST reuse `errors.Is` on this wrapped cause rather
than classify diagnostic text. Only while `modeResponse` is pending may this
authority attach the existing complete-mode-removal advice; advertised
unavailable modes retain their independent correction. Authentication, unknown,
internal, malformed, format, cancellation and missing-resource failures do not
offer that remedy. No public typed-error API or automatic retry is introduced.
`startProcess` separately bounds OS-start reasons to missing executable/cwd,
permission denial or unknown. No executable/version/login probe is added.
Malformed framing, transport loss and runtime death retain distinct evidence;
existing `ad.cursor.failed`, conditional cleanup, process-backed missing and
request-proof rules below remain the owners. A reason alone grants no
delivery, execution, termination or replacement-launch authority.

Launch remains asynchronous: return of `pending` is not successful initialize,
new/load, mode selection or prompt execution. The TS subprocess client's
default 30,000 ms call budget is separate from the existing 45-second ACP
initialize/new/load operation bound. Held generation/load/dialogs do not turn
launch into a readiness wait. Configured longer pause waits require adequate
client allowance; neither deadline nor cancellation is reset or extended.

Finished-id reuse MUST follow the existing `spawnReuse` → `reuseExamine` →
`ComposeLaunch` → `ResetForReuse` → `CreateAndLabel` → `finishedLaunch` path.
It creates a fresh conversation; it never calls `ComposeRelaunch` or loads a
saved session. Only an explicitly named, successfully examined finished row
whose exact agent differs from the resolved target enables `DropResumeArgs`.
Cursor validation then uses the existing copied `ExtractResumeArgs` output
and validates survivors with `CursorArgs` before publishing arguments and
ordered original dropped tokens. Plain/same-agent paths do not drop selectors;
the reset rechecks the old agent and full examined snapshot atomically.

`ResetForReuse` MUST remain the atomic transaction for archive, reset, request
deletion and subagent closure for all agents. Same-agent reuse retains life; every switch
increments life, including switchback, permanently surrendering prior-life AD
resume access. History reads filter to current life and exclude the current
session. Cursor's public subagent projection remains untracked/empty even when
raw closed entries remain stored. Child AD spawns are independent rows and
retain their parent association; the append-only trail spans all lives.

`finishedLaunch` MUST remain the shared create/label outcome owner. Known
`CreateUnlabelledEnded` and `CreateUnlabelledRunning` outcomes attempt the same
conditional full `RawLife` restore as other determinate failures, retaining
survivor/manual-recovery warnings. Restore requires pending at the reset
version; pane identity publication advances that version and defeats a stale
restore. Registration alone is not claimed to advance row version. Restore
preserves the archive, deleted requests and closed entries rather than
resurrecting cleanup state. Timeouts, lost replies and indeterminate nonzero
create replies retain existing non-restoration behavior.

Reuse receives the concrete opened base store's `Path()` beside `StoreID()`
through private `reuseDeps`, independently of injected reuse read/write
wrappers. For Cursor only, it sets the existing
`AGENT_DIRECTOR_CURSOR_STORE_PATH` in the create environment. This value is
launch-only, never saved in `ExtraEnv` or exposed as a new public option;
config/default-path inference cannot replace actual-store provenance.

Retained runtime descriptors are not deleted to enable reuse or restore. A
new registration can replace an earlier token/life descriptor only after
independent verification of the pending row, launch, process and pane; a
conflicting same-launch registration cannot replace current ownership. The
complete descriptor read/write guard below also requires exact examined
session/termination fields or true absence.
Registration, restore or any descriptor change defeats stale reconciliation.
Prompt, permission, hook and rotation paths retain launch/life/conversation/
connection/process/pane ownership and epoch checks. An old conversation end
cannot retire a continuing rotated conversation; independently proven owned
process death remains liveness evidence. Neither death nor cleanup creates
request receipt, delivery or execution proof. No schema or new lifecycle
framework is required.

**Canonical guidance and scoped MCP.** Fresh, latest-loaded and rotated
conversations MUST reuse `internal/cursormcp.New` for their typed ACP stdio
`mcpServers` registration when `defaults.inject_help_hook` is enabled. Off keeps
the explicit empty list and skips guidance work. The registration invokes the
gateway's actual executable with structured `--home`, `--store-path`,
`--create-if-missing=false`, `serve --stdio` arguments. It supplies the protected
parent id, `AGENT_DIRECTOR_AGENT=cursor`, reconstructed `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE`, empty
`TMUX_TMPDIR` and private scope. Actual `Store.Path()`/`StoreID()`, HOME and the
row's socket/server/pane supply provenance; ambient store hints and dashboard
configuration do not. A comma-bearing socket is refused rather than ambiguously
encoded in `TMUX`. This routing prerequisite grants no additional tool permission
or lifecycle authority; real caller/child/restart acceptance is separate.

Public CLI and ordinary stdio MCP clients MUST reuse `clisetup.APIOptions`
for explicit global overrides. `--home` applies before config/default-path
resolution; arbitrary override stores require `--store-path`.
`AGENT_DIRECTOR_CURSOR_STORE_PATH` carries the actual opened store to the
gateway and direct reporting hooks, not generic public CLI configuration.
Fresh/reuse composition and resume's pending transition MUST reuse
`spawn.ParentIDFromEnv` for association. That text and public `get`/`list --parent`
are not caller authentication or protected launch authority. Fresh launches
select the intended caller socket; resume MUST reuse `ResolveRowLaunchSocket`
and finished-id reuse its existing recorded-socket selection before ambient
fallback. Wrappers around opened stores must forward `Path()` so resume keeps
the actual override store.

`cursorMCPScope` in the CLI MUST remain the pure preflight before `setupClient`
opens a store for a privately scoped `serve`. It requires exact explicit routing
and no creation, so malformed scope cannot open or create an ambient fallback
store. `cursorMCPOptions` reuses that parser, then `Scope.Binding`,
`VerifyRuntime` and `VerifyPane` at server construction and acknowledgement.
Each verification rereads the protected binding and verifies the runtime before
pane evidence and again afterward; the gateway confirmation checks its captured
binding against fresh protected records on both sides of the pane check too.
Protected store, parent, token/life, connection, gateway/runtime PID/start and
unterminated current records must agree. `Parse` requires an explicitly present
nonnegative int64 life: zero is the valid first life, while missing/null,
negative, fractional, string and overflow values cannot select it. Future
consumers MUST reuse these owners rather than add scope parsing or ownership
shortcuts. Scope deliberately does not freeze the conversation id; current
protected binding still decides authority.

Private guidance admission, acknowledgement and gateway confirmation MUST reuse
`cursorhost.VerifyGuidanceOwnership` in `guidance_ownership.go`, rather than add
another retry or supervision framework. `VerifyPane` distinguishes unavailable
evidence (`paneUncertain`) from proven ownership or pane mismatch. Only an actual
typed lookup or pane-listing timeout or pipe cut permits re-verification, within
the original absolute setup deadline or the expired-replacement allowance below.
`tmux.CallError.QueryInterrupted` uses the
call kind, timeout failure and private runner-recorded cut provenance; error text,
`FirstLine`, empty output, malformed output or generic uncertainty cannot grant
retry eligibility. Partial replies never grant ownership or authority. Proven
mismatch and other noneligible failures refuse immediately. Configured query and
pipe-close bounds are unchanged. This policy is private to guidance; public pane
operations, tool dispatch, permission relay and ACP writes gain no retries.

Each setup attempt owns a fresh random nonce and Unix observation socket in a
new private 0700 directory, with a 0600 socket. `Observation.Wait` accepts only
that nonce before the existing absolute operation deadline. The real MCP server
acknowledges only after writing its correlated successful `initialize` response,
receiving standard `notifications/initialized` and rechecking protected ownership.
This socket carries no guidance payload. Closing/replacing an observation also
closes a stalled accepted receipt connection. An older server's receipt cannot
qualify another attempt; a restart after the receipt deadline cannot retroactively
admit input.

Ordinary external caller recreation and replacement of the actual configured
runtime-descendant MCP process are separate boundaries. Under the still-current
binding, the latter reuses the exact registration and standard initialization,
including after the original observer deadline. It preserves gateway/runtime
PID and start, token/life, connection/pipes, current conversation, protected
transcript and parent history; subsequent prompt records may append normally.
It neither certifies a new setup attempt nor relaxes protected ownership or
prompt/decision guards. `Scope.Acknowledge` is a no-op after its original
`Until`; a retired token/life/connection or terminated runtime still refuses
the registration. `cursorMCPOptions` captures setup versus expired-replacement mode
once at adapter entry. A setup beginning before `Scope.Until` retains that original
absolute deadline and cannot switch modes after expiry. An already-expired
replacement additionally requires a nonempty current protected runtime session
matching the current row session, before and after positive pane evidence. Pending
state alone does not refuse a confirmed load; session identity remains dynamic.
Each existing ownership-verification call receives one absolute read-only allowance
of `2 * (EffectiveQueryTimeout() + EffectivePipeCloseWait())`, 3.2 seconds at
defaults, bounded by the caller context. Typed timeout/cut retries consume that
call's allowance without resetting it. Constructor and `Initialized` checks remain
independent, preserving arbitrary notification delay between them. This allowance
does not renew `Scope.Until`, the observation or setup/publication authority.
Re-verification does not replay `initialize`, session new/load, tools or permission actions, nor
replace the observer nonce. Independently AD-spawned children own their rows and runtime
cleanup; parent association never adopts them as runtime descendants.

`session.go` MUST retain `configureGuidance`/`confirmGuidance` through the existing
`await` loop, with control, signal, runtime-loss, epoch and deadline supervision.
Fresh creation shares `sessionUntil`, load shares `loadUntil` (45 seconds), and
rotation shares the first control's `cancelAt + cancelWait` (three seconds).
Guidance never renews those bounds. `guidance_configured` and
`guidance_initialized` record the candidate id and operation; the latter records
`evidence=mcp_client_initialized` and `model_consumption=unverified`. Configuration,
transport initialization, confirmed candidate identity, committed publication and
prompt admission remain separate facts. Existing mode confirmation,
`SetCursorRuntimeSession`, `BindLoadedCursorSession`, atomic rotation publication,
protected recording and prompt/hold/FIFO guards remain mandatory. Initialization
alone neither commits identity nor releases provisionally held input.

The shared verifier checks cancellation and the applicable absolute deadline after evidence
returns, rejecting late positive results. Gateway controls, runtime loss, current
input epoch and publication checks remain authoritative; acknowledgement receipt
writes are context-gated. Workers abandoned by their caller only read evidence
and cannot acknowledge or publish. Only an unfinished or canceled/deadline
verification permits asynchronous private-store cleanup; a completed hard refusal
keeps normal synchronous cleanup and error joining. After independent proof that
the exact runtime binding is dead, abandoned gateway verification serializes its
remaining store reads, fresh token/life/connection-guarded failed-launch retirement
and store close under the same private mutex. A worker acquiring that mutex after
cancellation cannot touch the closed store. Deferred retirement is best effort
and cannot change the returned failure or delay it on SQL; scoped `serve` also
closes its private store asynchronously when verification was abandoned.

This route has no qualified automatic ACP compaction delivery or forced
reinsertion inside an already compacted conversation. Both pinned versions'
shared ACP resource wrappers can invoke the native `preCompact` executor;
that reachability alone does not qualify automatic delivery. That is the
compaction-only limitation;
fresh/load/every confirmed replacement still require current initialization.
Source and synthetic transport evidence do not establish native full-guidance
model consumption, which remains pending separately for each lifecycle path.

Latest-only resume MUST reuse the existing public state/session/environment
checks and guarded move/create/label/conditional-restore flow described in
[Resume](#resume). `ComposeRelaunch` filters a copied saved argument list through
`ExtractResumeArgs`, preserves saved cwd/environment/labels/group configuration
mechanically and selects today's `cursor_path`. This does not establish group
or account isolation. The actual opened store's `Path()` is forwarded through
the same private `AGENT_DIRECTOR_CURSOR_STORE_PATH` route as fresh launch before
pre-trust or move; saved `ExtraEnv` is unchanged. Injected `ResumeStore` wrappers
around an override store MUST forward `Path()`; a config-path fallback cannot
discover an arbitrary wrapper's database. No public gateway/store option is added.

The private `LoadSession` option carries only the saved latest identity and is
validated against the owned pending row before runtime start. It is not a public
resume parameter. Public preflight uses `internal/cursortranscript.VerifyAppend`
without creating, writing or parsing native Cursor storage. After ACP1 initialize
advertises `loadSession`, the sole controller issues `session/load` with that id,
cwd and the scoped `mcpServers` above (empty with help off). A standard object
result `{}` is valid; an optional
returned `sessionId` must match exactly. Missing native session, unsupported load,
malformed/error response, timeout or transport failure never falls back to an
older session or `session/new`.

Every method frame received during load before its authoritative response is
quarantined before transcript recording, state, admission, requests or proof.
Historical notifications are discarded; historical authorization/questions
receive finite fail-closed protocol handling without durable request or choice
revival. Unsupported cancellation-required replay fails the load. Both question
settings retain denial and independent genuine dialog holds.

Loaded publication MUST use `Store.BindLoadedCursorSession` and the existing
controller `await`. Capture input epoch before input starts and absolute
`loadUntil` before dispatch. One cancelable context bounds acquisition,
BEGIN/UPDATE/COMMIT and cleanup through `inWriteTxContext`; no phase renews time.
The conditional write requires the examined pending row/session/protected path,
snapshot, token/life/server/pane and full new unbound, unterminated connection,
with post-lock/post-UPDATE epoch and kernel runtime checks. A provisional UPDATE
is not publication. Only confirmed commit grants loaded authority; interruption
or unconfirmed commit grants no loaded-success record or prompt admission.
Confirmed commit followed by retirement retains truthful durable identity while
refusing input, without automatic retry or a rollback claim.

Load emits `session_loaded`, not synthetic SessionStart or waiting. Persistent
session identity grants no inherited connection-local authority. Only
`reporter.promptEligible` with `Store.CheckLoadedCursorPrompt` admits the first
real prompt while pending, requiring the exact saved session/path, full current
binding, independent runtime/pane verification and every durable hold. General
pending permission authority stays refused. Public callers explicitly use the
existing `allow_pending` after pane inspection; it bypasses no gateway guard.
The real prompt reports UserPromptSubmit through the unchanged direct-parent
hook. Saved initial text remains once per launch after successful load and hold
checks; transient queued, held and editable draft input is never reconstructed.

Explicit mode is private launch configuration, carried by `RequestedMode` and
the internal gateway's `--requested-mode`, never a public spawn/template field
or MCP control. `runtime-args` contains model arguments only; mode and prompt
cannot enter runtime argv through private parsing. `mode.go` validates the
target session's advertised current/available mode state and the requested ID.
The sole controller adds `new_mode`, `load_mode` or `rotate_new_mode` after the
corresponding response, before the original publication/admission branch.
It sends one correlated `session/set_mode`; a valid object `{}` suffices.
Optional echoed session/mode IDs must agree, and contradictory main mode
updates fail. Unsolicited, retired or child metadata cannot replace the response.
Configuration re-enters the original validated response branch once; rotation
must not issue another `session/new` while configuration is pending.

Before confirmed configuration and publication, target traffic supplies no
prompt, permission or lifecycle authority; authorization attempts are denied
through the existing owner. Each mode write checks captured input epoch and
the original absolute deadline both before and after independent runtime
verification. Acknowledgement/record completion rechecks them, then the usual
binding, life, session, process and pane guards still apply. Fresh configuration
uses the original creation bound, load shares `loadUntil`, and rotation shares
the first control's `cancelAt + cancelWait` (three seconds). No phase renews time.
Unavailable state, rejected/malformed acknowledgement, interruption or authority
loss remains a truthful asynchronous failure, with no default-mode retry.
Successful startup configuration is not a permanent lock: legitimate later
mode changes, including plan approval, remain allowed. Initial text is delivered
once per launch after configuration and durable holds; same-launch rotation
never replays it.

The gateway is the recorded pane/main process, starts one selected runtime
with `acp`, and owns both protocol pipes. The runtime never reads terminal
input. `protocol.go` bounds frames, correlates one outstanding initialize,
session/new, session/load, session/set_mode or session/prompt request, validates
protocol 1 and completions,
and rejects stale/mismatched responses. Its bounded FIFO and single outbound
writer serialize frames without blocking the controller. Enqueueing is not
delivery: each frame has a fixed write deadline from enqueue, independent of
startup, prompt and cancellation deadlines. Expired frames are never written;
short writes, transport errors and write timeouts make delivery uncertain and
fatal, with no retry or replay. The controller continues observing child
death, input and signals while writes stall. Cancellation retains the first
request's fixed deadline; repeated interrupts or denials cannot extend it.
`session.go` owns one active prompt and a transient FIFO bound to the confirmed
launch/conversation. `inputMailbox` reserves at most 32 waiting submissions and
8 MiB of waiting text, separately from the active prompt; individual input is
bounded to 1 MiB. Reservations persist across transfer to the controller queue
and release at dispatch or cancellation. Future input paths MUST reuse
`promptAdmission` and `inputMailbox`: initial startup retains one idle
reservation, Enter can verify committed waiting through `reporter.verifyReport`
while the hook finishes, and the saved initial prompt retains priority. Once
startup is confirmed, eligible complete follow-ups queue in observed terminal
order. `terminal_linux.go` preserves editable Unicode and multiline text;
pending startup, stale or excess input is explicitly refused. Literal text and
Enter remain separate public send-keys operations, without concurrent-caller
atomicity. `/clear` and `/new` share the priority control lane and start a
same-life conversation rotation. Old accepted queue entries are cancelled
individually and never migrate. Ordinary input consumed during rotation captures
its epoch, conversation and provisional status together under the mailbox lock;
that observation survives a delayed insertion across publication. Separate held
reservations have the same 32-entry/8 MiB aggregate and 1 MiB individual bounds.
They are not admission to either conversation. After publication, held input
remains provisional until `CheckCursorPrompt` accepts every durable guard.
`inputMailbox.promote` transfers reservation ownership and `insertSubmission`
merges by original observation order ahead of newer accepted work. Future
rotation/admission paths MUST reuse these components and the captured status.

Dispatch requires the previous turn to finish and every retained durable dialog
hold to resolve. Future dispatch paths MUST reuse `reporter.promptEligible`
and `Store.CheckCursorPrompt`, which bound authority acquisition and verify
runtime/pane/current binding and all unproven durable requests. An empty local
request map, acknowledgement or local cancellation supplies no dialog proof.
Late exact tool execution can discharge only its matching hold after completion.
The guarded protocol request allocates its ACP identity before synchronizing
`submission_started`; no prompt bytes may pass before that record succeeds.
Both writer guards retire an obsolete prompt epoch before bytes. Known zero-byte
retirement preserves a healthy transport for later explicit input; partial or
uncertain output remains fatal and is never replayed.

Controls use an independent mailbox lane and advance the cancellation epoch at
consumption, including across a slow admission-to-insertion handoff. They retire
affected prompt and decision authority and give each retained accepted submission
an explicit disposition while persistence remains available. The first control's
three-second deadline supervises cancellation, slow protected records, reporting
and finalization; repeated controls cannot extend it. Recovery clears that bound
and enables later explicit input only while owning its captured epoch with no
pending control. Local exit and eligible pause cancel waiting work and require
confirmed owned termination before an intentional end report; working and dialog
pause guards remain. No accepted FIFO entry is restored or replayed after failure.

For rotation, an outstanding prompt requires its correlated terminal response
or positive retirement before any bytes at the existing prompt writer gate.
An idle rotation does not wait for a response to the cancel notification.
The original three-second first-control deadline covers cancellation, fresh
creation, publication and protected records. Repeated aliases coalesce with
an explicit ignored/count disposition, without new authority or extra time.
The new-session writer checks epoch and expiry before bytes. Fresh identity
confirmation must correlate to the one pending request and be nonempty, bounded,
unchanged by whitespace trimming, free of NUL/CR/LF and never previously confirmed
on this connection. Confirmed identities and their request-origin boundaries
share the 4096 connection cap. Timeout, ambiguous identity, lost authority or
publication failure refuses held work to both conversations and stops admission.
Interrupt during rotation stops the owned runtime; it cannot resume the outgoing
conversation. Exit and eligible public pause preempt supervised phases but still
require real owned death and verified durable SessionEnd for intentional success.

Cursor `session/update` decoding is variant-scoped: retain tool and unknown
`content` as `json.RawMessage`; decode text content only for
`agent_message_chunk` and `agent_thought_chunk`. Render text only for main-agent
attribution. Raw retention supplies no lifecycle, authorization or execution
proof; existing top-level session, retired-session and exact-request execution
gates remain mandatory. Schema failures are diagnosed separately from session
mismatches. Future update variants MUST preserve this separation.

`paneDisplay` separates bounded rendering from input/control consumption; future
rendering paths MUST reuse it. Nonblocking producers retain the existing frame
and byte bounds; a capacity-one loss wakeup lets the single rendering consumer
report pending loss after physical output resumes, even without another
producer. Only that consumer writes output, outside the display mutex,
including stop-drain checks. A permanently blocked writer still cannot render
the notice, and the existing bounded stop is unchanged. The protected
transcript remains authoritative; display content or loss never classifies AD
state or authority.

`process_linux.go` installs ptrace EXITKILL and parent-death protection at the
initial exec stop before ACP input. Fork/clone/exec descendants stay guarded
across launcher chains. Runtime/pipes are independently identified; a second
ACP owner is refused. Only an explicitly identified same-runtime executable
or script worker-server possessing neither ACP pipe may detach. Unknown
process evidence grants no ownership. Stop reconciles inherited tracees
through kernel `TracerPid` matching the locked supervisor OS-thread id,
including an announcement overtaken by SIGKILL, then signals/drains those
exact tracees. `PTRACE_O_TRACEEXIT` also reconciles these exact-owned tasks at
the early exit stop: normal descendant group exit can overtake a clone
announcement and otherwise prevent the leader's final wait status. The early
event is not death proof; actual `Wait4` exit/signaled status remains required.
The configured MCP child and its ordinary descendants retain this same owned
cleanup path and receive no worker detach exception. No independent worker or
AD child is adopted. Success requires confirmed leader exit and owned tracees gone.
The transport writes through a separately closeable, pollable duplicate of
the owned input pipe. Closing it releases stalled I/O while the registered
ownership descriptor remains open through verified intentional end reporting.
Transport closure supplies no process-death evidence.
No process-group cleanup or arbitrary-child wait is allowed. Independent or
shared surviving work retains the existing kill limits. EOF is transport
failure, never child-death evidence; child loss stops the gateway rather than
leaving a renderer classified live. Non-Linux lifetime/terminal operations
fail closed.

On a fatal `Run` return after registration, terminate and join the exact owned
runtime, then independently call `VerifyRuntime` for terminated evidence while
the gateway's registered ownership descriptors remain open. Only that proof
permits failure cleanup to publish `missing`; preserve both the original failure
and any cleanup error. Do not manufacture intentional SessionEnd,
`prompt_input_exit` or turn success for this path. Keep SIGINT/SIGHUP/SIGTERM
capture installed through terminal restoration (including ISIG), runtime/binding/
store cleanup and final failure-event emission. `signal.Stop` must run after
those defers; `signal.Notify` keeps its existing activation point. Repeated
signals do not extend cancellation deadlines or supply death evidence.

Public `Client.Get` and `Client.Status` collect fresh launch-scoped gateway
loss evidence through `reconcileCursorGateway`. `Client.List` validates filters
before store access, selects candidates within `Labels`/`Parent`/`Cwd`/
`TmuxSessionName` with `State` and `Limit` removed, and examines each live Cursor
candidate. CLI, MCP, Go and Bun public verbs reach these methods. The helper
judges the recorded gateway PID/start-time with `tmux.JudgeProcess`; a different
start time proves the old identity gone. Alive or unknown evidence leaves the
row unchanged. Positive gateway loss permits a read-scoped `missing` projection
even when the runtime is alive or unknown; it cannot authorize intentional
`ended`. Only after exact gateway loss and `ReadCursorRuntime` returning
`sql.ErrNoRows` may the helper carry examined absence, retaining instance,
token/life, gateway PID/start and session with every runtime field empty.
An existing stale binding is not absence. Evidence is never cached across calls
or reused for a replacement launch. Already terminal and non-Cursor rows incur
no process probe or mutation. Standalone package-level `api.Get`/`api.Status`/
`api.List` remain database projections without these Client checks.

**Must use:** `Store.WithCursorMissingReads` (`internal/store/cursor_missing_read.go`)
is the read adapter for this evidence. Its `cursorMissingGuard` is also the
terminal write's guard: full row snapshot, agent, token/life, gateway PID/start,
session/path and complete runtime PID/start, connection, pipes/fds, session and
terminated binding. A retained obsolete descriptor is exact examined present
evidence, even when it names an earlier launch; positive current gateway death
does not make that descriptor current authority or absence. New registration,
restore or any examined binding change defeats the same read/write guard.
Only true examined absence uses `NOT EXISTS` for **any** runtime binding for examined
absence. Raw and reported state become `missing` only
while that guard matches in the SELECT. List applies the guarded state inside
SQL before settled/raw `State` filtering and `LIMIT`; missing bypasses settle
delay. The existing JSON1 support carries one bound proof array per expression,
with at most two predicate shapes generated from the shared guard. Bind count
and expression depth do not grow with proof count; there is no new durable
table or proof-count ceiling. Correlated proof traversal still grows with data;
this is no general performance claim. A changed same-launch snapshot or binding
cannot be returned as working; unsafe live results fail validation. A replacement
launch retains its own state.

The Client assembles the complete public result, including permission lists,
BEFORE attempting terminal persistence. No required result read follows a
write timeout that may leave native work holding the store's sole connection.
The projection changes only raw/reported state. `ended_at`, liveness and other
timestamps remain the durable facts read, so this first missing result may lack
`ended_at` even if the subsequent write succeeds. `launch_started_at` is omitted
because the projected raw state is terminal. Terminal permission lists are
empty by the existing read rule; this is no per-request proof of dialog absence,
delivery, receipt, decision or runtime death. Projection invents no durable
request facts or trail events.

The read's separate persistence attempt MUST reuse
`Store.MarkCursorMissingIfSameLaunch`; fatal cleanup MUST use
`Store.MarkFailedCursorRuntimeMissing`. Both use `terminalMarkWithoutWait`, through
`inWriteTxContext(ctx, 0)` and the common `terminalMarkOnConn` payload. The write
repeats the shared guard and atomically closes requests and running subagents,
advances row version and applies terminal state. An inserted binding, including
a stale one after examined absence, defeats the close. Changed guards cannot
close a newer launch; an unresolved live conflict on the same dead launch fails.
Fatal cleanup requires exact owned termination and independent
`VerifyRuntime(binding, true)`. Its guard permits only the matching binding's monotonic
termination-bit advancement, retaining every other complete identity/snapshot
predicate and requiring the row's token/life/gateway to match the proven-dead
runtime. Public missing reconciliation keeps its strict termination-bit check.
No runtime identity, retirement or intentional SessionEnd is fabricated, and
Cursor per-request proof rules remain unchanged. Context-aware request-deny and
orphan-tick emitters preserve event values, order and pending/failed/rejected
accounting within the same operation context.

After assembly, attempt each examined launch's terminal write once with the
unchanged zero-lock-wait, fixed one-second `operationContext(0)` allowance,
capped by the caller context through SQL, cleanup and fail-open post-commit
audit. Only this write's `ErrStoreBusy` or `context.DeadlineExceeded` may be
deferred while the caller context remains valid. Read failures, non-deadline
write failures and caller cancellation/exhaustion propagate with the existing
empty failure shapes (`Get`/`Status` zero results; `List.Spawns` non-nil empty).
`persistCursorMissing` checks caller context again after the whole persistence
loop, including successful cleanup/audit. A confirmed store commit stays
confirmed even if the public call fails on its caller budget. A timed-out COMMIT
remains unconfirmed; a successful missing read certifies neither commit nor
rollback. No retry, new audit budget, deadline extension or uncertain replay is
allowed. Fatal cleanup retains its error propagation; it does not adopt the
public read's deferral rule. The allowance is not a whole-read deadline:
preceding reads/process probes and multiple candidates have separate costs.
Legacy `FindMissing`/`MarkEnded` retain their background transaction contracts.
Repeated terminal reads are idempotent; explicit `find-missing` and other agents
retain their contracts. Public held-writer/trail coverage and fixture-backed
native store COMMIT coverage exercise separate boundaries; they do not establish
an end-to-end public Client native-COMMIT test.

The v9→v10 hop adds only `cursor_runtimes`, the current launch/life gateway and
runtime pid/start-time, connection, private pipe/fd, session and retirement
binding. Registration, session assignment, retirement and report writes are
conditional on the existing store/row/token/life/server/pane identity. The
v9-to-v10 hop is guarded and transactional; fresh and migrated stores share
the schema. Existing Claude/Codex and legacy NULL data retain their identity
and visibility. The agent-rename migration remains the immutable v8-to-v9
hop. Runtime binding never becomes authority based solely on a stored claim.

Schema v11 separately adds durable request proof eligibility; see
[v11 proof eligibility](#v11-columns-durable-main-turn-proof-eligibility).
No Cursor permission or plan admission is implemented by this metadata change.

`reporter.report` directly execs the AD hook with the gateway as its immediate
parent. The unchanged gate must accept that parent; Cursor additionally checks
current launch, life, registered runtime/connection/session and termination.
The CLI's `hookCursorVerifier` independently composes `VerifyRuntime`,
`VerifyTranscriptPath` and `VerifyPane`. An absent/error verifier rejects the
report. `internal/hook.HandleConfig.VerifyCursor` injects this evidence seam
without adding probe/tmux/cursorhost dependencies to `internal/hook`.
Conditional store writes repeat the binding predicates after verification.
SessionEnd uses a reporter copy so retirement cannot race cleanup's binding.
The final report and direct child hook share the original first-control
absolute deadline; an expired worker cannot start a fresh reporting window
or launch a late helper. Genuine expiry remains an error; fatal missing cleanup
never supplies per-request death proof or a delivery receipt.
Startup `SetCursorRuntimeSession` is not rotation authority. Same-launch rotation
MUST use `Store.RotateCursorSession` in `internal/store/cursor_rotation.go`, via
the direct-parent SessionStart report carrying `cursor_previous_session` and the
absolute `cursor_rotation_deadline`. `HandleConfig.VerifyCursorRotation` and the
CLI verifier independently recheck runtime, protected transcript and pane from
the transaction-read row. The bounded immediate transaction repeats the full
examined snapshot, launch/life/server/socket/pane, outgoing session and runtime
connection/process/pipe/fd predicates, including post-wait expiry. It publishes
the row's fresh session/path, required outgoing current-life history and runtime
binding atomically. Required archive or COMMIT failure rolls back publication;
generic Claude/Codex fail-open archival is unchanged. Existing state/settle
writers preserve independent request holds as `check_permission`.

Future publication observers MUST reuse `ObserveCursorRotation` (committed-only)
and `ReconcileCursorRotation` (committed fresh, unchanged outgoing, or unknown).
They read actual atomic binding/row/history snapshots under the original deadline;
a false committed result alone does not prove the outgoing identity unchanged.
The reporter observes COMMIT while the hook is alive, independently of hook
completion. Consumed intentional exit cancels that hook and joins only within
the remaining bound. Confirmed hook exit or failed Start permits a final bounded
reconciliation; parent cancellation does not cancel this authoritative read
early. Only positive committed or unchanged proof permits normal intentional
finalization. Unknown/error/exhaustion cannot establish rollback or successful
ended. An observed committed fresh identity remains authoritative after a later
report error, transcript failure or timeout. SQL knowledge never proves runtime
death or durable SessionEnd.
Report confirmation must reuse `reporter.verifyReport` for both the Enter
waiting check and post-hook verification. Post-hook verification also accepts
`check_permission` in place of nominal
working/waiting only when a genuine request still awaits an answer and is
unproven. It verifies its own token/life/session/transcript path and a strictly
newer row version, rereads the exact runtime binding (connection, pipes,
session and termination included), and independently rechecks runtime and pane
evidence. An unrelated version increment, empty hold, stale session or changed
binding cannot confirm a report. Intentional SessionEnd still requires `ended`.
The actual opened store path is forwarded for routing, including client
store overrides; that path supplies no authority. Optional Cursor tool hooks
from a child, unrelated controllers, nested agents and stale launches cannot
report lifecycle. Unknown/child update provenance is retained without
inventing main-agent lifecycle or subagent records. Cursor subagent listing
always returns untracked and empty; existing status response shapes remain.

`transcript_linux.go` creates random private JSONL artifacts beneath the AD
config directory and syncs each sequence-numbered record. Shared
`internal/cursortranscript` owns no-follow component traversal, private directory,
regular user-owned single-link file and access checks. Public preflight and
gateway reopen MUST reuse it; nonblocking opens refuse special files without
hanging and unsupported platforms fail closed. Resume opens the same existing
file for append without creation, reads only a bounded valid final record and
continues its sequence after checking complete newline, instance/life and
non-overflow. It preserves the original prefix and never reconstructs ACP
history; malformed continuity fails rather than replacing the file. Records bind launch,
life, connection and confirmed conversation to submission acceptance, dispatch
start, updates, cancellation, refusal and outcomes. Submission identities are
independent of ACP request IDs; start/update/outcome records correlate both.
Accepted initial input remains tracked through pre-dispatch failures. A start
record has unconfirmed delivery; termination and unconfirmed completion are
separate dispositions. Replacement/symlink/insecure-path and persistence failures
halt admission and cannot yield a false successful end or complete saved history.
Future lifecycle records MUST reuse this protected synchronized recorder.
Reports expose the actual recorded path through `jsonl_path`;
`transcript_status` remains a reference summary, not a new reader-time file
verification. Native Cursor storage remains runtime-owned and separate; neither
a Claude JSONL substitute nor successful unrecorded outcome is claimed.
One protected file continued across launches can be referenced by current and multiple prior
current-life sessions. Per-record attribution remains separate: accepted input
keeps its consumption-time conversation, provisional `input_held` and
`held_input_refused` have none, and known retired records keep their actual
outgoing conversation. Requested, confirmed and published rotation are distinct
records. Cleanup visibly disposes every known held or unstarted queue owner
even after recorder failure; protected final dispositions require recorder health
and remaining original budget. No deadline extension manufactures a final record,
complete history, rollback or successful intentional end.

### Cursor authorization dataflow and authority

`authorization.go` owns the version-grounded adapters and shared pre-admission
question policy for Cursor `2026.10.12-d47ca18` / ACP1 envelopes.
`parseAuthorization` validates the complete permission option list and captured
`cursor/create_plan` fields, rejects duplicate JSON keys at every depth and retains the original params bytes as `ToolInput`.
`ToolName` is the supplied title/plan name and `ToolUseID` the actual
`toolCallId`. Optional absent/null plan fields remain untouched; plans acquire
no fabricated session or native option list. Captured accepted/rejected plan
outcomes are distinct from cancellation. API allow selects only `allow_once`,
API deny `reject_once`; native persistent selection requires the exact
explicitly offered option. Generic `other` is not non-question evidence: only
the captured MCP title/option shape is admitted. Unsupported/ambiguous shapes
fail closed visibly within a bound; no schema is invented for unobserved
approvals. String and numeric request IDs have separate namespaces; equivalent
numeric spellings normalize. They are independent of outbound RPC IDs, cannot
replace active/answered IDs, and are bounded to 4096 per connection and 32
active requests. Tool IDs also cannot be reused on the connection.

`requests.go` owns one `requestController` event-loop arbiter for API decisions,
native keys, timeout, cancellation and execution proof. Admission calls
`InsertCursorRequest` to atomically raise `check_permission` and insert the
request with unknown origin (`MainTurnEndEligible=false`, NULL child identity).
`internal/store/cursor_permission.go` supplies authenticated gateway entry
points; no gateway PID is disguised as per-request hook evidence and no fake
`HookGate` is constructed. Each transaction acquires `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`,
rereads Spawn and the complete CursorRuntime binding, and checks launch token,
life, server/pane identity and pid/start, current confirmed session,
runtime/connection/pipes/fds, nonretirement and nonterminal row state.
`CursorCheck` independently runs `VerifyRuntime` and `VerifyPane` after the lock; time is checked after potentially
slow evidence. The immediate-parent hook gate remains unchanged.
Gateway callbacks capture the exact launch binding before dispatch through
`checkFor`; a later rotation cannot change an outstanding operation's evidence.
Bounded callbacks may outlive the caller while native work is quarantined.
Their inputs must stay immutable and their captured outputs must only be read
after a successful helper return. `CheckCursorPrompt` returns `false, err`
before reading captured eligibility on failure; relay/Cursor ack and timeout
helpers likewise return zero outputs on error. `RecordHookGone` clones its
request-id slice before dispatch. None of these ownership rules replaces the
authenticated authority checks or derives permission from pane text.

Admission fixes a finite millisecond `SettledAt`: configured relay window plus
four seconds. The approval deadline is settlement minus that reserve. Relay-off
settlement is immediately past, so existing readers truthfully show
`fallen_back` and pane availability without enabling `decide`. Native lifetime
is separately bounded to 30 minutes from admission (relay off), or settlement
plus 30 minutes (relay on). Prompt timing pauses while actual requests own
these bounds. Caller restart never rearms settlement or replays a response.

`AckCursorDecision` reuses first-writer decision/ack/timeout predicates and
checks immutable settlement after lock/evidence delays. Every relay answer,
allow, deny and timeout denial, commits its own `delivered_at` BEFORE enqueue.
Failed/missing acknowledgement means zero relay reply bytes; admission/storage
failure is bounded failure, not a generic unacknowledged denial. Supported
policy rejection and separately validated cancellation are separate paths.
An existing allow is never rewritten or acknowledged late. `delivered` is
acknowledgement, not pipe output, Cursor receipt, native claim, execution or
dialog closure; an ack-before-crash can remain delivered without receipt.

`protocol.sendGuarded` uses the existing serialized bounded writer with a
request-specific guard, fixed deadline and completion callback. Immediately
before Write, `CheckCursorAnswer` rechecks current authority and the exact
acknowledgement/native claim; the writer checks transport expiry again after
slow guards. Both guards use the earlier of the existing frame and applicable
request deadlines. `CheckCursorAnswer` bounds connection and transaction
acquisition by that remaining time, then revalidates current authority,
retirement and expiry after waiting and independent evidence. Allows expire
at the decision deadline, denials by settlement.
Queued allow AND deny retire on settlement/cancellation/ownership loss.
Partial/uncertain output is never replayed. Close and enqueue linearize under
`outputMu`; active/queued accepted frames receive bounded failure completion,
with callbacks outside the lock and no locks held across guards or I/O.

`terminalInputLoop` routes a displayed single key immediately without Enter.
The menu binds each key to token/option at read time; keys are unique across
the connection and simultaneous menus, never inferred upstream option numbers.
`ClaimCursorPaneAnswer` arbitrates native choice against API decision, consuming
automated intent only after `sent` and only when its claimed verdict matches
the actual selected option. A native choice derives its verdict from that
option. Neither sent nor native claim proves ACP delivery or receipt.
Existing send-keys token/hash/ownership and
intent/sent rules remain. `record-pane-answer` outside claims supply neither
ACP approval authority nor proof. Before fallback transition, expired captured
choices are discarded. A fresh deliberate connected choice after settlement
may resolve an unacknowledged still-open native request, including a recorded
API decision. Queued/uncertain replies, native timeout and terminal cancellation
cannot revive. Disconnection is visible failure, never fake pane availability
or runtime receipt.

Questions are never advertised. Direct, fallback, multi-question and ambiguous
authorization forms are rejected before admission in both relay modes and both
`disable_ask_user` settings, with no answerable `ask_user` or pane choices.
Supported direct extension cancellation does not cancel independent genuine
requests. Unsupported authorization can require validated bounded session
cancellation; independent stored holds remain conservative.

Invocation proof is deliberately narrow: the current exact request token,
`toolCallId`, launch, life, session, connection and full runtime binding must
match a `tool_call_update`, with current pipe, descriptor and pane checks.
`authorization.executionOutput` accepts execute-kind shell output with
completed/failed status, integer `exitCode` and non-null string
`stdout`/`stderr`. For an already-admitted MCP kind-other request, it accepts
only completed status and `rawOutput` containing exactly the single boolean
`success: true` property. Complete-envelope duplicate-key validation remains
mandatory; generic other-kind admission and ambiguous MCP output supply no
execution proof. `authorization.completedMCPError` separately accepts only an
already-admitted MCP kind-other request's completed update with exactly
`rawOutput:{"error":"Tool execution error"}` under the same checks.
`ProveCursorToolRan` then applies existing proof/close semantics to that request
only for validated execution. `ProveCursorToolFailed` instead writes only missing
`proven_gone_at` / `proven_gone_how`, using `tool_ran` for the exact invocation's
end, consistent with Claude's matching `PostToolUseFailure`. It establishes that
the dialog is gone without asserting that the underlying server action ran or
succeeded. Decision, reason, decided-at, delivery, pane answer and pane verdict
remain unchanged, including NULLs; it never infers allow. Both methods reuse
`proveCursorTool`, the existing write transaction and current `cursorAuthority`
owner, preserve earlier proof, exclude closed rows and emit the final retained
verdict/reason only after a committed mutation. A fully duplicate failed proof
performs no matched UPDATE and emits no event.
Generic status, other failed MCP output, plan acceptance, main/child Stop/Interrupt/completion and
session identity alone provide no such evidence. Other execution evidence
remains conservative. Generic `CloseToolRanRequests` and
`ProveRequestsGone(tool_ran)` exclude actual Cursor in SQL with `IS NOT`,
preserving NULL-agent/Claude/Codex compatibility. Main-turn proof still requires
durable eligibility plus NULL child identity; actual unknown-origin admission
never grants it. No child tracking or main conversation replacement is inferred.

`protocol.retiredResponse` uses a bounded numeric retirement watermark;
current/pending correlation remains strict. Known retired session events and
authorization/tool identities are inspectable without current lifecycle,
completion, answer or held-release authority. Numeric response attribution uses
the known per-conversation request boundaries; initialize/unknown origin remains
empty. Missing current update attribution fails closed. Owned-runtime death is
checked before retired traffic. Rotation and local cancellation never turn
unknown request origin into eligible main-turn proof, nor close independent
holds. Both guarded answer writers and acknowledgement-before-output remain
mandatory across identity changes.

Expanded runtime acceptance, group profiles and session help remain outside
this bounded argument/configuration change. Linux protected lifetime and
account limits remain; synthetic controller evidence does not establish
runtime/version/platform acceptance or all interleavings. Existing formal
models do not prove this controller; its formal assessment remains separate.

**Must use:** Cursor launch composition and argument checks use the existing
`internal/spawn` seams, `ReadCursorArgs` and `CursorLaunchArgs` (or its
`CursorArgs` validation wrapper); no surface builds another launch or token parser.
Session configuration extends `mode.go` and the existing controller phases,
correlation and guarded writer rather than introducing another ACP controller.
Runtime/report checks use `VerifyRuntime`, `VerifyTranscriptPath`, `VerifyPane`
and `HandleConfig.VerifyCursor`, keeping immediate-parent and conditional
store guards mandatory. New Cursor record writes use the existing
`RegisterCursorRuntime`, startup-only `SetCursorRuntimeSession`,
`BindLoadedCursorSession`, `CheckLoadedCursorPrompt`,
`RotateCursorSession`, `ObserveCursorRotation`, `ReconcileCursorRotation`,
`MarkCursorRuntimeGone`
and conditional hook store paths; missing cleanup uses the distinct strict-read
and proven-dead fatal methods above. Authorization changes MUST extend
`parseAuthorization`, `authorization.result`, `authorization.executionOutput`,
`authorization.completedMCPError`
and the single `requestController`;
reuse `InsertCursorRequest`, `AckCursorDecision`, `ClaimCursorPaneAnswer`,
`CheckCursorAnswer`, `ProveCursorToolRan` and `ProveCursorToolFailed` with mandatory
`CursorCheck`. Proof changes MUST reuse their shared `proveCursorTool` and
`cursorAuthority` transaction owner rather than introduce another proof framework,
bypass transactional authority or fabricate hook evidence.
Outbound protocol changes use the bounded, serialized writer and independently
closeable transport; preserve the registered ownership descriptor until end verification. Protocol, input and
persistence changes extend the single `internal/cursorhost`
controller/recorder; do not create parallel pipes, a second input owner,
screen classification or another transcript format.

### cursorfix: synthetic ACP runtime (reusable test fixture)

`internal/testsupport/cursorfix` owns `runtime.js` at its package root, embedded
by `cursorfix.go`. `New` and `NewWithWorker` produce a private executable
Node stand-in, trace and independently observable accepting runtime/worker
pid and release files. `Runtime.Frames` decodes complete incoming JSON lines;
`Raw` records all incoming bytes before readline, including partial lines.
`Sent`/`SentFrames` record scripted peer output; actual gateway admission
separately establishes reception. An optional synchronous executable at
`Observer` can read independently committed store state at the raw data callback,
before line parsing. These are test observations, not production APIs or
authenticated Cursor evidence.
`Runtime.MCPTrace` records the configured real MCP child's PID/start, correlated
initialize response, standard initialized notification and tool responses.
`MCPRelease` and `Scenario` controls can delay or omit that notification for
ordering and deadline cases. The fixture starts the registered command with its
actual argv and explicit environment and validates canonical instructions; it
never fabricates the private nonce receipt. Null session parameters remain valid
for existing protocol-only fixtures. The peer retains the exact configured
process handle and captured registration. `Runtime.MCPControl` and `MCPCommand`
serialize post-readiness useful calls, abrupt stop with bounded actual exit,
and restart of that same command/argv/environment through the existing standard
exchange. New attempts retain correlated replies and PID/start observations;
they do not amend scope or manufacture receipts. `Runtime.Settings()` exposes
isolated per-child files through explicit `AD_CURSOR_FIX_SETTINGS` selection
while sharing one stable fixture executable. Child scenarios, traces, runtime
PIDs and release/control files remain independent; tests MUST reuse this
selection rather than rewrite the running parent's config or executable.
The synthetic MCP peer retries only `read-pane` after a valid correlated
JSON-RPC 2.0 error with code `-32000` and structured
`error.data.err_name: ErrTmuxUnresponsive`. Each logical tool call retains one
original monotonic 10-second allowance across physical attempts and backoff;
attempts use fresh IDs and the original arguments. Failed physical
request/response metadata remains in the trace; only the final complete success
emits a logical `tool_response`. Partial capture data never counts as success.
Other tools, malformed replies, other errors and request timeouts do not retry.
Exit or transport failure cancels pending requests and backoff; a retired handle
cannot continue against its replacement. This fixture recovery adds no public
automatic retry or product deadline and establishes no authenticated or native
Cursor evidence.
Future guidance and configured-process restart cases MUST extend this
shared peer and its existing session/load/rotation helpers. In-process gateway

`internal/testsupport/clibuild.Build` is the sandbox-guarded shared actual CLI
