> detectable via `errors.Is`.

CLI callers set `Options.CreateIfMissing = true`: a missing store is
created and initialized automatically on the first store-backed invocation.

The global flag `--create-if-missing false` (both command binaries, `serve`
included) turns that off for one run (b.78b): `clisetup.APIOptions` passes
`CreateIfMissing: false`, so a store-backed verb on a missing store fails
with `ErrStoreOpen` (`clisetup.NewOpenError`; cause
`store.ErrStoreNotInitialized`, `database not initialized`) before the verb
runs, and nothing is created: no parent directory, file or schema.
`--create-if-missing true`, or no flag, keeps the default. Verbs that open no
store (`help`, `version`, the no-verb run, `trail-emit`) are unaffected, and
`hook`, which takes no global flags, opens Claude/Codex stores with
`OpenOrInitWithBusyTimeout`. Cursor hooks use `OpenWithBusyTimeout` and
require an existing store and authenticated runtime binding. The TS client's `createIfMissing: false`
forwards the flag (see [Client lifecycle](#client-lifecycle)).

**`Close`.** Marks the Client closed under its mutex, then releases the
mutex before closing the store. New verb calls observe `ErrClientClosed`
without waiting behind database cleanup. It does not stop an agent or drain
the process trail writer. Idempotent: a second call
returns `nil` without double-closing the underlying `*store.Store`. After
`Close` returns, any subsequent verb method call on the client returns the
sentinel `ErrClientClosed` (detectable via `errors.Is`).

### `internal/layout`

The directory agent-director keeps its files in is `.config/agent-director`
under the user's home, shown as `~/.config/agent-director`. `internal/layout`
is its one definition (see its row in the package inventory); the config
defaults, the store, the error log, the trail, the templates, the install
layout and the version result's `config_dir` all take the directory and the
names in it from there.

**HOME only.** The home is `os.UserHomeDir` (`$HOME`), never the passwd
entry, and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` is never read: a user who sets it still gets
`~/.config/agent-director`. With `HOME` unset or empty there is no directory,
and each caller refuses or skips as it did for the old directory (see "No
usable home" under [internal/store](#internalstore)).

**The old directory.** Before the move agent-director kept its files in a
directory directly under the home, named like the new one with a leading dot
and no `.config` parent. `old.go` is the only code that names it. Its rules:

| Function | True when |
| --- | --- |
| `OldPresent(home)` | anything exists at the old name, a dangling link included, except a link whose target is AD's directory (a compatibility link, judged lexically from the link's raw target, taken relative to home when relative, whether or not the target exists). A `home` that is not absolute has no old directory. |
| `NewPresent(home)` | AD's directory exists, as a directory or a link that resolves to one. |
| `OnlyOldPresent(home)` | `OldPresent` and not `NewPresent`: the state in which the trail writes nothing. |
| `StoreExists(home)` | a store file exists at the default path (a link counts when its target exists; an error other than not-exist, such as a refused permission, counts as existing, because the open reports it better). |

Two refusals use them. `store.CheckOldLayout()` returns `store.ErrOldLayout`
when `OldPresent` and not `StoreExists`; `pkg/api.New` and `clisetup.Open`
call it only when about to open the default store (see [Old layout (step
2b)](#pkgapi-client-lifecycle)). The trail writer asks `OnlyOldPresent` on
every `Emit` and writes, creates and logs nothing while it is true (see [Trail
file](#trail-file)). The hook asks `store.CheckOldLayout` under the same default-store rule
after its stdin peek and before its logger (`hookOldLayout` in
`cmd/agent-director/main.go`; a config that does not load is not judged
there): it
fails open with exit 0 and one stderr line, writes nothing, and a relayed
`PermissionRequest` still gets its deny.

**Must use:** a new default path derives from `layout.Dir` / `layout.Join`
and the name constants, never a literal; a check "is the old directory
there" goes through `old.go`. `TestOldPathAbsentFromProduct` fails on a
product file that names the old directory (see [The old-path
test](#the-old-path-test)).

### `internal/store`

`internal/store` is the only layer in the binary permitted to speak SQL.
All other packages call typed methods on a `*store.Store` and never see a
`*sql.DB`, a SQL string, or a database driver error. Hard rule, kept here
verbatim so future code review can grep for it:

> No SQL outside `internal/store`; callers use typed query primitives only.

**Schema v13** lives in `internal/store/schema.go`. Seven tables. The v9 hop
renamed agent-generic fields; v13's `claude_capacity` is deliberately
Claude-specific capacity provenance (see
[Store upgrade to agent-generic names](#store-upgrade-to-agent-generic-names)):

- `spawns` — one row per agent instance under direction (Claude Code,
  Codex or Cursor), keyed by `instance_id`, with parent/child link (`parent_id`),
  lifecycle (`state`, the raw state, `started_at`, `last_seen_at`,
  `ended_at`), the settle columns `settled_state` and `state_changed_ms`
  (see "v8 columns" below), the agent columns `agent` and
  `end_reported_at` and the subagent tracking flag `subagent_tracking`
  (see "v9 columns" below), the v12 `family_state`, `family_settled_state`
  and `family_changed_ms` columns (see [Family reporting](#family-reporting)),
  nullable v13 `codex_startup` origin metadata and
  `claude_capacity` capacity provenance
  (see [Experimental context readers](#experimental-context-readers)), the agent's arguments
  (`agent_args`) and session id (`session_id`), tmux + relay metadata, and a
  JSON-encoded `labels` blob. Indexed on `state`, `last_seen_at`, and
  `parent_id`.
- `cursor_runtimes` — the independently verified current Cursor launch
  binding, including gateway/runtime identities, private pipes, connection,
  session and termination marker; see [Cursor gateway](#cursor-gateway-and-current-launch-binding).
- `permission_requests` — one row per `(instance_id, request_token)`
  pair, FK-cascaded on spawn delete; `request_token TEXT NOT NULL`, composite
  `UNIQUE(instance_id, request_token)`, with `tool_name`, `tool_input`,
  `decision`, `decision_reason`, `decided_at`, `created_at` and the v7
  relay columns plus durable proof eligibility (see v7/v11 columns below). Indexed on
  `(instance_id, decision)` and `(decision, decided_at)`.
- `session_history` (v4, b.v2c) — one row per `(instance_id,
  session_id)` pair the row has archived, FK-cascaded on spawn
  delete; `session_id TEXT NOT NULL`, nullable `jsonl_path`,
  `recorded_at`, composite `UNIQUE(instance_id, session_id)`,
  indexed on `instance_id`. When a session rotates (the agent's row
  is reported with a new session id), the prior `(session id, jsonl_path)`
  is archived here within the gated transaction. Successful archival keeps
  its reference inspectable; a fail-open archive error can strand it.
  - **History belongs to a life.** Each entry carries the life it belongs to
    (`life_number`, see "v5 columns" below): the life the row was in when that
    session ran. A life begins at insert or an agent-switch reset and ends at the
    next switch. Same-agent reuse, resume and session rotation keep it.
    The rotation archive, inside SessionStart's gated write,
    takes the outgoing session id from the snapshot the hook examined and
    that session's jsonl path and life from a read pinned to that same
    snapshot, so all three belong to one row version. The reuse archive,
    inside `ResetForReuse`'s transaction, takes the current session id,
    path and life from its own in-transaction read and tags the entry with
    the outgoing life, whether or not the agent changes; it moves an entry
    archived in an earlier life to that life. Only a reset whose raw agent
    differs exactly from `fresh.Agent` advances `life_number`. Same-agent
    reuse retains visible history; switching either way, including back,
    starts empty visible history. Earlier lives' entries remain hidden.
    Resume never tries archived sessions, even within the current life.
    An applied restore
    after a failed reuse writes the pre-reuse life number back, so that
    life's visible history is exactly as before the attempt (the entry the
    reuse archived is the row's current session id, which the visible
    history drops). After a restored switch, its abandoned number can be
    used by the next switch; a same-agent reset keeps the restored life.
    No entry belongs to the
    abandoned attempt's life, because the reset row records no pane, so no
    hook (and so no rotation archive) applies to it before the restore.
  - **One entry per instance and session id.** Re-archiving a session id
    within the same life keeps an already-recorded path when the new path is
    NULL and refreshes `recorded_at`. Re-archiving it in a later life moves
    the entry to that life, with that life's path exactly (NULL included),
    and refreshes `recorded_at`; no path from the earlier life survives.
  - **Retention and reads.** The store keeps every entry until the row is
    deleted or expired. Its history read, `ListSessionHistory(id, life)`,
    returns one life's entries, newest first, and keeps an entry equal to the
    row's current session id. `resume` and `get` read the life of the row
    they read and use only its *visible history*: that life's entries minus
    any entry whose session id equals the row's current, non-empty session
    id (`visibleHistory` in `pkg/api/visible_history.go`). The visible
    history is the queryable link from a row back to the earlier sessions of
    its current life, surfaced through `get`'s `prior_sessions` and consulted
    by `resume` only to classify a failed current-session lookup as
    never-written or missing. No history entry is statted or selected.
    **Must use:** every
    `pkg/api` reader of session history applies the current-session rule
    through `visibleHistory` (`pkg/api/visible_history.go`), never its own
    filter.
  - **Must use:** every product-code archive into `session_history` goes
    through
    `upsertSessionHistoryEntry(q querier, instanceID, sessionID, jsonlPath,
    life)` in `internal/store/session_history.go`. It runs one statement on
    the pool or on a transaction the caller already holds, reads nothing
    (the caller passes values it has already read), and applies the rules
    above: within the same life a known path is kept, and in another life
    the entry moves with that life's path exactly. It emits no trail event
    and advances no `row_version`; callers own their events and failure
    policy. Two archives call it: the rotation archive, on SessionStart's
    transaction (fail-open: a history error still commits the
    SessionStart write and emits `ad.session.archive_failed`), and the
    reuse archive, on `ResetForReuse`'s transaction through
    `connQuerier` (fail-closed: a history error rolls the whole change
    back and returns an error holding `ErrReuseArchive`). Every new code
    path that archives a session must call it too, never a second upsert.
- `subagents` (v9, b.xjn) — one row per subagent id and life of a spawn row: a
  record (`confirmed` 1) or an observation (`confirmed` 0). Only
  `internal/store` reads or writes it; `list-subagents` returns its confirmed
  records through the store read. The
  columns, with their exact text in `schemaDDL` for a fresh store and in
  `v9SubagentTablesSQL`, the v8 → v9 hop's own copy
  (`internal/store/schema.go`):
  - `created_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT` grows with each insert and
    is never reused, so it orders creation and breaks every tie.
  - `instance_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES spawns(instance_id) ON DELETE
    CASCADE`, with `UNIQUE(instance_id, life_number, subagent_id)`: one entry
    per row, life and subagent id. That constraint's implicit index serves the
    per-row read, the
    per-launch transitions and the cap, which all lead with `instance_id`;
    the table has no explicit index.
  - `launch_token TEXT NOT NULL`, the launch the entry belongs to;
    `confirmed INTEGER NOT NULL`; `state TEXT NOT NULL` (the values
    `store.SubagentStateRunning`, `SubagentStateStopped` and
    `SubagentStateLost`); `close_reason TEXT`, NULL while running (the values
    `SubagentCloseStopEvent`, `SubagentCloseAbsentFromSnapshot` and
    `SubagentCloseAgentGone`).
  - Nullable fields: `session_id`, `subagent_type`, `description`, `model`,
    `parent_type` (`SubagentParentAgent` or `SubagentParentSubagent`),
    `parent_id`, `tool_use_id`, `run_mode` (`SubagentRunModeBackground` or
    `SubagentRunModeForeground`), all TEXT, and the INTEGER times
    `first_started_at`, `started_at`, `stopped_at` and `lost_at`, in
    milliseconds since the epoch. NULL means the value is unknown.
  - `opened_at INTEGER NOT NULL`: the latest time the entry became running,
    or its creation time. `activity_at INTEGER NOT NULL`: the instant of the
    latest write that changed the entry. Both are what the cap's eviction
    order reads.
  - `subagent_type_source`, `run_mode_source` and `stopped_at_source`, all
    nullable TEXT: which source set a value that has more than one
    (`SubagentSourceStart`, `SubagentSourceDetails`, `SubagentSourceSnapshot`,
    `SubagentSourceStop`; NULL while the value is unknown).
  - `life_number INTEGER NOT NULL`, appended after `stopped_at_source` in
    both fresh and migrated schemas. An entry's life is immutable: its insert
    reads `spawns.life_number` in the same gated `INSERT … SELECT` that reads
    the current launch token; later entry updates never change its life.
- `subagent_launches` (v9, b.xjn) — one row per open claimable launch: an
  internal note that an agent's Agent tool call has not yet been matched to a
  subagent. Internal to `internal/store`, and never shown by any verb.
  `created_seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT`, `instance_id TEXT NOT NULL
  REFERENCES spawns(instance_id) ON DELETE CASCADE`, `launch_token`,
  `tool_use_id` and `subagent_type` (all TEXT NOT NULL), `opened_at INTEGER
  NOT NULL`, with `UNIQUE(instance_id, tool_use_id)` (one note per row and
  tool call, and the index later closes use) and one explicit index,
  `idx_subagent_launches_claim` on `(instance_id, launch_token,
  subagent_type, opened_at)`, which serves the claim of the oldest note of the
  current launch and type.
  - **Lifetime.** Both tables belong to the row, not to a launch: no end or
    start of a launch deletes an entry, so entries survive a resume and a reuse
    (an entry's immutable `life_number` says which life it belongs to, and its
    mutable `launch_token` which launch within that life), their
    `running` ones closed and the row's notes deleted by the liveness close
    (see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)). They go with the row through the foreign key's
    cascade: `expire`'s `DeleteFinishedIfSameLife` and the admin `delete`
    (`DeleteSpawn`) remove a row's entries and notes with the row (see
    [`expire`](#expire) and [`delete`](#delete)).
  - **Retention: two caps of 300.** One row holds at most
    `store.SubagentCap` (300) entries (records and observations of every launch
    and life together, including hidden earlier-life entries) and at most 300
    claimable launches. At the cap, one more insert
    evicts exactly one row first. Entries: the closed observation (`confirmed`
    0, `state` not `running`) with the oldest `activity_at`; when no
    observation is closed, the closed record with the oldest `activity_at`;
    when nothing closed remains, the running entry with the oldest
    `activity_at`; ties go to the lowest `created_seq`. Claimable launches: the
    note with the oldest `opened_at`, ties to the lowest `created_seq`. Below
    the cap nothing is evicted.
  - **Must use:** every insert of an entry or a claimable launch calls the
    gated cap step first, `evictSubagentEntryGated` or
    `evictSubagentLaunchGated` (`internal/store/subagents.go`), never its own
    count or delete and never an ungated eviction (none exists). Each is one
    `DELETE` on the caller's transaction, connection or pool (the `querier`),
    with the hook gate and the four row conditions in its own `WHERE` (see
    [Subagent capture](#subagent-capture)), so it commits or rolls back with
    the caller's write; it never begins or ends a transaction, and returns
    whether it evicted a row. A writer holds the write lock first
    (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, see "the write lock before the read" under "Versioned
    writes"), so the count and the insert see one state. The value sets
    above are `store.Subagent*` constants; compare against them, never
    against literals. The eviction tests reach the two functions through the
    export shim `internal/store/subagents_export_test.go`
    (`store.EvictSubagentEntryGatedForTest` and
    `store.EvictSubagentLaunchGatedForTest`, each one committed transaction
    that takes the `HookGate`).
- `store_meta` (v5, b.fmk; SR-5.1) — `key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT
  NULL`, with one row in Phase 1: `store_id`, the store's identity. Every
  `@ad_owner` label carries it as its last field (see `internal/tmux` in the
  package inventory).
  - **Value.** 64 random bits from `crypto/rand`, written as 16 lowercase hex
    characters. It is random, not secret, but no error message ever contains
    it (SR-15).
  - **Created once, never changed.** `createSchema` (a new store) and
    `migrateV4toV5` (the hop) insert it inside their own transaction, before
    the stamp, only when no `store_id` row exists (`insertStoreIDOnceSQL` in
    `internal/store/storeid.go`, the only statement that writes
    `store_meta`). No verb changes it, and a restore keeps it because it is in
    the file.
  - **Read once at open.** `openDB` reads it after `ensureSchema` succeeds
    (`readStoreID`), and `(*Store).StoreID()` returns it. A current-version
    store with no `store_meta` table, no `store_id` row, or a value that is
    not 16 lowercase hex refuses to open with an error wrapping
    `ErrSchemaMismatch`; the DB is closed and nothing is written. Any other
    read error (busy, I/O) is returned as it is. So every open `*Store` holds
    a well-formed id; treating a malformed value like a missing row keeps a
    made-up id out of labels.
  - **Must use:** production code reads the id through `(*Store).StoreID()`,
    never by querying `store_meta`, and writes it only through
    `insertStoreIDOnce`. Tests read and pin it through the `apitest` store-id
    helpers (`ReadStoreID`, `SeedStoreID`).

**v5 columns (b.fmk).** Schema v5 adds twelve `spawns` columns, after the
v4 columns, and one `session_history` column. They are the storage later work
builds on. The store gives each column its default on insert and on
migration. Beyond that, the v5 writes are the ones under "Versioned writes"
below (every `spawns` update advances `row_version`, and some clear
`launch_started_at`) and the rotation and reuse archives, which write
`session_history.life_number` through `upsertSessionHistoryEntry`. Verbs
report two of the columns, and only for display: `status`, `get` and `list`
report the launch start as `launch_started_at`, and `get` alone reports the
recorded socket as `tmux_socket` (see "Where callers see the launch start"
and "Where the socket is shown" under [Launch identity](#launch-identity)).
No verb reports any other v5 column.

- **Row version** — `spawns.row_version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. A
  per-row change counter, so a conditional write can tell that the row changed
  since it was read.
- **Launch start** — `spawns.launch_started_at INTEGER` (nullable). The time,
  in epoch milliseconds, that the row's current launch began; NULL when no
  launch is in progress.
- **Life numbers** — `spawns.life_number` and `session_history.life_number`,
  both `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. The row's current life and the life each
  history entry belongs to, so the history of a reused id can be split by
  life. `spawns.life_number` changes only through reuse: the reset
  (`ResetForReuse`) advances it by one only on an exact raw-agent mismatch;
  same-agent reuse keeps it. Recorded older lives are never renumbered. An applied restore after a
  failed reuse (`RestoreAfterFailedReuse`) sets it back to the pre-reuse
  value. A `resume` keeps it.
- **Pre-trust choice** — `spawns.no_pre_trust INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`. The
  pre-trust choice of the latest spawn or reuse, until the next spawn or reuse:
  0 means pre-trust allowed, anything else means the caller opted out.
- **Launch identity** — eight nullable `spawns` columns: `launch_token` (TEXT,
  the launch's token), `tmux_socket` (TEXT, the tmux socket the launch uses),
  the tmux server's identity `tmux_server_pid` (INTEGER),
  `tmux_server_started` (INTEGER) and `tmux_server_starttime` (TEXT), and the
  agent's pane `pane_id` (TEXT), `pane_pid` (INTEGER) and `pane_starttime`
  (TEXT). Together they say which tmux server, session label and pane belong
  to the row's current launch.

None of the thirteen has a CHECK constraint or an index. `schemaDDL` and
`migrateV4toV5` declare them with the same text, in the same order, so a
fresh store and a migrated store have identical column lists on both tables.

**v6 columns: the launch owner (b.kdf; b.146 rule 11).** Schema v6 adds three
nullable `spawns` columns after `pane_starttime`, in this order:
`launch_owner_pid` (INTEGER), `launch_owner_starttime` (TEXT, in
`proc_starttime`'s form) and `launch_owner_pidns` (TEXT, the owner's pid
namespace as `probe.SelfPIDNamespace` reads it). Together they name the
process that began the row's current launch, while that launch holds the
row, so `find-missing` can tell a launch still in progress (a `spawn` or
`resume` stalled past the pending grace period) from one whose process is
gone. None has a CHECK constraint or an index; `schemaDDL` and
`migrateV5toV6` declare them with the same text, in the same order. No verb
reports them.

- **Type.** `store.LaunchOwner{PID, Starttime, PIDNamespace}` (alias
  `api.LaunchOwner`), zero values meaning NULL. PID 0 records no owner: a
  row from before schema v6, a launch whose own start time or pid namespace
  could not be read, or a launch whose hold has ended. The columns mean
  something only on a `pending` row; on any other row they are never read.
- **Writers.** The three writes that begin a launch record the owner:
  `InsertPending` (plain spawn) and `ResetForReuse` (reuse) from
  `Spawn.LaunchOwner`, and `MoveToPending` (resume) from its `owner`
  parameter, each zero field as NULL. Two writes end the hold by NULLing all
  three (`launchOwnerClear`): `RecordLaunchIdentity`, the launch's last
  write, and `ReleaseLaunchOwner`, for a launch that ends without it.
  `RestoreAfterFailedReuse` writes the three back as part of `RawLife`. No
  other write touches them.
- **Readers.** Every read that returns a `Spawn` fills `Spawn.LaunchOwner`
  through `launchOwnerColumns` after `lifeColumns` (`spawnColumns`), and
  the live-row read fills `LiveSpawnIdentity.LaunchOwner` through the same
  fragment, so the two agree for a row.
- **Must use:** a read of the launch owner selects `launchOwnerColumns` and
  scans with `launchOwnerDest`; a write of it binds `launchOwnerArgs`; a
  write that ends a launch's hold uses `launchOwnerClear`
  (`internal/store/rowsnapshot.go`). A launch takes its owner only from
  `spawn.CurrentLaunchOwner` (the calling process: its pid, its start time
  through the same start-time reader every process judgement uses, and its
  pid namespace; the zero owner when either cannot be read), and a reader
  decides whether an owner still holds a row only through
  `spawn.LaunchOwnerAlive` (an owner is recorded, the caller's own pid
  namespace can be read and equals the owner's, and `tmux.JudgeProcess`
  finds the owner's pid alive with exactly its recorded start time; every
  other case is false, so the row falls back to its pending grace period).
  A path that ends a launch without its identity write ends the hold through
  `spawn.ReleaseLaunchOwner` (`internal/spawn/launch_owner.go`), never a
  write of its own.
- **One process identity type.** `store.LaunchOwner` is an alias of
  `store.ProcessIdentity{PID, Starttime, PIDNamespace}` (b.146 rule 14), the
  type of every recorded process: a row's launch owner, and a permission
  request's relay hook and pane-answer sender (v7 columns below). A write
  binds one through `processIdentityArgs`.

**v7 columns: the relay's delivery facts (b.146 steps 2, 2b and 2c; one
migration).** Schema v7 adds nineteen columns to `permission_requests`,
after `created_at`, and one to `spawns`, after `launch_owner_pidns`. They
are listed once, with their exact DDL text, in `v7Columns`
(`internal/store/schema.go`), which `migrateV6toV7` walks and `schemaDDL`
repeats. Steps 2, 2b and 2c ship in one release, so a later step adds its
columns to this same list. None has a CHECK constraint or an index.

| Column | Type | Written by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `hook_pid`, `hook_starttime`, `hook_pidns` | INTEGER, TEXT, TEXT | the relay hook's first write (all NULL for Cursor gateway requests) | The relay hook as it read itself at its start (`HandleConfig.Self`): its pid, its start time (field 22 of `/proc/self/stat`, the form `proc_starttime` records) and its pid namespace (the target of `/proc/self/ns/pid`, as `probe.SelfPIDNamespace` reads it; `""` on darwin). NULL when it could not read them. |
| `tool_use_id`, `agent_id` | TEXT | initial request admission | Hook input fields, or Cursor's actual `toolCallId` and NULL child identity. NULL when absent. No index or UNIQUE covers either; Cursor proof additionally binds the exact request token. |
| `delivered_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms) | the relay hook's or Cursor request controller's ack/timeout deny | Durable acknowledgement committed before answer output; Cursor commits before enqueue. Never receipt or execution proof. |
| `settled_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms) | initial request admission | The fixed `confirm_by`: Claude/Codex hook kill plus 2 s; Cursor decision window plus 4 s, immediately past for relay off. NULL marks a request recorded before v7 (`PermissionRow.PreV7`). |
| `hook_gone_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms) | readers, `decide`, `send-keys`, `record-pane-answer`, pane intent, Cursor native claim and the PostToolUse close | When a reader first found the request fallen back; `COALESCE`d, so the first value stays. |
| `attempted_decision`, `attempted_at` | TEXT, INTEGER (epoch ms) | `decide` refusing with `ErrRelayFallenBack` | The refused verdict, the latest one; shown, never acted on. |
| `pane_answer` | TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT `'none'` | pane writes (`internal/store/pane_writes.go`), Cursor native claim/proof | How the request was answered at the pane (b.146 step 2b): `none` (nothing recorded through agent-director), `intent` (a pane answer's intent, its key maybe typed), `sent` (its key sent or a Cursor native choice recorded; neither establishes ACP delivery, receipt or proof), `outside` (`record-pane-answer`), `tool_ran` (Claude PostToolUse close or validated Cursor execution). `none` and `intent` leave a request awaiting an answer; the other three close it (`PermissionRow.PaneAnswered`). The values are the `PaneAnswer*` constants of `internal/store/permission.go`. |
| `pane_as` | TEXT | pane intent, `record-pane-answer`, Cursor native claim | The claimed verdict (`allow`, `deny`; `unknown` from `record-pane-answer`). Public pane writes store it without interpreting the screen or verifying its verdict. Before granting ACP response authority, Cursor additionally requires a sent claim to match the actual selected option; native choices derive their verdict from that option. An outside claim never supplies ACP approval authority or proof. |
| `pane_sender_pid`, `pane_sender_starttime`, `pane_sender_pidns` | INTEGER, TEXT, TEXT | a pane answer's intent | The process that sends the pane answer's key (`SendKeysEnv.Self`), judged as a relay hook is (`relayJudge.sender`); NULL when it could not read itself, and NULLed when it releases its intent. |
| `pane_intent_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms) | a pane answer's intent | When the intent was written, read inside `RecordPaneIntent`'s transaction after its `PaneCheck` (so it is the commit's instant, not the call's start): the key of the sender's own later writes (`paneIntentOwnerSQL`) and the start of `paneIntentHold` for a sender that cannot be checked. NULLed with the sender when the intent is released; never cleared by age. |
| `closed_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms) | a close of the Spawn's requests (`closeOrphanedRequests`): `find-missing`'s mark, the terminal SessionEnd's move to `ended`, and resume's move to `pending` | When the close closed the request, which still awaited an answer when its Spawn was marked `missing` or ended, or when its finished Spawn was resumed (b.146 rule 12): an undecided one is also denied (`find_missing` for the mark, `ended` for the other two); a decided one whose hook had not acked keeps its verdict. A closed request no longer awaits an answer (`PermissionRow.Closed`). NULL on every request no close closed; a decided pre-v7 request without an ack or completed pane answer is closed too, preserving its verdict. |
| `proven_gone_at`, `proven_gone_how` | INTEGER (epoch ms), TEXT | a hook's proof (`ProveRequestsGone`, `internal/store/request_proof.go`), validated Cursor invocation proof (`ProveCursorToolRan` / `ProveCursorToolFailed`), the PostToolUse close, a close of the Spawn's requests (`closeOrphanedRequests`), and `migrateV6toV7`'s phase 3 (`v7ProveFinishedSQL`) | When the agent proved the request's permission dialog gone (b.146 step 2c; see "Proofs by agent" under [The dialog hold](#the-dialog-hold-step-2c)), and how: `tool_ran` (Claude `PostToolUse`/`PostToolUseFailure` with its `tool_use_id`, or authenticated exact-request Cursor invocation proof under [Cursor authorization dataflow and authority](#cursor-authorization-dataflow-and-authority), where a failed MCP invocation proves only dialog closure; Codex has no tool-run proof), `turn_end` (the turn of the agent that asked ended after it was written; Claude's main-agent `Stop` or idle-prompt Notification, or Codex's main-agent `Stop` or `Interrupt`, proves a durably eligible request with no `agent_id` whose `created_at` is before the second the hook started, b.omt), `agent_gone` (a close of its Spawn's requests, including the Codex move to `ended` after its verified process is gone and its end report is recorded, or the v6 → v7 hop on a row already `ended` or `missing`). The values are the `ProvenGone*` constants of `internal/store/permission.go`; `PermissionRow.ProvenGone` reports a proven request. Each is written once: a write never replaces an earlier proof. NULL until proven, every request recorded before v7 on a live row included; while NULL on a live relay-on Spawn, the request holds plain `send-keys` without a pane hash and `pause` (`ErrDialogMaybeOpen`) and is never evicted at the cap (see "Cap-based GC"), and, while it also awaits an answer, holds the row (`holdsRowSQL`: the working hold, the idle-prompt Notification's move out of `check_permission` and `find-missing`'s repair; b.omt). Once set, the request holds the row no longer, even while it still awaits an answer. |
| `spawns.idle_since` | TEXT (`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`) | the idle-prompt Notification | When the main agent's idle-prompt Notification last landed; NULLed by every other applied hook (`idleClear`). |

### v11 columns: durable main-turn proof eligibility

`permission_requests.main_turn_end_eligible INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` is
appended after `proven_gone_how`. `PermissionRow.MainTurnEndEligible` carries
the persisted bool; nullable `agent_id` separately carries known child identity.
Main-turn proof requires BOTH `main_turn_end_eligible = 1` AND `agent_id IS NULL`;
NULL child identity alone supplies no origin evidence. Even an already-current
current row corrupted to child=true remains excluded from main-turn proof.
Only matching owning tool-use proof or owning-spawn end can release such a hold.

`RelayRequest.MainTurnEndEligible` is an internal optional `*bool`: nil resolves
once inside `InsertRelayRequest`'s immediate transaction from the actual nullable
owning agent, preserving non-Cursor main/child behavior and defaulting Cursor to
false. An explicit false remains false; a nonempty child id overrides true to
false. The existing Claude/Codex hook writer supplies established origin.
Legacy `UpsertOpenPermissionRequest[Result]` uses the same NULL-safe non-Cursor
semantics in its gated INSERT SELECT. Supported historical NULL/malformed agents
are compatibility data, never a public agent default. All public JSON and
CLI/MCP/Go/TypeScript parameters remain unchanged; the bit is internal metadata.
`InsertCursorRequest` explicitly persists false with NULL child identity for
actual Cursor admissions. Any future main-origin support requires independent
evidence; authorization admission, plan acceptance and native claims grant none.

Every request reader uses `permissionColumns`/`scanPermissionRow`, reconstructing
the bit from SQLite after restart. Decision, acknowledgement, timeout, pane
intent/sent/outside/tool-ran claims, eviction and recovery never confer or
recompute eligibility. **Must use:** new request writers/readers reuse these
canonical construction/materialization seams and `RequestProof.match`, never
infer eligibility from a missing child id or gateway memory.

The distinct registered `migrateV10toV11` hop (`request_eligibility.go`) wraps
column DDL, backfill, validation, version stamp and commit in one transaction.
Only a newly added column is backfilled: `agent_id IS NULL` plus an existing
owning spawn whose `agent IS NOT 'cursor'` becomes true. Historical Cursor,
children and orphans stay false. Compatible existing columns retain explicit
values; incompatible case/type/null/default/primary-key shape, non-integer or
out-of-range values and true with a known child are refused transactionally
with `ErrSchemaMismatch`, preserving v10/data/authorization for corrected retry.
Fresh DDL retains the same eligibility shape alongside v12 family history
and v13 startup/capacity provenance. Earlier runtime/rename hops remain unchanged; rename threshold9 is immutable. Full engineering recovery
policy is in [migration-guide.md](migration-guide.md#historical-worked-example-v10--v11).

- **Readers.** Every read returning a `PermissionRow` selects
  `permissionColumns` and scans with `scanPermissionRow`
  (`internal/store/permission.go`), so all fill the v7 fields and v11 eligibility alike; the
  seven instants go through `millisArg` / `millisTime`
  (`internal/store/lockwait.go`). Every read returning a `Spawn` fills
  `Spawn.IdleSince` (`spawnColumns`, last).
- **Must use:** `awaitingAnswerSQL` (`internal/store/permission.go`) is the
  one statement of "a request still awaits an answer" (b.146 rules 9 and
  12): a request no close has closed (`closed_at IS NULL`) with no
  completed pane answer (`pane_answer` `none` or `intent`) that, recorded
  from v7 on, is not acked, decided or not, or, recorded before v7, is
  undecided. `OpenPermissionRequestsForSpawn` (`list`'s
  requests), the cap
  eviction, the undecided branch of the close of a Spawn's requests
  (`denyOrphanedRequestsSQL`), the pane writes (a pane answer's intent,
  `record-pane-answer`'s record) and the PostToolUse close all use it,
  and so does `holdsRowSQL` (below);
  never restate it. In Go, `PermissionRow.AwaitsAnswer()` states the same
  rule for a row already read (`get` picks its `permission_requests` out
  of its one read of every request with it), `Closed()` reports a closed request,
  `PaneAnswered()` a completed pane answer, and `CloseDenied()` a deny a
  close wrote (`decision_reason` `find_missing` or `ended`, no verdict a
  caller or relay hook chose). The decided branch of the lifecycle close
  (`closeDecidedRequestsSQL`) deliberately uses a separate predicate:
  decision present, `closed_at` and `delivered_at` NULL, `pane_answer`
  `none` or `intent`. Decided pre-v7 rows do not await an answer under
  `awaitingAnswerSQL`, but need durable closure before resume; do not
  broaden the shared awaiting-answer predicate to close them.
- **Must use:** `holdsRowSQL` (`internal/store/permission.go`) is the one
  statement of "a request holds its Spawn's row" (b.omt):
  `awaitingAnswerSQL` and `proven_gone_at IS NULL`. The non-Cursor working hold, Cursor working/waiting transitions,
  the idle-prompt Notification's move from `check_permission` to `waiting`
  (`ApplyHookWaitingIfWorking`) and `find-missing`'s repair
  (`repairCheckPermissionSQL`) use it. Non-Cursor working transitions first
  read `holdingRequestSQL` (`holdWorkingTransition`), then guard the UPDATE
  (`applyWorkingWrite`) with `NOT EXISTS` so a concurrently inserted request
  still holds the row. Cursor skips that preliminary hold read and attempts
  the guarded UPDATE for working and waiting (Stop/Interrupt). If rejected,
  it performs a gated soft refresh, retaining state and settle columns while
  refreshing activity and advancing row version even when `idle_since` was NULL.
  The Notification and repair carry the hold guard in their own statement. The move to
  `working` and the idle-prompt Notification's move share that `NOT
  EXISTS` as one fragment, `noRequestHoldsRowSQL`
  (`internal/store/hook_writes.go`); `repairCheckPermissionSQL` spells out
  its own. A request proven gone holds none of
  them, whatever agent-director's records say of it: one a person answered
  at the pane, which nothing records, still awaits an answer, and once the
  main agent's turn end after it (`turn_end`) or its tool's `PostToolUse`
  (`tool_ran`) proves it gone it no longer keeps the row in
  `check_permission`. Every other reader of a request that awaits an answer
  (`get` and `list`, `decide`, `send-keys` and its pane answers, the
  cap eviction) reads `awaitingAnswerSQL` alone, so such a
  request is still listed, decided, refused and closed as before. A new
  write that a request should hold off reads `holdsRowSQL`, never
  `awaitingAnswerSQL` with a proof test of its own, and carries it in the
  WHERE of the statement that writes (a hook write joins
  `noRequestHoldsRowSQL`), never in a separate read alone: a request's
  first write can commit between the read and the write.
- **Must use: a request's proof (b.146 step 2c).** A hook's proof that
  requests' dialogs are gone is written only by `ProveRequestsGone`
  (`internal/store/request_proof.go`, with a `RequestProof`: `How`
  `tool_ran` and its `ToolUseID`, or `turn_end` and its `RecordedBefore`,
  the hook's start; b.omt), the end of a non-Cursor Spawn's
  agent only by `closeOrphanedRequests`' third statement
  (`proveAgentGoneSQL`) and, for a row already finished when the store
  is migrated, `migrateV6toV7`'s phase 3 (`v7ProveFinishedSQL`), and the
  PostToolUse close sets it on what it closes; every write leaves an
  earlier proof as it is. "Proven gone" is
  `proven_gone_at IS NOT NULL` in SQL and `PermissionRow.ProvenGone()` in
  Go; agent-director's own records (`delivered_at`, `pane_answer`,
  `closed_at`) never stand for it.

**v8 columns: the settle time (b.3ie; one migration).** Schema v8 adds two
`spawns` columns after `idle_since`. They are listed once, with their exact
DDL text, in `v8Columns` (`internal/store/schema.go`), which
`migrateV7toV8` walks and `schemaDDL` repeats. Neither has a CHECK
constraint or an index. `state` stays the raw state, the one column every
guard reads. The writes and the derivation live in
`internal/store/settle.go` (model: `spec/tla/settle/`; see
[Settle time (b.3ie)](#settle-time-b3ie) for the semantics).

| Column | Type | Written by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `settled_state` | TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT `''` | every write of `state`, in the same statement | The last settled state as of the row's last raw change: what a read with a settle time reports while that change has not held long enough. `''` only on a row no write has given one (a hand-inserted row), which every reader takes as its raw state. |
| `state_changed_ms` | INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 (epoch ms) | every write that changes `state`'s value, in the same statement | When the raw state last changed, from SQLite's own clock inside the writing statement, under its write lock (`nowMsSQL`: `unixepoch('subsec')` in whole milliseconds; SQLite 3.42 or later, the bundled one is 3.46.0). 0 is older than any settle time. A write of the same value keeps it. |

- **Settling writes** of a non-terminal value V (`ApplyHookTransitionResult`'s
  transitions, both statements of `ApplyHookWaitingIfWorking`,
  `RecordSessionStartIdentity` and `InsertRelayRequest`), plus authenticated
  gateway admission through `InsertCursorRequest`, use `hookWriteStateSet`
  (which selects `hookStateSet` for a non-terminal value), with the writing
  process's settle time (`Store.settleMs`, set by `SetSettleMs`). SET sees the row as it was before the statement,
  so the statement alone decides: V equal to the raw state changes none of
  the three columns, so a same-value write or a duplicate hook never
  restarts the clock (a soft refresh writes no state at all); otherwise
  `settled_state` becomes the old raw state when it had settled (a settle
  time of 0, or it held at least that long) and keeps its value when it
  had not (the old raw state when it is `''`), `state` becomes V and
  `state_changed_ms` the statement's clock. A hook that moves a row out of
  `missing` or `ended`, which the hook gate allows for the row's own agent
  (find-missing's mark and the ended transition keep the pane, and resume's
  restore writes it back; SessionStart sets `waiting` whatever the prior
  state), makes such a write: the move settles.
- **Immediate writes**: a terminal value (`ended`, `missing`), a hook's
  included, and every state write outside the settling category above:
  `InsertPending`,
  `find-missing`'s mark (`MarkMissingIfSameLife`), its Codex move
  (`MarkEndedIfSameLife`) and its repair
  (`RepairCheckPermissionIfSameLife`), `EndHeldLaunch`, `MoveToPending`,
  `RestoreAfterFailedResume`, `ResetForReuse` and
  `RestoreAfterFailedReuse`. They use `immediateStateSet` (`state` and
  `settled_state` both V, `state_changed_ms` the statement's clock when V
  changes the raw value), so V reports at once and becomes the last
  settled value. `hookWriteStateSet(v)` picks it for a hook's terminal
  value. The reuse restore, whose SET list `rawLifeColumns` generates (the
  settle columns are not part of `RawLife`), appends `immediateSettleSet`;
  the repair, whose new state SQL picks from `idle_since`, sets
  `settled_state` with the same `CASE` and `state_changed_ms` to
  `nowMsSQL`; `InsertPending` inserts `pending` and `nowMsSQL`.
- **Reads.** `SettleRead{SettleMs, NowMs}` is a reader's settle time and
  clock, and `SettleRead.stateExpr` is the one derivation: with a settle
  time T, `CASE WHEN NowMs - state_changed_ms >= T THEN state ELSE
  COALESCE(NULLIF(settled_state, ''), state) END`, so a negative age (a
  clock behind the stamp) is not settled; with none, the bare `state`
  column and no argument, so the read statement is exactly the one before
  v8. Its readers are `SpawnStatusSettled` (`status`), `GetSpawnSettled`
  (`get`) and `ListSpawns` with `ListFilters.Settle` (`list`, whose state
  filter is the same expression, in the statement, ahead of its `LIMIT`).
  They fill `Spawn.ReportedState`, which every other read sets equal to
  `State`; `SpawnStatus`, `GetSpawn` and a `ListSpawns` with a zero
  `Settle` are unchanged. This state projection is one SELECT and never waits
  for a state to settle. Public Client reads first apply the
  [Cursor gateway checks](#cursor-gateway-and-current-launch-binding).
- **Must use:** every statement that writes `spawns.state` writes both
  settle columns in that same statement, through `hookWriteStateSet` (a
  hook's write or authenticated Cursor request admission) or
  `immediateStateSet` / `immediateSettleSet` (every other state write), never
  from a Go-side read of the row (a duplicate hook would
  restart the clock) and never with a Go clock (the statement takes
  `nowMsSQL` under its write lock). Every read that reports a state to a
  caller takes it from `SettleRead.stateExpr`, with the reader's clock taken
  before the read (a clock taken after it can report a value that never
  held). Guards read `State`, the raw column (`GetSpawn`, `GetSpawnState`,
  `SpawnState`, `ReadForReuse` or a raw `state` WHERE), never
  `ReportedState`.

**v9 columns: the row's agent, its end report and its subagent tracking (b.ssz,
b.xjn; one migration).**
Schema v9 adds three `spawns` columns after `state_changed_ms`, in this order.
They are listed once, with their exact DDL text, in `v9Columns`
(`internal/store/schema.go`), which `migrateV8toV9` walks and `schemaDDL`
repeats. None has a CHECK constraint or an index. The same hop renames
six Claude-named columns and creates the `subagents` and `subagent_launches`
tables (see [Store upgrade to agent-generic
names](#store-upgrade-to-agent-generic-names)).

| Column | Type | Written by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `agent` | TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT `''` | `InsertPending` and `ResetForReuse`, from `Spawn.Agent`; the hop's backfill | Which agent the row runs: exactly `claude`, `codex` or `cursor` (`store.AgentClaude`, `store.AgentCodex`, `store.AgentCursor`). The empty default is only what SQLite needs to add a not-null column; it is no agent, and no write relies on it: the hop sets every existing row to `claude`, and the two writes that begin a row name the agent. Spawn and reuse write the agent the call resolved (`Resolved.Agent`), and `ComposeLaunch` composes that agent's launch (see [Per-agent launch composition](#per-agent-launch-composition)). |
| `end_reported_at` | INTEGER (epoch ms), nullable | the Codex end report | When a Codex row's verified agent process reported its session's end. NULL on every row until then, and always on a Claude or Cursor row. `ApplyHookEndReport` sets it (a Codex `SessionEnd` without `agent_id`, any reason); `RecordSessionStartIdentity` clears it (a `SessionStart` from the same verified process); the life rules below keep or reset it. Read by `find-missing` and `pause`, which move a Codex row to `ended` only while it is set (`MarkEndedIfSameLife`, which leaves it set), and by the live-identity read (`LiveSpawnIdentity.EndReportedAtMillis`, with `Agent`). See [The agent-aware hook classifier](#the-agent-aware-hook-classifier). |
| `subagent_tracking` | INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 | `InsertPending`, `MoveToPending` and `ResetForReuse`, each by the launch's agent (see "The tracking flag's rules"); `RestoreAfterFailedResume` and `RestoreAfterFailedReuse`, the earlier value | Whether the settings the row's current launch was given register the agent's subagent start and stop events: 1 yes, 0 no. A Claude launch's settings register them and store 1; Codex and Cursor launches register none and store 0. So a row launched, resumed or reused by this build reads 1 if its agent is `claude` and 0 if it is `codex` or `cursor`. A row from before the v9 migration reads 0 (untracked) until its next launch write, because the hop does no backfill. Nothing else writes it. `get`, `list` and `status` do not show it. |

- **Agent write refusal.** `InsertPending` and `ResetForReuse` refuse a
  `Spawn` whose `Agent` is anything but exactly `claude`, `codex` or `cursor` (the empty
  string, another case or a padded value included) with an error wrapping
  `store.ErrRowAgentInvalid`, before any write: no row is inserted and a
  reset changes no row, archives no session and deletes no request. No other
  write takes an agent, so no other write can change a row's.
- **Raw-life rules for the two columns.** `Spawn.Agent` and
  `Spawn.EndReportedAtMillis` (0 = NULL) come back on every read that returns
  a `Spawn` (`spawnColumns`, last). `RawLife` holds both as stored, so reuse
  saves them (`ReadForReuse`) and a failed reuse puts them back
  (`RestoreAfterFailedReuse`, through `rawLifeColumns`). `ResetForReuse`
  writes the new call's agent and sets `end_reported_at` to NULL, so a reused
  row starts a launch with no end report. Resume's `MoveToPending` sets
  `end_reported_at` to NULL, and `RestoreAfterFailedResume` writes the prior
  value back (`ResumePrior.EndReportedAtMillis`). Resume keeps `agent`: it
  neither writes nor restores it.
- **The tracking flag's rules.** `Spawn.SubagentTracking` (bool, `spawnColumns`,
  last) comes back on every read that returns a `Spawn`: true only for the
  stored integer 1, false for 0 and any other stored value, so no stored value
  fails a read (`decodeSubagentTracking` in `internal/store/rowsnapshot.go`). It
  is on no `SpawnRow` or `ListRow`. The three launch writes write one rule: 1 for a `claude`
  launch, 0 for a `codex` or `cursor` launch, with nothing taken from a `Spawn` but its
  agent, including over a row that held the other value. The rule is two
  SQL expressions in `internal/store/spawns.go`, the same `CASE` over two
  sources of the agent: `subagentTrackedParamSQL` takes the agent as the
  statement's own parameter, in `InsertPending` and in `ResetForReuse`, which
  can change the row's agent; `subagentTrackedColumnSQL` reads the row's
  `agent` column, in `MoveToPending`, which keeps it. Both restores write the earlier
  launch's flag back, since that launch becomes current again: reuse saves it
  in `RawLife` (`ReadForReuse`) and `RestoreAfterFailedReuse` writes it back
  verbatim through `rawLifeColumns`; resume's caller sets
  `ResumePrior.SubagentTracking` from the `Spawn` it read (`resumePriorOf`,
  `pkg/api/resume.go`) and `RestoreAfterFailedResume` writes 1 or 0. **Must
  use:** every new write that begins a launch of a row writes
  `subagent_tracking` through `subagentTrackedParamSQL` (a statement that
  states the agent) or `subagentTrackedColumnSQL` (one that keeps it), never
  a literal, and every new restore of a failed launch writes the saved flag
  back. A future tracked agent requires a new `WHEN` in both expressions; untracked agents use the existing `ELSE 0`.
- **Reads decode it without failing.** A stored `end_reported_at` that is not
  a positive integer reads as absent (0), as `decodeEndReportedAt` in
  `internal/store/rowsnapshot.go` decides.

**v5 row types and narrow reads (b.fmk).** `store.Spawn` (and its alias
`api.Spawn`) carries the v5 columns on every read that returns a row
(`GetSpawn` and `ListSpawns` share one column list, `spawnColumns`, and one
scanner, `scanSpawn`, so both fill them identically): `RowVersion`,
`LaunchStartedAtMillis` (0 = absent), `LifeNumber`, `NoPreTrust` (the
recorded pre-trust choice), `EndedAtText` (`ended_at` exactly as stored, ""
for NULL), `Snapshot` and `Identity`, the v6 `LaunchOwner` and the v7
`IdleSince` (`""` for NULL), and the v9 `Agent`, `EndReportedAtMillis` (0
for NULL) and `SubagentTracking` (see "v9 columns" above). (It also carries `ReportedState`, b.3ie,
which is no column: see "v8 columns" above.) Two writes
take a `Spawn`: `InsertPending` and `ResetForReuse` (its `fresh` row), each
taking `LaunchStartedAtMillis`, `NoPreTrust`, `Identity.Token`,
`Identity.Socket`, `LaunchOwner` and `Agent` from it (both also write the
tracking flag by the `Spawn`'s agent, 1 for `claude` and 0 for `codex` or `cursor`, and nothing else); no write takes the other
v5 fields from one.
Reuse reads a finished row through its own narrow read, `ReadForReuse`
(`store.ReuseRow`, with the raw `store.RawLife`; see "Versioned writes"). A caller passes `Snapshot` to `MoveToPending`, and builds the `store.ResumePrior` that
`RestoreAfterFailedResume` takes from `EndedAtText`, `Identity` and the other
fields the move clears. No verb reports these fields, with two exceptions.
The launch start: `get` and `list` report `LaunchStartedAtMillis` as
`launch_started_at` on a `pending` row, and `status` reports it through
`SpawnStatus` (see "Where callers see the launch start"). The socket: `get`
reports `Identity.Socket` as `tmux_socket` on a row in any state (see "Where
the socket is shown").

- **`store.RowSnapshot`** (alias `api.RowSnapshot`) is the SR-5.3
  change-detection key: `row_version`, `started_at`, `session_id`,
  `pid`, `proc_starttime` and `tmux_session_name`, held as the stored values
  (the timestamps as stored text, selected with `CAST(col AS TEXT)`). They are
  never parsed and re-formatted. Two snapshots compare with `==`.
- **`store.LaunchIdentity`** (alias `api.LaunchIdentity`) holds the eight
  launch-identity columns: token, socket, tmux server pid/start/starttime,
  pane id/pid/starttime. A zero field means NULL. It holds handles and
  liveness evidence only. The session label, not this value, proves ownership
  of a launch.
- **SR-5.5 narrow reads.** A `launch_started_at` that is NULL, is not an
  integer, or is an integer outside the years 0 to 9999 UTC reads as absent
  (0). The range is inclusive, from `minLaunchStartedAtMillis` (the first
  millisecond of year 0) to `maxLaunchStartedAtMillis` (the last millisecond
  of year 9999), both in `internal/store/rowsnapshot.go`. A time outside it
  has no RFC3339 form, so it would fail JSON encoding. Only a hand edit can
  store such a value, and it never fails a read or a `status`, `get` or
  `list` result. A `launch_token` that is not exactly 16 lowercase hex
  characters reads as absent (""). Any `no_pre_trust` other than the integer
  0 reads as the opt-out. None of these fails a read. Every other column keeps
  its existing failure behaviour; for example, malformed `labels` or a text
  `pid` still fail the read with the same error text. A wrong storage class in
  any other v5 column (for example, a text `tmux_server_pid`) also fails the
  read, as a text `pid` does. These are new columns, so there is no earlier
  error text to keep.
- **Must use:** every read of `launch_started_at`, `launch_token` or
  `no_pre_trust` goes through the shared decoders in
  `internal/store/rowsnapshot.go` (`decodeLaunchStartedAt`,
  `decodeLaunchToken`, `decodeNoPreTrust`; each takes the column scanned into
  an `any` and never fails). The year 0 to 9999 range rule lives only in
  `decodeLaunchStartedAt`, so every consumer inherits it: `SpawnStatus`,
  `GetSpawn`/`ListSpawns` (through `scanSpawn`), `ListLiveSpawnIdentities`
  (`find-missing`'s live-row read, in `internal/store/recovery.go`) and
  `resume`'s refusal, which reads the row with `GetSpawn`. A new read
  returning a `Spawn` selects `spawnColumns` and scans with `scanSpawn`. Never
  re-derive the rules in a new read.
- **Must use:** `store.InsidePendingGrace` (in
  `internal/store/rowsnapshot.go`) is the only statement of the SR-11.2 rule:
  a `pending` row is inside its grace period while its age, measured from the
  launch start, is below the grace period. Any check of whether a `pending`
  row is inside its grace period calls it, passing the decoded launch start,
  the grace period and the caller's clock. Never re-derive the age
  arithmetic. It has two callers, both with the effective pending grace
  period (SR-13.4): `find-missing`'s step 2 (see
  [`find-missing`](#find-missing)) and the hook's SessionStart wait for its
  launch's identity write (`waitingForIdentity` in
  `internal/hook/handler.go`, which adds the no-pane condition; see [Hooks
  move a row only for its own
  agent](#hooks-move-a-row-only-for-its-own-agent)).
- **The live-row read** (SR-11.7; `internal/store/recovery.go`).
  `ListLiveSpawnIdentities` returns one `store.LiveSpawnIdentity` per row
  in a live state, `pending` included, in no set order: the instance id,
  `State`, the SessionStart identity (`PID`, `ProcStarttime`),
  `LaunchStartedAtMillis` (through `decodeLaunchStartedAt`, 0 = absent),
  `TmuxSessionName`, `LivenessNote` (`""` = NULL), `Snapshot` (the snapshot
  every guarded write of the sweep compares against), `Identity` (the
  launch identity, token through `decodeLaunchToken`) and `LaunchOwner`
  (the v6 launch owner, zero for none). Snapshot and identity are selected
  through `lifeColumns`, and the owner through `launchOwnerColumns`, as
  every read returning a `Spawn` selects them, so all three equal
  `GetSpawn`'s for the same row. No
  stored launch start, token or identity value fails the read, and the
  structured columns (`labels`, `agent_args`, `extra_env`) are never read.
  The struct grows additively.

**Versioned writes (b.fmk, SR-5.2).** The row version exists so that a later
compare-and-set write can guard on it: the write checks that the version is
still the one it read, so it knows the row has not changed since. As built:

- Every lifecycle or metadata statement that updates a `spawns` row advances
  `row_version` by exactly one in that same statement. The shared
  SET fragment is `rowVersionAdvance` in `internal/store/spawns.go`. This
  covers every branch of `ApplyHookTransition` / `ApplyHookTransitionResult`
  (state transitions, the `ended` transition, soft refreshes),
  `ApplyHookWaitingIfWorking`, `RecordSessionStartIdentity`, `SetParentID`,
  `HealJsonlPath`, the relay hook's first write `InsertRelayRequest` (its
  move to `check_permission`), the working hold's clearing of `idle_since`
  (`clearIdleSinceSQL`, only on a row that has it set and whose gate holds,
  whether the hold's read held the move or the move's own UPDATE matched
  no row), and
  `RecordLaunchIdentity`, `ReleaseLaunchOwner`, `MoveToPending`,
  `RestoreAfterFailedResume`, `ResetForReuse`'s reset,
  `RestoreAfterFailedReuse`, `EndHeldLaunch`, `AdoptIdentityIfUnchanged`
  and `find-missing`'s seven guarded writes `MarkMissingIfSameLife`, `MarkEndedIfSameLife`,
  `SetLivenessNoteIfSameLife`, `ClearLivenessIfSameLife`,
  `AdoptIdentityIfSameLife`, `NoteUnreportedIfSameLife` and
  `RepairCheckPermissionIfSameLife` (each when it applies; the clear
  advances the version whether or not a note was set). The relay's
  `permission_requests` writes (the ack, the timeout deny, `decide`'s
  verdict, `hook_gone_at`, the refused verdict, a pane answer's three
  writes, `record-pane-answer`'s record and the PostToolUse close) touch no
  `spawns` row and advance nothing; nor does the close of a Spawn's
  requests, whose `spawns` change (the mark, the ended transition, resume's
  move) advances the version once.
- Derived family-history updates through `refreshFamilies` are an exception:
  they change only `family_state`, `family_settled_state` and
  `family_changed_ms`, without advancing the row's or any ancestor's
  `row_version`. Lifecycle mutations and their family refresh share a
  transaction and commit or roll back together; see [Family reporting](#family-reporting).
- `InsertPending` starts a row at 0 (the column default). A path that writes
  nothing advances nothing. Examples are the non-Cursor `working`-transition hold path
  (a permission request holding the row, `holdsRowSQL`, at the hold's read
  or at the move's own UPDATE; a row with no `idle_since` set). Cursor
  instead performs a gated soft refresh after a rejected guarded working
  or waiting UPDATE; an applied refresh advances the version even with
  `idle_since` already NULL. Other examples are a write
  whose `WHERE` matches no row (a
  hook the gate did not apply included), and `HealJsonlPath` or any
  guarded write (`find-missing`'s seven, resume's, the end write, the
  adoption, the release of a launch's hold) when its guard misses. `DeleteSpawn` removes the row, and so
  does `expire`'s `DeleteFinishedIfSameLife` when it applies; when its
  guard misses it removes nothing and answers `CondChanged` (the row is
  live or its snapshot differs) or `CondAbsent` (no row).
- Archiving the prior session into `session_history` on a rotation does not
  advance the version by itself. The `RecordSessionStartIdentity` update it
  belongs to advances it once. The same holds for the reuse archive and the
  permission-request deletion: `ResetForReuse`'s reset UPDATE advances the
  version once for the whole change.
- The foreign-key action that clears a child's `parent_id` when its parent
  is deleted (`ON DELETE SET NULL`) does not advance the child's version.
  `parent_id` is not in `RowSnapshot`.
- Launch-start rule: every write that sets `state` to a value other than
  `pending` also sets `launch_started_at` to NULL in the same statement
  (shared fragment `launchStartClear`). These writes are the `ended`
  transition, every other hook transition whose target is not `pending`
  (`InsertRelayRequest`'s included), `MarkMissingIfSameLife`,
  `MarkEndedIfSameLife`, `RepairCheckPermissionIfSameLife`, `RestoreAfterFailedResume`,
  `RestoreAfterFailedReuse` and `EndHeldLaunch`. Every other write leaves
  `launch_started_at` unchanged (`find-missing`'s `unreported` note
  included: the row stays `pending` and keeps its launch start), except the
  three that set a launch start:
  `InsertPending` (plain spawn), `ResetForReuse` (reuse's reset) and
  `MoveToPending` (resume's move).
- Those same three writes are the ones that write `subagent_tracking` (1 for a `claude`
  launch and 0 for a `codex` one, by the one rule in "The tracking flag's
  rules"), and the two restores of a failed launch write it
  back (see "v9 columns"). No other write touches it.
- `InsertPending` writes `launch_started_at`, `launch_token`,
  `tmux_socket` and the three launch-owner columns in the INSERT (zero
  values as NULL) and never the six identity columns. The same INSERT
  records the caller's pre-trust choice: `no_pre_trust` is 1 when
  `Spawn.NoPreTrust` is true, else 0. `RecordLaunchIdentity(instanceID, launchVersion, token,
  identity)` is the one update that records a launch's six tmux server and
  pane identity columns: one UPDATE, guarded on `state = 'pending'`, the given
  `row_version` and the given `launch_token`, that NULLs the launch owner
  (it is the launch's last write, so it ends the launch's hold) and
  advances `row_version` (zero values written as NULL). When it updates nothing, one follow-up
  read tells `CondChanged` from `CondAbsent` (`store.CondResult`,
  `rowsnapshot.go`; every conditional write shares the helper
  `condNotApplied`). Only reuse's two writes touch `life_number` and
  `no_pre_trust` after the insert: the reset advances life only on an agent switch and writes its own
  call's choice; an applied restore writes the pre-reuse values back.
  The choice lasts until the next spawn or reuse, including same-agent reuse.
- The release of a launch's hold (b.kdf; `internal/store/spawns.go`,
  `releaseLaunchOwnerSQL`). `ReleaseLaunchOwner(instanceID, token)` is one
  UPDATE, guarded on `state = 'pending'`, the given `launch_token` (so it
  never touches a later launch of the row) and a recorded owner
  (`launch_owner_pid IS NOT NULL`), that NULLs the three launch-owner
  columns and advances `row_version`. It writes no other column, makes no
  tmux call and emits no trail event. Not applied: `CondChanged` (not
  `pending`, another token, or no owner) or `CondAbsent`, through
  `condNotApplied`; a driver error is returned wrapped with a zero
  `CondResult`. Its caller is `spawn.ReleaseLaunchOwner`, which makes at
  most three tries in all: it retries only a store error, sleeping 50 ms
  before the second try and 100 ms before the third, never retries a write
  that did not apply, and after the last failed try logs one WARN line
  naming the instance id and the number of tries. It never changes the
  launch's result. Every launch that recorded an owner and ends without an
  applied identity write calls it: plain spawn after a lost reply, a failed
  or timed-out create (every create failure but "duplicate session") or an
  identity write that did not apply or failed; plain spawn's held-name path
  after "duplicate session" (`endHeldRow`) when its end write
  `EndHeldLaunch` failed in the store or found the row changed or absent;
  `resume` and reuse (`finishedLaunch.releaseOwner`) after a lost reply, a
  timeout, an identity write that did not apply or failed, or a restore
  that did not apply or failed. Without it, a launch run by a long-lived
  process (the MCP server, a Go caller of `pkg/api`) would hold its row for
  as long as that process lives, and `find-missing` would never judge it.
  Residual: a release that fails on all three tries leaves that hold in
  place, so the row is not judged until its owner process exits (for
  `agent-director serve`, the end of its Claude session).
  `RestoreAfterFailedResume` does not touch the three columns, so a resume
  whose restore applied leaves its own owner on the restored `ended` or
  `missing` row; that is harmless, since the owner is read only on a
  `pending` row and the next launch overwrites it.
- Resume's writes (SR-8.3, SR-8.5; `internal/store/resume_writes.go`;
  called only by `resume`, see [Resume](#resume)). `MoveToPending` moves
  an `ended` or `missing` row whose `RowSnapshot` still equals the
  examined one to `pending`: it sets the launch start, `launch_token`, `tmux_socket`, `parent_id`, `subagent_tracking` (by the row's agent: 1 for `claude`, 0 for `codex` or `cursor`, `subagentTrackedColumnSQL`) and the launch owner (its `owner` parameter, the resuming process), and clears `pid`,
  `proc_starttime`, `ended_at`, the liveness columns, `end_reported_at` and the
  six identity columns. In the same `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction (`inImmediateTx`),
  when the move applied, it closes every request of the row that still
  awaits an answer (`closeOrphanedRequests`, reason `ended`; b.146 rule
  12), a backstop for a request left open on a row that finished before
  the ended close existed, and proves every request of the row gone
  (`agent_gone`, b.146 step 2c), so none of the earlier launch's holds
  plain `send-keys` in the new one. Last in the same transaction it closes
  the row's running subagent entries and deletes its claimable launches
  (`closeSubagentsAgentGone`, the instant the move's own `launch_started_at`;
  see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)). The move, both closes and the proof are all or nothing.
  It returns the
  version it produced. `RestoreAfterFailedResume`, guarded on `pending` at that
  version, writes a `ResumePrior` back (state, cleared columns, `end_reported_at`
  as `ResumePrior.EndReportedAtMillis`, `subagent_tracking` as
  `ResumePrior.SubagentTracking`, token,
  socket, identity; `parent_id` keeps the move's value) and clears the
  launch start; it does not reopen a request or an entry the move closed. The move
  emits one `ad.row_mutation.committed` (writer `resume`, `decision_reason`
  `ended`) per request it denied, after its commit; neither emits any other
  trail event.
- Reuse's read, change and restore (SR-10.2 to SR-10.4, SR-5.3, SR-5.6,
  SR-5.8, SR-5.9; `internal/store/reuse.go`; called only by `spawn` with
  the reuse opt-in, see [Reuse of a finished id](#reuse-of-a-finished-id)).
  None emits a trail event.
  - `ReadForReuse(id) (ReuseRow, found, error)`: the one pre-check read,
    one SELECT by primary key. `ReuseRow.Agent` is the exact stored text,
    without canonicalization; NULL or any non-text storage class reads `""`.
    The same reading (`reuseAgentTextSQL`) is used in both reset guards.
    `ReuseRow` holds `State`, `EndedAtText`
    (`ended_at` as stored text, `""` for NULL), `EndedAt` (as the driver
    parses it, the way `scanSpawn` does; nil for NULL or a value that does
    not parse), `Snapshot` and `Identity` (through `lifeColumns`, so equal
    to `GetSpawn`'s), and `Life`, a `RawLife`: every column the restore
    writes back, each selected as `typeof(col), +col` so the stored value
    and storage class come back unparsed (NULL distinct from empty, a
    zero-length blob kept a blob; `agent`, `end_reported_at` and
    `subagent_tracking` included). It
    never decodes `labels`, `agent_args` or `extra_env`, and no stored timestamp, token or
    pre-trust value fails it, so a hand-edited malformed row can be reused
    and restored byte for byte. No row: `found` false, no error.
  - `ResetForReuse(id, examined, examinedAgent, fresh) (CondResult, archivedSessionID,
    resetVersion, error)`: the change, one transaction. It encodes the
    request fields first (a failure begins nothing), then takes one
    connection from the pool and runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, so it holds the
    write lock before it reads (see the write-lock-before-read rule
    below). Its in-transaction read takes the session id, path and
    `life_number` and the identical raw-agent reading and decides, with
    `finishedStateGuardSQL`, `snapshotMatchSQL` and the `examinedAgent`
    equality guard, whether the row is still finished with the examined
    snapshot and agent: no row is `CondAbsent`, a live or changed row
    `CondChanged`, both writing nothing. Otherwise, in order: the keyed
    archive of a non-empty session id in the outgoing life through
    `upsertSessionHistoryEntry` (fail-closed; its error holds
    `ErrReuseArchive`); the reset UPDATE, still guarded and required to
    change exactly one row: state `pending`; `session_id`,
    `jsonl_path`, `pid`, `proc_starttime`, both liveness columns,
    `ended_at`, `end_reported_at` and the six server and pane identity
    columns NULL;
    `started_at` and `last_seen_at` from `fresh.StartedAt` in the store's
    layout; `launch_started_at` from `fresh.LaunchStartedAtMillis`; the
    request fields and `parent_id` from `fresh`; `no_pre_trust` from this
    call; `launch_token` and `tmux_socket` from `fresh.Identity`; the three
    launch-owner columns from `fresh.LaunchOwner` (the reusing process);
    `agent` from `fresh.Agent`, refused before anything is written, with an
    error holding `ErrRowAgentInvalid`, when it is not exactly `claude`,
    `codex` or `cursor`; `subagent_tracking` by that agent (1 for `claude`, 0 for `codex` or `cursor`, `subagentTrackedParamSQL`); `life_number` advances by one only when
    `reuseAgentTextSQL` differs exactly from `fresh.Agent` in this UPDATE;
    `row_version` + 1; then the deletion of every
    permission request of the id, decided or not; then the subagent close
    (`closeSubagentsAgentGone`: every running entry of the id turns `lost`,
    `agent_gone`, at `fresh.LaunchStartedAtMillis`, and every claimable launch
    is deleted; the entries stay; see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)); then COMMIT. Applied, it
    returns the archived session id (`""` when none) and `resetVersion`,
    the examined version + 1. Any failure rolls everything back and
    returns a wrapped error with a zero `CondResult`; only an archive
    failure holds `ErrReuseArchive`. Children keep their `parent_id`; the
    store reads no clock. Both the transactional read and UPDATE guard
    `examinedAgent` using `reuseAgentTextSQL`; an agent-only edit produces
    `CondChanged` with no committed writes. Invalid text and non-text values
    count as switches to either valid fresh agent. No trimmed or defaulted
    agent comparison may replace this rule.
  - `RestoreAfterFailedReuse(id, resetVersion, prior, failedAt)`: one
    UPDATE, guarded on `state = 'pending'` and `row_version =
    resetVersion`. It writes every `RawLife` column back exactly as
    stored (state, `life_number`, `no_pre_trust`, the session id and path,
    pid and start time, `started_at`, `last_seen_at`, the liveness
    columns, the request fields, token, socket, the six identity
    columns, the three launch-owner columns, `agent`, `end_reported_at` and `subagent_tracking`); `ended_at` as stored, or
    `failedAt` when it was NULL;
    `parent_id` only while that row still exists (else NULL, decided in
    the same statement, so the foreign key never fails it); clears
    `launch_started_at`; advances `row_version`. It never touches
    `session_history` (the archived entry stays), `permission_requests`
    (the deleted requests stay deleted), a subagent entry or a claimable
    launch (the entries the reset closed stay closed). A zero `RawLife`, or one whose
    state is not finished, is refused with an error and nothing written.
    Not applied: `CondChanged` or `CondAbsent` through `condNotApplied`; a
    store failure: a wrapped error, the row left as the reset left it.
  - **The fail-closed archive versus the fail-open rotation archive.** Both
    write through `upsertSessionHistoryEntry`. A rotation archive failure
    never blocks the agent's SessionStart; a reuse archive failure stops the
    whole change, because a reset that lost the old session's entry would
    orphan its transcript.
  - **Must use:** `ErrReuseArchive` (`internal/store/spawns.go`) is the one
    marker of a failed reuse archive. It is not a catalogued sentinel and
    is never aliased in `pkg/api`; a caller tells an archive failure apart
    only with `errors.Is` (as `reuseChangeError` does), never by text.
  - **Must use: the write lock before the read.** A store write that must
    read and change a row with no other writer in between, and must never
    fail because another process committed after its read began, takes
    one connection with `s.db.Conn`, runs `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` on it, runs
    every statement on that connection (helpers that take a `querier` get
    the `connQuerier` adapter, `internal/store/session_history.go`), never
    goes through the pool inside it (the pool has one connection and would
    wait for itself), and rolls back with `rollbackConn`, which discards a
    connection whose ROLLBACK failed so a stuck transaction never returns
    to the pool. `ResetForReuse` and `MarkMissingIfSameLife` (find-missing's
    mark with its close of the row's open permission requests, b.kdf) are
    the pattern's users, and so is every bounded write below.
    `inImmediateTx(fn)` (`internal/store/lockwait.go`) is the pattern as one
    helper for a write that waits the store's own busy timeout: one
    connection, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, `fn` on that connection, `COMMIT`, and a
    rollback through `rollbackConn` when `fn` or the commit fails. Unlike
    `inWriteTx`, a lock not taken in time is the driver's busy error, an
    unnamed store failure, never `ErrStoreBusy`, so it serves a write whose
    verb names no `ErrStoreBusy`. Its users are the hook's ended transition
    (`applyEndedTransition`) and resume's `MoveToPending`. **Must use:** a
    new write of that kind goes through `inImmediateTx`, never a hand-made
    `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`.
  - **Must use: the close of a Spawn's requests (b.146 rule 12).**
    `closeOrphanedRequests(ctx, conn, instanceID, reason, at)`
    (`internal/store/request_close.go`) closes every request of a row that
    still awaits an answer, plus decided unacked pre-v7 requests without
    a completed pane answer, on the caller's connection, inside the
    transaction the caller holds: first `denyOrphanedRequestsSQL` denies
    each undecided one (`decision` `deny`, `decision_reason` `reason`,
    `decided_at`, `closed_at`), then `closeDecidedRequestsSQL` sets only
    `closed_at` on each decided, unacked request with `pane_answer` `none`
    or `intent` and no prior close (including pre-v7), then
    `proveAgentGoneSQL` proves every request of a non-Cursor row not yet proven
    gone, closed now or before (`proven_gone_at`, `proven_gone_how`
    `agent_gone`; b.146 step 2c), one instant `at` for all three, in
    milliseconds, which the caller reads from the store's clock
    (`storeNowMillis`) inside its transaction. The proof statement checks the
    actual row with `agent IS NOT 'cursor'` in that transaction; NULL-agent
    legacy rows retain this proof. Cursor requests retain their proof state,
    including existing exact-request execution proof and unproven delivery
    acknowledgements. Gateway/runtime death or terminal SessionEnd supplies no
    Cursor request proof. Row closure, request deny/close and subagent cleanup
    remain atomic. It returns
    what it closed in request-id order and
    emits nothing; the caller emits once its transaction commits, through
    `closedRequest.emitDeny` (one `ad.row_mutation.committed` per denied
    request, with the caller's writer). Its four callers run it in the
    transaction of the write that ends the asking agent's launch:
    `MarkMissingIfSameLife` (reason `find_missing`, writer `find_missing`),
    `MarkEndedIfSameLife` (reason `ended`, writer `find_missing`), the
    hook's ended transition (reason `ended`, writer `hook`) and
    `MoveToPending` (reason `ended`, writer `resume`). (Reuse's reset
    deletes the row's requests instead.) A new write that ends a row's
    launch and keeps its requests closes them through it, never with
    statements of its own. The ended write, the mark and the Codex move pass the same `at` to
    the close of the row's subagent entries (see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)).
  - **Must use: a bounded write for a caller with a deadline (b.146).** A
    store write whose caller must keep a deadline whatever `[store]
    busy_timeout_ms` is runs through `inWriteTx(maxWait, fn)`
    (`internal/store/lockwait.go`): one `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction on
    the store's one connection, taken through `boundedConnContext`.
    **Must use:** `Store.WithContext(ctx)` scopes an immutable per-call
    handle to the original caller context, sharing the pool and cleanup lane;
    it does not own the pool and must not be closed independently. Duration
    methods intersect their local allowance with this context through
    `operationContext`; a later relative wait cannot renew an expired
    original deadline. Acquisition, setup PRAGMA, BEGIN, queries, COMMIT,
    rollback and timeout restoration retain the operation context.
    Deadline-bounded SQL disables SQLite's busy handler (`busy_timeout = 0`);
    `retryBusy` supplies cancellable Go retries for reads and BEGIN, capped
    by both the available busy allowance and the context. Callbacks use only
    their leased connection, never the one-connection pool.

    Zero wait takes a free connection or operation slot however late a
    scheduling stall lets the call reach it, and waits `connGrab` (1 ms) only
    for one another call holds, counted from when that wait starts (b.q5r).
    **Must use:** `connGrabContext` (`lockwait.go`, which names the
    database/sql behaviour it relies on) and `admitOperation`
    (`connection_cleanup.go`); never pre-arm a `connGrab` timeout. Accepted
    residue: a connection holder releasing just as `connGrab` runs out can
    still yield `ErrStoreBusy` (database/sql's random select). Zero wait has
    zero SQLite lock allowance and no retries. Immediately available
    execution and cleanup get one fixed `immediateWorkBudget` (1 s),
    intersected with any enclosing original deadline. An expired positive
    call cannot start SQL through a renewed zero-wait allowance.
    `DefaultLockWait` (negative) retains the store's configured waits unless
    an enclosing context cuts them shorter.
    Setup context cancellation before BEGIN and precommit exhaustion wrap
    `ErrStoreBusy`; no COMMIT is attempted after precommit expiry. A caller
    context that ends an operation before its first statement (a
