`HandleConfig.Clock` and reads time only through `HandleConfig.Now`, never
`time.Sleep` or `time.Now`, and decides "inside the grace period" only
through `store.InsidePendingGrace`. The relay poll (`Poll` in
`internal/hook/polling.go`) also waits on the store but keeps its own seams:
it sleeps on its `PollClock` and reads its deadline through `nowFunc`
(`time.Now`). Tests drive the SessionStart wait with a virtual clock whose
`Sleep` advances `Now` (`hookConfig` in
`internal/hook/hook_parent_fakes_test.go` wires one, with the default grace,
by default). The wait has one budget, fixed when it begins:
min(grace bound − `Now` at the start, `sessionStartWaitCap`).

- **Elapsed time comes from `HandleConfig.Now`.** The cap is measured as
  `Now` at each turn minus `Now` at the start (`capEnd` is the start
  reading plus the cap). `runHook` wires `time.Now` as is, whose readings
  carry Go's monotonic clock reading, so that difference is monotonic and
  no wall-clock step moves it; production wiring must keep that reading
  and never pass `Now`'s value through `.UTC`, `.Local`, `.Round(0)`, `.Truncate`
  or `.In`, which strip it. In tests the difference of two virtual-clock
  readings is the virtual elapsed time, whether the clock was seeded with
  `time.Now()` (`hookConfig`) or with `time.UnixMilli` (the wait tests'
  `runSessionStartWait`), since `Sleep` advances both readings alike.
- **The grace bound is wall clock.** It comes from `time.UnixMilli` (the
  launch start plus the grace), which carries no monotonic reading, so
  `bound.Sub(Now())` and `store.InsidePendingGrace` compare wall-clock
  times.
- **The re-read cap** is ⌊budget / 250 ms⌋ + 1 re-reads. With a clock that
  advances steadily it never binds; it is the guard against a `Now` that
  never advances (a frozen test clock), which would otherwise never reach
  either bound.
- **Clock steps.** A launch start in the future, or a wall-clock step back
  before the wait begins, moves the grace bound later but not the cap, so
  the wait ends at the cap at the latest (a launch start 10 s in the future
  with a 60 s grace ends the wait at the grace bound, after 70 s). A step back during the wait makes the grace bound
  report more time left; the wait then ends at whichever comes first, the
  re-read cap (about the time left at its start) or the cap.

**SessionStart is one statement.** An applied SessionStart sets
`waiting` whatever the prior state and, in the same UPDATE, records the
payload's session id and transcript path (presence rule), `pid` and
`proc_starttime` = the hook's parent (the pane process), `pane_starttime`
when NULL, bumps `last_seen_at`, clears `ended_at`, the liveness notes
and `launch_started_at`, and advances `row_version` once. The rotation
archive runs inside the same transaction, only when the write applied
(see [SessionStart hook side of the
contract](#sessionstart-hook-side-of-the-contract)).

**Must use:** every store write a hook makes takes the hook's
`store.HookGate`, puts `hookGateSQL` (with `hookGateArgs`) in its own
statement (an UPDATE also carries `hookPaneStartSet` in its SET), and
reports
`store.HookApplied`, with the not-applied reason from `notAppliedReason`
(`internal/store/hook_gate.go`). No ungated hook write exists in
production code; never add one, and never check the gate in a separate
read before the write. The subagent entry and claimable-launch writes are
hook writes too: each statement carries the gate and the row conditions
itself (see [Subagent capture](#subagent-capture)). An ordinary hook records the session id only
through `hookSessionRecordSet`; a hook whose payload carries `agent_id`
passes an empty session id in its `store.HookGate` (and an empty
transcript path), so that fragment records nothing. The `ad.hook.ignored`
reason constants (`store.HookReasonPIDMismatch`,
`store.HookReasonNoPaneRecorded`, `store.HookReasonSubagentEvent`,
`store.HookReasonNoExecForm`) live together in
`internal/store/hook_gate.go`; a new reason goes beside them. Every
`ad.hook.ignored` record's SR-14 fields come from the one builder
`ignoredFields` (`internal/hook/gate.go`), which `emitIgnored` (hook
path, then filling `row_session_id` / `row_pane_pid` from its row read)
and `emitNoExecForm` (no-verb path, row fields null) both use; never
build those fields elsewhere.

**Pane is the hook's grandparent (b.9n6, b.zde).** A `claude` on PATH
that runs Claude Code as a child instead of exec-ing it (a `codex` that is
npm's node launcher or a wrapper that does not `exec` is the same case)
makes the pane process the launcher, so SR-22.9 refuses every hook of the agent with
`pid_mismatch` and the row stays `pending`. A hook run through a shell
instead of in exec form has the same structure; the two are not told
apart. Only for a SessionStart refused with `pid_mismatch` whose one row
read found the row `pending` does `emitIgnored`, after writing
`ad.hook.ignored`, read the parent's own parent pid, once
(`paneIsGrandparent`, through `HandleConfig.ParentProc.PPID`, the
[parent-pid reader](#parent-pid-reader-parentpidreader-ppidgo)); no other
hook reads it. When it is the row's `pane_pid`, `emitPaneIsGrandparent`
reads the pane process's command name and writes one
`ad.hook.pane_is_grandparent` (see [`ad.*` event
namespace](#ad-event-namespace)). The event claims only that structure;
its `advice` (`paneIsGrandparentAdviceFor`, chosen by the row's `agent`,
not by the hook's argument) names both causes, asserts neither, and never
advises ending a session by hand. A Claude row's advice also names `[launch]
claude_path`; a Codex row's names the `codex` program, the launcher case
(the node launcher npm installs) and `[launch] codex_path`. Fail-open: an
unreadable parent pid writes no record, an unreadable command name
leaves `pane_command` null, and the gate's decision, the row, stdout and
exit stay those of any ignored hook. Neither read is evidence.

**A Codex hook's parent.** The gate is agent-blind: it compares the hook's
parent with the row's pane process, whichever agent the row has. Codex runs
each hook as `<shell> -c <command>`, where the shell is the account's login
shell when that is bash or zsh and bash for any other (dash, fish); it ignores
`$SHELL` and starts no login shell. The command of a Codex hook entry begins
with `exec`, so the hook replaces the shell and its parent is the Codex
process, the pane process of a direct launch. A command without `exec` leaves
the shell as the parent and Codex as the grandparent, which is the
`pane_is_grandparent` case. A shell startup file that prints on stdout (zsh's
`.zshenv`, the file `BASH_ENV` names for bash) puts text ahead of the hook's
own stdout; the gate and the writes do not read it. A marked Codex hook (a
non-empty `agent_id`) follows the Claude rules: a `SessionStart` or
`SessionEnd` is ignored as `subagent_event` before the gate, and any other
applies its table row, records no session id or path, and writes no subagent
entry (subagent capture is Claude only).

**No resolver, no tmux for Claude/Codex.** `internal/hook` imports neither
`internal/tmux` nor `internal/probe`. Claude/Codex hooks make no tmux
call and walk no process ancestry. Its only reads past the parent are
`ad.hook.pane_is_grandparent`'s, above; they report and never decide. A
slow or wedged tmux never delays a Claude/Codex hook. Cursor admission
uses the CLI-injected `VerifyCursor` callback (`hookCursorVerifier`), which
checks the runtime, protected transcript and pane through `VerifyPane`;
that pane verification can call tmux within its configured bounds. Adopting the
pane of a row whose create reply was lost is never a hook's job (SR-3.6
gives it to `kill`, `send-keys`, `pause` and `find-missing`).

**What it rejects and keeps.** A nested `claude` started in the agent's
shell (its hooks' parent is the nested process), a teammate pane split in
the agent's session (its own main process), a leftover of an earlier
life and any stray process that inherited `AGENT_DIRECTOR_INSTANCE_ID`
are all ignored, for every event, SessionStart included. `/clear`,
`/resume` and compaction inside the agent's own process are applied,
because the process is the same, and SessionStart records the new session
id. An `ended` row stays `ended` against every other process's hooks:
only the row's own agent, or a verb such as `resume`, moves it again. The
ended transition therefore comes only from the row's own agent (or from
agent-director's own writes). A subagent's or in-process teammate's
SessionStart and SessionEnd (`agent_id`) are rejected too, even from the
pane process; its other hooks are kept but record no session id.

**Residuals (SR-18.12).** A nested `claude`'s and a teammate pane's hooks
are ignored, so their work is not reflected in the row. A row whose
create reply was lost takes no hook, and stays `pending`, until a verb
adopts its pane by `@ad_pane` (SR-3.6: `kill`, and `send-keys` with
`allow_pending`, through `adoptIdentity`, and `find-missing`, once the row
is past its pending grace period, through `adoptInSweep`; `read-pane` uses
the pane for its call only and writes nothing). Its SessionStart waits to the bound and, unless the
pane is adopted meanwhile, is ignored as `no_pane_recorded`, so after a
later adoption an idle agent's row stays `pending` until the agent's
next hook; `find-missing`, past the grace period, notes it `unreported`
so a caller that reads the pane can act on it (the lost-reply residual,
reported by the sweep; b.kdf). The SessionStart wait bounds the
race with the identity write by the pending grace period and by the
540 s cap, so an identity write slower than that period, or than 540 s,
leaves the row `pending` the same way (residual (ii); TLA+
`ci_H_Lrep_slow`), until the agent's next hook, noted `unreported` by
`find-missing` meanwhile. The wait ends at the earlier of its grace bound and 540 s
after it began, before the `"timeout": 600` its hook entry states,
whatever the grace or a clock step does (WD 2026-09-30c); the hook's store
writes around the wait can still outlast that timeout and get it killed
with no record (see "The cap and the hook timeout" above). With a grace
above 540 s, SessionStart stops waiting at 540 s while `find-missing`
still counts the row as inside its grace period; the row stays `pending`
until the agent's next hook (noted `unreported` by `find-missing` once
the grace period has passed), as in residual (ii), with its
`no_pane_recorded` record. A launch
start later than the hook's clock (a wall-clock step back, or clocks
that disagree) likewise keeps `find-missing` counting the row as inside
the grace period; the hook's wait still ends by the cap at the latest. While a SessionStart waits, the agent's first response
waits too, since Claude Code waits on SessionStart hooks. A Claude Code
version that does not run exec-form hooks (Claude Code 2.1.120, the
Docker pin, is one) never applies a hook, so its rows stay `pending`
until `kill` or until `find-missing` marks them `missing`, noted
`unreported` by `find-missing` while the agent runs (no hook of theirs
clears the note); each of its hooks writes
`ad.hook.ignored` `no_exec_form`, so the trail says why (RN-9; the
README states the minimum version). A `claude` on PATH that runs Claude
Code as a child instead of exec-ing it likewise never applies a hook, and
its rows stay `pending`, noted `unreported` the same way once
`find-missing` finds the launcher (the pane process) running; each refused SessionStart writes
`ad.hook.pane_is_grandparent` (see above; the README states the
prerequisite). Subagents' and in-process teammates'
tool and permission events move the row's state and use its relay, so a
row can read `working` while only they work: the row reflects the
process. Claude Code and Codex hooks follow this process gate (see
[The agent-aware hook classifier](#the-agent-aware-hook-classifier)). Cursor
is also supported through its authenticated ACP runtime and lifecycle gate;
validated permissions and blocking plans use the
[Cursor authorization controller](#cursor-authorization-dataflow-and-authority).
Questions and unsupported or policy-rejected authorization remain denied or
cancelled before admission. `respawn-pane` of the agent's pane changes the
pane pid, so
the agent's hooks are then ignored, visibly.

### Subagent capture

Registering `SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` and reading the Agent tool's
hooks puts a subagent's own entry in the store as the hooks arrive. The store
half is agent-neutral; the payload half is Claude Code's. The tables are
described under [`internal/store`](#internalstore) (`subagents`,
`subagent_launches`); this section does not restate them. Nothing here shows
an entry to a caller; the one verb that does is `list-subagents` (see [The
`list-subagents` verb](#the-list-subagents-verb)).

**Where the line is.** `internal/store` (`subagent_hook_writes.go`,
`subagent_writes.go`) takes agent-neutral events (`SubagentLifecycleEvent`,
`SubagentLaunchRequest`, `SubagentLaunchDetails`, `SubagentLaunchFailure`,
`SubagentTurnEnd` with its `SubagentSnapshot` of `SubagentListed` ids, and a stop's
`Listing` of the same) and applies them; it reads no clock, no payload and no
config. `internal/hook/subagent.go` is the Claude Code side: it names the
events and the `Agent` tool (`EventNameSubagentStart`, `EventNameSubagentStop`,
`ToolAgent`), reads the payload fields (`readSubagentFields`) and the
`background_tasks` list (`readBackgroundTasks`), and maps them onto the store's
events. The store applies these agent-neutral events without parsing an
agent's payloads.

**Capture is Claude only.** `internal/hook` takes the capture path
only for a result whose `SubagentCapture` flag is set, and the classifier sets
it for Claude's table alone (see [The agent-aware hook
classifier](#the-agent-aware-hook-classifier)): `isSubagentLifecycle`,
`isAgentToolHook` and `isMainAgentStop` each require it. A Codex hook, a
`SubagentStart` and `SubagentStop` included, makes its ordinary gated write (a
soft refresh for those two) and no entry transaction, and a Codex `Stop` makes
no turn-end transaction. Independently, each store entry write requires the
row's `subagent_tracking` to be 1 (see "The gate" below). A Codex launch
stores 0, so even a hand-registered hook classified as Claude cannot write
its records. Conversely, Codex's classifier disables capture even for a
seeded row whose tracking flag is 1. These guards do not change the ordinary
gated row write or the permission relay: a Codex `SubagentStart` or
`SubagentStop` soft-refreshes the row and proves no request gone.

**The three transactions.**

- **`ApplySubagentLifecycle`** (`SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`): one
  `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` (`inImmediateTx`) holding the gated soft refresh and, when
  the event names a subagent (`agent_id`), its entry writes. The soft refresh is
  `gatedHookUpdate` with `hookGateSQL` in its own `WHERE`: the state stays,
  `last_seen_at` is bumped, `row_version` advances by 1, the liveness markers
  clear, and `idle_since` and the settle columns are untouched. It records no
  session id when `agent_id` is present (the gate carries none). Without an
  `agent_id` it is the soft refresh alone, with no entry write and no claim.
  When the row write matches no row (the gate did not hold) the transaction
  rolls back and the outcome is `no_change` with the not-applied reason; any
  other failure, an entry write's or a busy store's, rolls the whole
  transaction back (the row as it was) and the outcome is `error`. One
  `ad.spawn.state_transition` (`soft_refresh` true, prior state to itself) is
  emitted after the commit; the entry writes emit none. A `SubagentStop`'s
  entry writes are two steps in this order: the stop (`stopEntry`), then its
  listing (`applyListed` without create). The listing runs whatever the stop did
  (it may have changed nothing, or found an entry of an earlier launch), only
  when the row write applied and `SubagentID` is not empty; the hook passes a
  listing only for a `SubagentStop` that carries an `agent_id`.
- **`ApplySubagentAfterWrite`**: its own `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, for the Agent
  tool's `PreToolUse` (a launch request), `PostToolUse` (a launch result),
  `PostToolUseFailure` (a launch failure) and a main-agent `Stop` (the turn
  end, with its snapshot). `Handle` runs it only after the hook's own row write applied (a held
  `working` transition counts as applied) and never checks that itself. It
  writes no trail record. A failure rolls it back, logs one line
  (`hook: subagent entry transaction (instance=…, event=…): <error>`; no payload
  string) and changes nothing else: `ad.hook.fired`'s `upsert_outcome` stays the
  row write's, and stdout stays empty.
- **`SubagentTurnEndHasWork(instanceID, SubagentTurnEnd)`**: a plain read, no
  write lock, that never writes, behind the main-agent `Stop`'s skip. It takes
  the whole turn end, snapshot included, and the transaction runs when any of
  three holds: the snapshot lists a subagent (after the cut; it answers true
  before reading the row); there is a snapshot (an empty one counts) and the
  current launch has a `running` background entry opened more than
  `SubagentGraceMs` before the Stop; the current launch has a claimable launch
  opened more than `SubagentGraceMs` before it. A `Stop` with no snapshot ignores
  background entries. Otherwise a `Stop` costs no extra write, and a skip only
  defers a close to a later `Stop`.

**The gate.** Every statement of these three transactions that creates, changes
or deletes an entry or a claimable launch carries `hookGateSQL` and four row conditions in its own
`WHERE`: the row's state is not `ended` or `missing`, its `subagent_tracking` is
1, its `launch_token` is not NULL (`subagentRowGateSQL`; `subagentGateExists`
for an update or delete), and the current launch is decided by the row's
`launch_token` read in that same statement: a create or a move targets only
it, and a stop or a claim acts only on an entry or claimable launch whose own
`launch_token` equals it. The cap evictions are gated the same way
(`evictSubagentEntryGated`, `evictSubagentLaunchGated`), and an insert that
inserts nothing after an eviction or a claim rolls the transaction back
(`errSubagentWriteRefused`), so an eviction or a claim never stands without its
insert. The read that picks a transition (`readEntry`, the row's launch token)
runs inside the transaction after its write lock, and decides which transition
applies only; each write re-reads the launch token in its own statement. A hook
of another process, or of a row that is not live, writes nothing.

**The transitions** (in `subagent_writes.go`; `SubagentLifecycleEvent.cut` and
the other `cut` methods apply `CutSubagentString`, 1 KiB cut at a character
boundary, to every payload-derived string on entry, so a caller cuts nothing):

Every entry lookup uses `readEntry` (`subagent_writes.go`), which requires the
entry's `life_number` to equal its owning row's current life. An id present
only in an earlier life therefore takes the no-entry branch below: creating
events insert a separate entry, while no-create events leave it untouched.
Existing entries can move between launches only within their immutable life.
**Must use:** entry transition writers use this current-life lookup and the
shared `insertEntry`/`writeEntry` helpers; no second lookup, insert or life update.

- **Entries and claimable launches.** An entry is a record (`confirmed` 1) once
  a claim, a launch result or a snapshot or listing confirms it, and an observation (`confirmed` 0)
  until then. A claimable launch is opened by the Agent tool's `PreToolUse`
  (`launchRequest`: it needs a `tool_use_id` and a type, and the type is
  `tool_input.subagent_type`; a call that carries `tool_input.name` opens none,
  which is how a teammate launch is told apart; a `tool_use_id` already open or
  already on an entry of the current launch changes nothing), and closed by the
  launch result (`closeLaunch`), by `PostToolUseFailure` (`launchFailure`), or by
  a main-agent `Stop` once it is more than `SubagentGraceMs` (2000) old
  (`turnEnd`). The Stop's close is of the current launch's claimable launches
  only; an earlier launch's are already gone, deleted by the liveness close
  (see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)).
- **Snapshot** (`turnEnd`, after the claimable-launch close, in the same
  transaction; only when the `Stop` has a snapshot): the listed ids are applied
  by `applyListed` with create, then `closeAbsent` runs.
  - *Create*: a listed id with no current-life entry gets a confirmed,
    `running` entry of the current launch, `run_mode` `background`, the listing's
    type (NULL when it gave none) and the Stop's session id, `opened_at` and
    `activity_at` at the receipt time; every other field is NULL. The gated entry
    cap eviction runs first, as for any create.
  - *Fill and confirm*: a listed id with a current-life entry of any launch is
    confirmed,
    moved into the current launch, and a NULL `run_mode` becomes `background`
    (never overwritten). State, times, type and description are never touched, so
    it never reopens a `stopped` or `lost` entry. `activity_at` is set only when
    something changed (`writeEntry`), so a listing that changes nothing writes
    nothing.
  - *Close* (`closeAbsent`): every entry of the current launch that is `running`,
    `run_mode` `background`, not listed, and has `opened_at` more than
    `SubagentGraceMs` before the receipt time becomes `lost` with
    `close_reason` `absent_from_snapshot` and `lost_at` and `activity_at` at the
    receipt time. An entry opened exactly the grace before is kept. The
    candidates are read first, and each is closed by its own gated `UPDATE` that
    re-checks every condition. There is no session or nesting filter, and a
    foreground or NULL-mode entry, a `stopped` or `lost` one and another launch's
    are untouched. The close is skipped when the row has no `launch_token`.
  - A `Stop` with no snapshot creates and closes nothing; its claimable-launch
    close still runs.
- **A SubagentStop's listing** (`stop`): the stop first (`stopEntry`), then
  `applyListed` without create: listed ids with an entry are confirmed, moved and
  filled as above, and nothing is created, closed or reopened.
- **Start** (`start`): a start with no entry creates one `running`, with the
  type from `agent_type` and the session id of the event, and, when it has a
  type, claims the oldest open claimable launch of that type (opened_at, then
  `created_seq`) in the current launch. The claim only confirms; it fills no
  field. A start with no type never claims and makes an untyped observation. A
  start with an entry already restarts it into the current launch.
- **Stop** (`stop`): acts only on an entry of the current launch. A `running`
  or `lost` entry becomes `stopped` with `stopped_at` and the `stop_event`
  reason; a `stopped` entry's `stopped_at` is replaced only when the payload says
  an earlier stop was blocked (`stop_hook_active`) or the time came from a
  details source. A stop with no entry creates none.
- **Launch result** (`launchDetails`): `status` `async_launched` is a background
  start and `completed` a foreground stop; any other status creates no entry
  and only closes its claimable launch. The type is `tool_input.subagent_type`,
  else a completed result's `agentType`. The parent is the payload's `agent_id`
  (the launching subagent) or, with none, the agent itself. The result creates
  the entry as a record, or confirms an existing one.
- **Source precedence** (`applyRanked`, `applyFirst`): a field with more than
  one source takes the higher (type: start over details over snapshot; run
  mode: details over snapshot; `stopped_at`: stop over details) and a source
  never replaces its own value; a field with one source keeps its first value.
  The snapshot or listing is the `snapshot` source (`SubagentSourceSnapshot`,
  the lowest): it sets `subagent_type` only when it creates the entry and
  `run_mode` `background` only while it is NULL, so a launch result's run mode
  outranks it. It never sets a description. An event that changes nothing writes
  nothing, `activity_at` included. A confirmation is a claim, a launch result or
  a snapshot or listing.

**Receipt time.** The store reads no clock for these events: each carries its
receipt time in integer milliseconds, `HandleConfig.Start` (the hook process's first
clock reading) as `start.UnixMilli()`. `SubagentGraceMs` is the one grace,
shared by the claimable-launch close, the snapshot's close and the skip read.

**The fields the hook reads.** `readSubagentFields` reads a field only as
supplied: present, not null, of the type it is read as and, for a string, not
empty, and `tool_input` and `tool_response` only when they are objects. A field
of the wrong type is not supplied and fails nothing (SR-5.1). It never reads the
value of `tool_input.name` (only whether it is supplied), the content fields, an
error, counters, `outputFile`, `tool_response.agent_id` or the cron list; none
reaches the store or a log line.

`readBackgroundTasks` reads a `Stop`'s or `SubagentStop`'s `background_tasks`
(a `SubagentStart`'s is not read). An absent, null or non-array field is no
snapshot (`nil`); any array, an empty one included, is a snapshot. Each element
is decoded in two passes. The first decodes into `backgroundTaskHead`, which has
only a `type` field: an element that is not an object, or whose `type` is not
`subagent`, is ignored, and nothing but its `type` was decoded. Only a
`subagent` element goes to the second pass, into `backgroundTaskSubagentFields`
(`status`, `id` and `agent_type`, all raw values). Neither struct has a
description field, so none is ever held. The element lists a subagent only when
`status` is `running` and `id` is a non-empty string; only then is `agent_type`
used (empty when missing or not a string). The store then cuts the
listed id and type to 1 KiB and drops an empty id (`cutListed`), and repeated
ids are deduplicated after the cut, the first in array order, whose type types a
created entry. A main-agent `Stop`'s snapshot carries the `Stop`'s own session id
(read leniently); a `SubagentStop` with no `agent_id` carries no listing.

**Extra `row_version` advances.** Each applied `SubagentStart` and
`SubagentStop` soft refresh advances `row_version` by one, as every applied
hook write does, so one run of a subagent adds two advances. The entry writes
advance nothing of their own. A snapshot-guarded write that one of them
overtakes is refused as changed (`row_version` is part of the snapshot match)
and handled as when any other hook overtakes it: `SessionStart`'s identity
write re-reads the row and retries once; find-missing's guarded writes
(`markMissingSameLife` and the other sweep writes) apply nothing and leave the
row to the next run; expire's delete (`DeleteFinishedIfSameLife`) keeps the row
as `changed_since_examined`, so the next run examines it again.

**Teammates and internal agents.** A teammate's launch request names the
teammate and so opens no claimable launch, and its result names no subagent,
so a teammate confirms nothing; an internal agent's `SubagentStop` finds no
entry, so an internal agent (Claude Code's own, for one) gets no record. A
start either fires can leave an observation, which stays one. The one way a
teammate shows as a record is a claim: a teammate whose type equals that of an
open claimable launch (a running launch of the same type) claims it with the
start that creates its entry, and so confirms its entry. The wrong match is
accepted; a claim fills no field (`TestSubagentClaimTeammate`).

**What it does not do.** The snapshot closes only background entries of the
current launch, so a foreground or unknown-mode entry stays `running` until its
own stop or the liveness close of its row (see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)). Only
the two caps of 300 remove an entry or a claimable launch, besides a claim, a
launch result, the main agent's `Stop`, the snapshot's close and the liveness
close's deletion of the row's claimable launches.

**Fail-open.** Every failure here exits 0 with empty stdout and one
content-free log line. A `SubagentStart` or `SubagentStop` write failure goes
through `failClosed`, which is silent for every event but `PermissionRequest`,
with `upsert_outcome` `error`. A background entry whose `SubagentStop` was
dropped is repaired by a later snapshot that does not list it. Each transaction waits at most one `[store]
busy_timeout_ms` for the write lock and the hook adds no sleep or poll. A
payload over 1 MiB is dropped whole before any of this.

**Must use:**

- **Subagent store writes.** A hook's entry or claimable-launch write goes
  through `ApplySubagentLifecycle` or `ApplySubagentAfterWrite`, never a
  statement of its own (the liveness close, which is not a hook write, is the
  one ungated writer; see [The liveness close of subagent entries](#the-liveness-close-of-subagent-entries)). A new statement that creates, changes or
  deletes an entry or a claimable launch carries the gate in its own `WHERE`
  (`subagentGateExists`, or `subagentRowGateSQL` in an insert-select), reads
  its deciding row inside the transaction after the write lock, and an eviction
  it needs is `evictSubagentEntryGated` / `evictSubagentLaunchGated`, never an
  eviction of its own. A new event is a new field of `SubagentAfterWrite`, not a new
  transaction.
- **Snapshot and listing store inputs.** A main-agent `Stop`'s `background_tasks`
  reaches the store only as `SubagentTurnEnd.Snapshot` (`SubagentSnapshot`: the
  Stop's session id and `[]SubagentListed`; nil is no snapshot, non-nil with an
  empty `Listed` is a snapshot that can close), and a `SubagentStop`'s only as
  `SubagentLifecycleEvent.Listing`. `SubagentListed` holds an id and a type and
  has no description field, and a new input must not add one. A new create,
  confirm, fill or close from a listing goes through `applyListed` or
  `closeAbsent` (`subagent_writes.go`), never a statement of its own, and a
  per-entry close re-checks every condition in its own gated `UPDATE`.
- **The soft refresh.** `ApplySubagentLifecycle` is the only soft refresh that
  runs in a transaction with other writes; a new hook that needs one uses
  `gatedHookUpdate` there, never a refresh of its own, and keeps its
  `idle_since`-free `SET`.
- **The `background_tasks` reader.** A hook reads a `background_tasks` list only
  through `readBackgroundTasks` (`internal/hook/subagent.go`), which applies
  "supplied" to every field and decodes only `backgroundTaskHead` (the `type`)
  and, for a subagent element, `backgroundTaskSubagentFields`; a field it does
  not name is never read, and a description never. A new field read from an
  entry is added to one of those structs (a field of a non-subagent element
  stays unread) and to the reader, with a wrong type meaning not supplied.
- **The event helpers.** A payload field the subagent feature reads is read
  through `readSubagentFields` (`rawObject`, `rawString`, `rawBool` for a
  new one: a wrong type is not supplied), and every string headed for an
  entry is cut by the store (`CutSubagentString`), never in the hook. The
  receipt time is `HandleConfig.Start`; no store function reads a clock.
- **The store's optional interfaces.** `subagentLifecycleWriter`,
  `subagentAfterWriter` and `subagentTurnEndReader` are optional extensions of
  `HookStore`: a test double that has none gets today's write. A change to what
  decides a `Stop`'s skip is made in `SubagentTurnEndHasWork` (it takes the whole
  `SubagentTurnEnd`) and in no caller; every call site passes the turn end it
  would apply.
- **The grace.** `SubagentGraceMs` (2000) is the one grace of every close by age;
  no close uses another number, and a close is by "more than" it, never "at
  least".
- **Hook payload fixtures.** A captured payload for a subagent or Agent-tool
  event goes in `internal/hook/testdata/hook-payloads/` and has a row in the
  `payloadFixtures` table of `hook_payload_fixtures_test.go`
  (`TestPayloadFixtureEventsMatchRegistered` fails on a file with none, and on a registered event with no fixture), never inline.
  The table's first column is the row's agent: a Codex payload goes in
  `internal/hook/testdata/codex-hook-payloads/` with the agent `codex`, and a
  test names it `codex/<file>` to `readPayloadFixture` (`fixtureName` builds
  the name from the agent column, since a Codex file may share a name with a
  Claude one). A Codex fixture is a real capture with home paths and every id
  replaced by a fixture value, the relations between ids kept (a subagent's
  and the `/review` thread's hooks carry the main session id and their own
  rollout; `resume` carries the resumed session's id; `clear` and `fork` carry
  new ones); one built from source, not captured, carries a `fixture_note`
  saying so. A Codex test that needs a payload with keys changed starts from
  these files with `codexPayload`, and never writes a payload inline. The
  relay's Codex requests are `permission-request-*.json`: a shell command
  outside the sandbox, an `apply_patch` outside the writable roots,
  `write_stdin`, an MCP tool, a network-access approval and a denied network
  escalation, beside `permission-request-bash.json` and
  `permission-request-subagent.json`. **Must use:** a test of the relay on a
  Codex row (`hook_codex_relay_test.go`, the `internal/mcp` and
  `cmd/agent-director` relay tests) reads one of them and does not write a
  `PermissionRequest` payload inline.
  These retained fixtures are historical probe evidence. The 2026-10-13
  native Codex 0.159.2 prerelease run observed subagent launch against a local
  mock provider and retained the empty, untracked view; it did not re-capture
  sandbox approvals, `/review` or actual memory consolidation. Those gaps
  establish no new marking, lifecycle or relay rule.
  A test that needs a fixture with keys set or removed, nested ones included,
  builds it with `variant` and the `setKey` and `delKey` edits
  (`hook_subagent_payloads_test.go`), never a JSON literal; a `background_tasks`
  listing is built with `taskEntry` (one running subagent, overrides for a type,
  a status or a wrong-typed id) and `tasks`, or `emptyListing` for an empty
  array, never a hand-written list; one that checks
  that no content reaches the store or a log line uses `sentinelPayload`.
- **Event helpers in tests.** A test outside `internal/store` that applies a
  subagent event directly uses `storefix`'s `ApplySubagent*` and
  `ApplyForeignSubagent*` helpers (`internal/testsupport/storefix/
  subagent_hooks.go`) or `apitest`'s (`pkg/api/apitest/subagent_hooks.go`), and
  `MainAgentStop` with its injected `ReceivedMs` and optional `Snapshot` for a
  turn end (a `SubagentStop`'s listing is `SubagentLifecycleEvent.Listing`;
  `apitest` aliases `SubagentListed` and `SubagentSnapshot`); never SQL of
  its own. Each helper follows the handler's call sequence (the one
  lifecycle transaction, or the ordinary row write followed, when it applied, by
  the entry transaction, with a `Stop`'s skip read over the same turn end), as the row's own agent or,
  for `ApplyForeign*`, as another process, which the gate refuses.

### The `list-subagents` verb

`list-subagents` is the one read of an agent's subagent records: its tracking
flag and every confirmed current-life record across launches, as structured
fields on every machine-readable
surface (CLI, MCP, Go, TypeScript). The verb and the store read behind it are
agent-neutral: they carry no Claude Code name and return the row's tracking
flag and confirmed records through the same read. `tracked` is the row's
`subagent_tracking` flag, which a launch sets by its agent: true for a Claude
launch, whose settings register the subagent events, and false for a Codex
launch, whose settings register none, so a Codex row reads `tracked` false
with `subagents` `[]` (the same answer as a row from before the flag existed,
see "The tracking flag's rules" under [`internal/store`](#internalstore)). What
writes the entries is in [Subagent capture](#subagent-capture); the tables are
under [`internal/store`](#internalstore).

**The verb on each surface.**

- **Manifest** (`pkg/api/manifest/manifest.go`): the entry sits right after
  `list`. `Callable` true, `HandleFree` false, one param `instance_id` (string,
  required, non-empty), `ErrorNames` `ErrSpawnNotFound` only. Its `Description`
  is one sentence of 64 B, since it reaches `help` (see "Help size guard" under
  [`pkg/api/manifest`](#pkgapimanifest--verb-registry)). Its result fields are
  `tracked` (`bool`) and `subagents` (`[]object`), both `Nullable` false and
  `AllowEmpty` true; the elements' fields, the value sets of `state`,
  `close_reason`, `parent_type` and `run_mode`, the order and the time form are
  said in `subagents`' `Description` (`subagentsDescription`), which reaches
  `surface.json`, `docs/cli-reference.md` and `docs/mcp-reference.md` and never
  `help`.
- **CLI** (`cmd/agent-director/spawn_cmd.go`): `listSubagentsHandlerWith`, the
  `list-subagents` key of `handlers()`, takes `--instance-id` and prints the
  `Client.ListSubagents` result on one line. A flag-parse error, an unknown flag
  and a missing or empty `--instance-id` are `ErrInvalidFlags`; an unknown id is
  `ErrSpawnNotFound`, written by `writeVerbError`.
- **MCP** (`internal/mcp/dispatch.go`): the `list-subagents` case of
  `LiveDispatcher.Call` decodes `instance_id` through `decodeParams`, as `get`
  does, and calls `Client.ListSubagents`. A missing or empty `instance_id`
  reaches the store and is `ErrSpawnNotFound`, as for `get`; an unknown key is
  refused by `checkParamNames`.
- **Go** (`pkg/api/list_subagents.go`): `Client.ListSubagents(id)` returns
  `ErrClientClosed` on a closed client and otherwise calls
  `api.ListSubagents(ListSubagentsStore, id)`, which takes no `RelayView` and no
  settle time. `ListSubagentsResult` is `Tracked` and `Subagents
  []SubagentRecord`. Every field of `SubagentRecord` is in the JSON with no
  `omitempty`: `SubagentID`, `InstanceID` and `State` are strings, the other
  text fields are `*string` and the four times `*time.Time` (UTC), each a nil
  pointer, encoded `null`, when nothing supplied it. Every failure returns
  `Tracked` false and a fresh non-nil empty slice, so the error result still
  encodes `subagents` as `[]`.
- **TypeScript** (`pkg/ts-bun-client/src/`): `Client.listSubagents(params)`
  (`internal/subprocessClient.ts`) runs `list-subagents --instance-id <id>`
  (`buildListSubagents` in `internal/argv.ts`) and returns the parsed stdout.
  `ListSubagentsParams`, `ListSubagentsResult` and `SubagentRecord`
  (`types.ts`, re-exported by `index.ts`) mirror the Go types: times are
  strings, unknown values `null`. The verb is in `VERBS` right after `list`.

**One result everywhere.** A time is encoded by `millisToUTC` (`pkg/api/get.go`),
the conversion `launch_started_at` uses, so the CLI, MCP, Go and TypeScript
results are the same JSON: RFC 3339 in UTC with the millisecond fraction,
trailing zeros dropped, no fraction on a whole second, ending `Z`.
`subagentRecordOf` projects a stored `SubagentRow` onto a `SubagentRecord`.

**Old names.** `instance_id` is the only param, and its old name is refused
like every verb's, by the shared table (see [Refusal of old names](#refusal-of-old-names)):
the CLI by `flagErr` (`oldnames.RefuseFlag`), MCP by `checkParamNames` and the
TypeScript client by `refuseOldKeys`. The verb added no row to the table.

**Read-only.** The verb takes no write lock, writes nothing, emits no trail
record and changes no `row_version`.

**The store read.** `(*store.Store).ListSubagentRecords(instanceID)`
(`internal/store/subagent_read.go`) is the one read behind the verb; `pkg/api`
names it as `ListSubagentsStore`. It returns the row's `subagent_tracking` flag
and its records from one statement, so the two are one consistent read. The
flag for a non-Cursor row reads `true` only when the column is the integer 1, as the hook gate and
`GetSpawn` read it; any other stored value, a text or `NULL` one included, reads
`false` and is never an error. The statement is a
`LEFT JOIN` of the row to its `confirmed = 1` entries whose `life_number`
equals `spawns.life_number`, across launches of that life and in any state.
Earlier-life entries remain stored and count toward the all-life cap, but
are hidden. The same subagent id can have a separate entry in another life;
it is unique among the records returned. It orders by `first_started_at`
ascending with `NULL`
last, then `subagent_id`. A non-Cursor row with no record gives the flag as stored and an
empty non-nil slice, so a row from before the upgrade is `false` with none. A
row that does not exist is an error matching `ErrSpawnNotFound`. It never
selects an observation (an unconfirmed entry) or a claimable launch, and it
waits for another process's write lock at most the store's busy timeout, as
`GetSpawn` does. A Cursor row always returns tracking `false` and an empty non-nil slice,
even if its stored flag is 1 or stored records exist: the SQL forces its
flag to 0 and excludes its joined records. Other agents retain the decoding
and current-life filtering above. A `SubagentRow` carries the table's record fields (times as
integer milliseconds, a nil pointer for `NULL`) and no internal column.

**Must use:**

- **The subagent read.** Every reader of subagent records goes through
  `ListSubagentRecords` (or `api.ListSubagents` above it): no other SQL on the
  `subagents` table, no second order, no second filter for which entries count
  as records. A new surface or an agent's later listing calls it, never a
  `SELECT` of its own.
- **The time and record conversion.** A `pkg/api` result that reports a stored
  millisecond time as a time uses `millisToUTC` (`optMillisToUTC` for a
  nullable one), so every such time encodes alike; a result that reports a
  subagent record builds it with `subagentRecordOf`, never field by field. The
  error result of a verb that returns a list is built with the verb's own
  `empty…Result` (`emptyListSubagentsResult`), so an error never encodes a
  list as `null`.

### Settle time (b.3ie)

**The rule.** `[state] settle_ms`, the settle time T (whole milliseconds,
0 to `config.MaxStateSettleMs`, 60000; 0 or a missing key is off), applies
to the `state` that `status`, `get` and `list` report on every surface
(CLI, MCP, the TypeScript client through the CLI, the Go `Client`):

- With T > 0, `state` moves to a new value only once that raw value has
  held for T; until then it reports the last settled value. There is no
  `settling` value or in-flight marker for own-state settling, and the reported
  value is always one the row's raw history held.
- Every raw change of value restarts the clock, a change no poll would
  have seen included; a write of the same value (`working → working`, a
  duplicate hook) and a soft refresh do not.
- **Flapping.** A raw A→B→A inside T reads A throughout: a working agent
  that flips to `waiting` and back reads `working`. A chain A→B→C inside T
  reads A, then C once C has held for T from the B→C change.
- **At once.** A raw `ended` or `missing` reports at once, a hook's
  included, so a dead agent never reads as alive for T. So does every
  command state change outside authenticated Cursor request admission:
  `InsertPending` (spawn), `EndHeldLaunch`
  (spawn's held name), `find-missing`'s mark and its `check_permission`
  repair, `MoveToPending` and `RestoreAfterFailedResume` (`resume`),
  `ResetForReuse` and `RestoreAfterFailedReuse` (spawn with the reuse
  opt-in). Such a value becomes the last settled value at once: a caller
  that has just run `resume` reads `pending`, never `ended` for another T.
  `InsertCursorRequest` instead uses the settling-write category described
  under [Settle time](#settle-time-b3ie).
- **Hooks out of a terminal state settle.** For Claude/Codex the hook gate checks only the
  hook's parent process, and a row keeps its pane through `find-missing`'s
  mark and the ended transition, and gets it back from resume's restore, so
  the row's own agent can move a row out of `missing` or `ended` (its
  SessionStart sets `waiting` whatever the prior state; `hook_gate_test.go`
  has a row marked `missing` before its agent reported in). Such a move is
  a hook write and settles: the row reads `missing` or `ended` for T, then
  the live value. Never state that hooks do not leave a terminal state.
- **Off preserves existing fields.** With T = 0 or unset, `stateExpr` gives
  the bare `state` column. Existing result fields keep their values; the
  additive `family_state` reports the raw aggregate. The settle-off goldens pin this contract
  (`cmd/agent-director/testdata/settle_off/`, with the MCP and TypeScript
  tests over the same store).

**Computed at read time.** The reported state is a pure expression over the
row's three columns and the reader's T and clock (see "v8 columns" under
[`internal/store`](#internalstore)): no daemon, no timer, nothing that must
run when a quiet period ends. Writers stamp each raw change inside their own
statement with SQLite's clock; readers take the Client's clock before their
one SELECT. No read waits for a state to settle, so no accepted T can push
a caller past its deadline (the TypeScript client's 30 s
`DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS`, `decide`'s `max_wait_ms`) or change a relay
outcome. A hook's own-state settle columns remain part of its state UPDATE;
the lifecycle transaction also refreshes family history before commit (see
[Family reporting](#family-reporting)).

**Who reads T.** Each process reads the config once: a hook process when it
fires (its T judges whether the state its write replaces had settled) and
a Client when it is built (its T judges what `status`, `get` and `list`
report; the MCP server keeps its T until it restarts). The setting covers
the whole host: every caller using that config, code callers that never
asked for settling included, can read a state up to T late (`pending` for
up to T after an agent reports in, for one), and nothing in the output
marks a state as late.

**A change of T.** Each earlier segment of the raw history is judged with
the T of the write that ended it, the current one with the reader's T
(`WellDefined` in the model). So right after a change of T a value can be
reported that held less than the new T (`lim_tchange_bee`), but never one
the raw history did not hold (`NeverUnsupported`).

**Guards act on the live state.** The settle time is a reporting layer
only. The raw `state` stays what every guard reads: `send-keys`' and
`pause`'s state and relay guards (`pause` runs `send-keys`' `relayGuard`,
b.zdz; the `state` in either verb's `ErrRelayFallenBack` and
`ErrDialogMaybeOpen` `err_details` included), `decide` (its
`ErrRelayFallenBack` `err_details.state` included), `find-missing`'s
live-row read, mark and repair, `resume`, `kill`, `expire`, spawn's
collision pre-check and reuse, and the hook path. So a guard can refuse on
a state `status` does not show yet (`send-keys` refusing a raw `working`
row while `status` reads `waiting`); the refusal is a named error, so the
outcome stays machine-readable. `ad.spawn.state_transition` records raw transitions.

**Not settled (accepted).**

- Permission requests are never delayed: `get`'s and `list`'s
  `permission_requests` (listed while the raw state is `check_permission`)
  and `get`'s `unproven_requests` (listed while the raw state is neither
  `ended` nor `missing`) follow the raw state, and `get-permission` and the
  relay's delivery states never read the settled state, so a caller learns
  of a permission request at once. The settle time changes neither when
  the lists are shown nor which requests they hold: `unproven_requests` is
  every request the agent's hooks have not proven gone, by the agent-specific
  proof rules of [The dialog hold](#the-dialog-hold-step-2c), including "Proofs by agent"
  (a `turn_end` proof covers only requests recorded before the second its
  hook started, b.omt). For up to T a row can read any state, even `ended`
  or `missing` (see **Hooks out of a terminal state settle** above), with
  an open request in `permission_requests`, or `check_permission` with
  `[]`, and a row its agent moved out of `ended` or `missing` can read
  `ended` or `missing` with requests in `unproven_requests`, also for up
  to T. And since a request proven gone no
  longer holds the row (b.omt), the raw state can leave `check_permission`
  while such a request still awaits an answer; the row can then read
  `check_permission` for up to T with that request in neither list
  (`get-permission` still reads it).
- `launch_started_at` follows the raw state: a row whose agent has reported
  in can read `pending` without it for up to T.
- A row with no recorded settled value (`settled_state` `''`, which only a
  hand-inserted row has, since every write path sets it) reports its raw
  state. This fallback is outside the TLA+ model and touches no row a code
  path writes.

**The short-turn limit.** A settled `waiting` agent that gets a message and
replies in less than T goes raw `waiting → working → waiting` but reads
`waiting` throughout, so a polling caller never sees that turn. T stays
short, 1 to 2 s, below the length of a real turn.

**Clock.** Writers use SQLite's clock and readers Go's `time.Now`; both are
the host's wall clock. A step back reads as not settled (a negative age;
safe, and bounded by the step); a jump forward can settle a change early.
The model assumes one clock.

**A polling caller** with T set needs no streak counter: it polls `status`
and acts on each change of `state` (`docs/usage.md`'s "Watch a Spawn's state").

**Model.** `spec/tla/settle/`: `B3ieSettle.tla`, its README (the design,
invariants, mutations and findings) and the run logs of its 32 scheduler
jobs, every verdict as expected (see [Model check (`make
tla`)](#model-check-make-tla)). Its invariants: with T = 0 the reported
state is the raw one; a reported value held raw for at least T or is the
last settled one; terminal and command-written values report at once; no
guard reads the reported state; every reported value is one the raw
history held.

### Family reporting

`family_state` is a separate binary report (`working` or `waiting`) on CLI
and MCP `status`, `get` and every returned `list` row. Go exposes
`StatusResult.FamilyState`, `SpawnRow.FamilyState` and `ListRow.FamilyState`;
TypeScript exposes `family_state` on `StatusResult`, `GetResult` and
`ListRow`. The manifest and generated references describe the same field.

**Membership and raw authority.** `familyAggregateSQL`
(`internal/store/family.go`) carries working membership upward through stored
`parent_id` links at every depth, including retained `ended` and `missing`
intermediates, excluding only their own contribution. Any live member with
raw state other than `waiting` makes the family `working`; otherwise,
including no live members, it is `waiting`. Refresh and migration join the
materialized aggregate with `UPDATE ... FROM`. Native subagent records do
not participate. Filters and limits select returned rows, never their
family members. Resume, reuse, restore,
reparenting and deletion use the relationships currently stored; deleted
ancestry is not reconstructed.

**v12 durable history.** Each `spawns` row appends `family_state TEXT NOT
NULL DEFAULT ''` (raw aggregate), `family_settled_state TEXT NOT NULL
DEFAULT ''` (retained settled aggregate), and `family_changed_ms INTEGER
NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (raw aggregate change in epoch milliseconds). They
are independent of the v8 own-state history. New rows initialize to their
raw aggregate. The authorized `migrateV11toV12` hop
(`internal/store/family_schema.go`) validates pre-existing column names,
types, nullability, defaults and primary-key shape before adding missing
columns. It validates binary-or-empty history values and an integer clock,
initializes empty history from the full tree and preserves compatible
established history. DDL, initialization and stamp share one transaction;
failure rolls back the hop. Fresh DDL converges with it; store identity and
own-state history are preserved. The family-only v12 → v11 recovery recipe
applies to genuine v12 stores; it cannot operate on v13. Recovery is in
[migration-guide.md §5](migration-guide.md#v12--v11-reverses-migratev11tov12).

**Writers must reuse** `refreshFamilies` in `family.go` for every mutation
that changes a member's binary contribution or parent membership.
`execFamily` wraps a single lifecycle statement in `inImmediateTx`, which
refreshes families before commit. The generic bounded `inWriteTx` and
`inWriteTxContext` do not refresh automatically: relevant lifecycle callbacks
use `refreshFamiliesAfterStateChange` to refresh only when the member's
binary contribution changes. Permission-only and authority-only writes,
and contribution-preserving state changes in those callbacks, skip refresh.
Cursor runtime registration, session binding and retirement use guarded
authority-only writes without family refresh. Aggregate changes and
lifecycle changes commit or roll back together, retaining each write's
guarded result. Refresh preserves the history and clock when the aggregate
is unchanged. When it changes, the writer's `settle_ms` judges whether the
preceding aggregate had settled, retaining the earlier settled value
otherwise; SQLite stamps the actual aggregate change under the lock.
An uninitialized aggregate starts settled at its raw value.

**Readers must reuse** `SettleRead.familyExpr`, alongside `stateExpr`, in
the existing status/get/list store reads. With settling off it reads the
raw aggregate. Otherwise it uses the reader's clock and T once, returning
the prior settled family value until the current raw aggregate has held
for T. Both directions settle, including changes from command writes or
terminal exclusions. Depth and member own-state settling add no delay;
short reversals remain invisible. History survives client and process
restarts, so the next read after T needs no intervening polling or timer.
Clock and configuration-change semantics match own-state settling.
Family projection adds no writer lock, write, settle wait or liveness probe.

Existing Cursor read checks, guarded terminal persistence and errors remain
in place. A projected `missing` own state does not remove a member from its
stored family until the terminal write commits. Ancestor own-state and
permission fields remain local to the ancestor; descendant `ask_user` or
`check_permission` affects only the binary family aggregate. Read failures
remain errors. A stored live working row continues to contribute until
existing detection or state changes say otherwise. Family waiting is no
task-success or action-safety guarantee, including while settling briefly
retains waiting after work begins.

## Spawn Parameter Resolution

`spawn` is implemented as a four-stage pipeline, preceded by one id
check in the shared verb layer and, for a caller-supplied id with no
row, followed by the label scan before the launch. The boundaries exist
so each stage can be tested in isolation against synthesized input.

```
  caller params         (CLI flags / MCP tool input / Go / TS client)
       │
       ▼
   ┌──────────────┐   pkg/api runSpawn, SRD SR-9.1: explicit
   │ Explicit-id  │   instance_id with a byte 0x00-0x1f or
   │ check        │   0x7f → ErrInvalidFlags. Runs before any stage.
   └────┬─────────┘   Empty id passes (ApplyDefaults mints one).
        ▼
   ┌─────────┐   template merge: caller fields overlay template
   │ Resolve │   defaults; nil caller field → template value kept.
   └────┬────┘   Agent: the call's, else the template's, else none.
        │        AgentArgs: nil means caller supplied nothing
        │        (template wins, and Resolved records whose agent
        │        the inherited list belongs to); non-nil replaces
        │        wholesale and inherits nothing.
        ▼
   (Opted-in explicit id: one ReadForReuse now; save its answer for
    argument eligibility and ApplyDefaults. No error returned here.)
        ▼
   ┌──────────┐   SRD §7.2: cwd shape/existence/type; relay_mode;
   │ Validate │   agent (invalid, missing); inherited agent_args vs
   └────┬─────┘   the agent; denied flags (Claude's list, CursorArgs, Codex's
        │         argument check); allow/deny/ask
        │         (codex/cursor refused); reserved env keys (HOME, then
        │         AGENT_DIRECTOR_*), malformed keys (empty, '=', NUL),
        │         then effective-Cursor selection; explicit tmux session name. No
        │         side effects on failure. See "The agent: resolution,
        │         ownership and checks".
        ▼
   ┌────────────┐   SRD §7.3: UUID4 if no instance_id;
   │ ApplyDefaults│  <basename(cwd)>-<id[:8]> session name;
   └────┬───────┘   relay_mode from config. Explicit id: one collision
        │           pre-check (SpawnState on a plain path, the saved
        │           ReadForReuse answer on the opted-in path; live row →
        │           ErrInstanceIdCollision; read failure → ErrInternal).
        │           Without the reuse opt-in any existing row collides
        │           here, live or finished (the insert's PRIMARY KEY
        │           catches only a row inserted after this read).
        │           Nothing created on error. Returns an IDCheck.
        │           With the opt-in, a finished row leaves the pipeline
        │           here for the reuse path (see "Reuse of a finished id").
        ▼
   ┌────────────┐   pkg/api scanForLeftover, IDNoRow only (explicit id,
   │ Label scan │   no row of any state): one tmux lookup on the socket
   └────┬───────┘   the caller's environment resolves, creating nothing.
        │           Leftover of this store → ErrTmuxSessionConflict;
        │           Can't tell → its error. A refusal writes no row and
        │           no trust entry.
        ▼
   ┌────────┐   resolve + create the socket's per-user dir (refusal →
   │ Launch │   ErrTmuxNotAvailable, nothing written); mint launch token;
   └────┬───┘   env compose; settings (claude: --settings synthesis;
        │       codex: the per-launch block); the pane command
        │       (claude_path or `claude`; codex_path or `codex`;
        │       fresh Cursor gateway selecting cursor_path or `agent`);
        │       pre-trust (codex: the outcome composed in); pending
        │       insert with launch start, token, socket and launch owner;
        │       one bounded create that labels the session (@ad_owner,
        │       @ad_pane); one conditional identity write (which ends the
        │       launch's hold), else one release of the hold. "duplicate session" →
        │       the held-name path instead: the end write (row → ended),
        │       one re-lookup of the name, the classified error, one
        │       ad.launch.name_held. See "Launch identity".
        ▼
   instance_id, pre_trust, optional dropped_args
   (state stays `pending` until SessionStart fires)
```

The verb returns once the create answers; it never waits for the agent
to report in. The create itself is bounded by the create timeout (see
[Launch identity](#launch-identity)).

### Explicit-id check

`runSpawn` in `pkg/api/spawn.go` calls `validateExplicitInstanceID`
before `spawn.Resolve`. An explicit `instance_id` that contains
any byte 0x00-0x1f or 0x7f returns `ErrInvalidFlags` with the
description "the instance id contains a control character". The id is
never included in the text. Such an id could never carry a valid
`@ad_owner` label: the label parser rejects control characters, and
lookup lines are split on tabs and newlines. The check runs before
template resolution, validation, the collision check and launch. A
rejected id therefore loads no template, reads and writes no store row,
and creates no tmux session, pre-trust write or trail entry. The CLI,
MCP, the Go client and the TypeScript client all reach `spawn` through
`runSpawn`, so every surface returns the same error. An empty or absent
id passes the check, and `ApplyDefaults` mints a fresh UUID4 for it.
Existing rows are not re-checked.

The check lives in `pkg/api` rather than `internal/spawn` because
`ErrInvalidFlags` is declared in `pkg/api`, and `internal/spawn` cannot
import it. Any future code path that accepts a caller-supplied instance
id for `spawn` must go through `runSpawn`, or call
`validateExplicitInstanceID` itself. The byte test is `hasControlChar`
(`pkg/api/spawn.go`), the one predicate behind this check and `resume`'s
refusal of a row whose id has a control character (SR-3.13, see
[Resume](#resume)). **Must use:** any code in `pkg/api` that tests an
instance id for control characters calls `hasControlChar`. Do not write a
second byte loop.

### The agent: resolution, ownership and checks

Every spawn names an agent, `claude`, `codex` or `cursor` (SRD SR-1, SR-2.1, SR-5).
`SpawnParams.Agent` is the per-call value (`--agent` on the CLI, `agent`
on MCP, `agent?` in the TypeScript client); a template file names its
own with the key `agent`. Values compare case-sensitively; an empty one
is "not given".

**Resolution** (`spawn.Resolve`, `internal/spawn/params.go`). The agent
is the call's, else the template's, else none; `Validate` refuses none.
A template's `agent_args` belong to the template's agent. When `Resolve`
inherits a non-empty template list (the call's `AgentArgs` is nil), it
records the template's agent in `Resolved.InheritedArgsAgent`; a call
that supplies its own list inherits nothing and leaves it empty. What
counts as "supplied" differs by surface: Go and MCP honour an explicit
empty list (the spawn gets no agent arguments, and is never refused for
ownership), while the CLI (no arguments after `--`) and the TypeScript
client (an empty array) send nothing, so the template's list is inherited
when its agent is the spawn's and otherwise refused with
`ErrAgentArgsMismatch`.

**Spawn's check order** (`spawn.Validate`, `internal/spawn/validate.go`),
after `validateExplicitInstanceID` and template loading, and before any
side effect:

1. `cwd` (shape, existence, type);
2. `relay_mode`;
3. `validateAgent`: a value other than `claude`, `codex` or `cursor` is
   `ErrAgentInvalid`, none at all is `ErrAgentMissing`;
4. `validateArgsOwnership`: inherited template `agent_args` whose agent
   differs from the resolved agent are `ErrAgentArgsMismatch`; it names
   the template, both agents, and the two ways out (spawn the template's
   agent, or pass the call's own non-empty `agent_args`);
5. `validateSpawnArgs`: denied arguments give `ErrSpawnDeniedFlag`.
   Claude print is checked on the full original list before extraction;
   exact denied long tokens owned as values always refuse. A verified
   finished-agent switch removes session selectors and validates the
   remainder; other paths refuse them. Ordinary Codex paths retain
   `CheckCodexArgs`' first-argument refusal order (see
   [Shared agent argument readers and resume extraction](#shared-agent-argument-readers-and-resume-extraction));
6. `RefuseCursorPermissions` for Cursor, or `RefuseCodexPermissions` for
   Codex: any `allow`, `deny`
   or `ask` entry, from the call or the template, is
   `ErrPermissionsUnsupported`. The question-tool deny entry that
   `disable_ask_user` adds is never a permission-list entry, so it does
   not trigger it;
7. `ValidateExtraEnv(env, agent)` (see
   [Reserved `HOME` in `extra_env`](#reserved-home-in-extra_env-bnas));
8. the explicit tmux session name.

A template that loads has already passed its own checks in
`config.LoadTemplate`, after `relay_mode`: an `agent` outside those three
values is `ErrTemplateMalformed`, and non-empty `agent_args` with no
`agent` is `ErrTemplateAgentMissing`. The path from the launch verbs'
caller to the error is the same on every surface, because all of them
reach `runSpawn`.

**The five errors** are `ErrAgentMissing`, `ErrAgentInvalid`,
`ErrAgentArgsMismatch`, `ErrPermissionsUnsupported` and
`ErrTemplateAgentMissing`. Each is declared beside its kind, re-exported
by `pkg/api/aliases.go`, catalogued in `errnames` (see
[err_name catalog](#err_name-catalog)) and listed in the manifest's
`ErrorNames`: spawn lists all five, `make-template` lists
`ErrTemplateAgentMissing` and `ErrPermissionsUnsupported`. The name is
the contract; the description is advice and names the way out.

**The row's agent.** `ComposeLaunch` sets `Row.Agent` from the resolved
agent, so plain spawn's insert and reuse's reset record it; `get` and
`list` show it as `agent` and `status` does not. A finished-id reuse takes the new
spawn's agent, and a failed reuse restores the previous one with the rest
of the row. `resume` takes no agent input: `ComposeRelaunch` uses the
row's agent for latest-only resumes, including Cursor. Cursor reuse and
switches follow the same fresh composition and conditional restore. Missing
latest Cursor recovery can preserve artifacts with a fresh unique id (see
[Cursor caller boundary](caller-contract.md#cursor-operation-boundaries)).

**Advice that names an agent.** Advice for a known row or call names the
agent it applies to: `spawn.AgentSpelling(agent)` ("agent claude
(--agent claude on the CLI)"; for no known agent, the pointer to the
row's agent that `get` shows), `spawn.ReuseSpawn(agent)` (the reuse
opt-in and that agent), `spawn.ReuseRetry(agent)` (the retry that works
for a finished row) and `spawn.ReservedHomeAlternative(agent)` (an
absolute `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` for claude, `CODEX_HOME` for codex, both
when no agent is known). The agent comes from the call or the template
when a spawn is refused, from the row for `resume`, held-name and
reuse advice (`HeldNameError.Agent`), and from the template for
`make-template`. **Must use:** advice that tells a caller to spawn again
or to set a config folder takes its text from these helpers, passing the
agent; do not spell the opt-in, the agent or the folder variable by hand.

**Launch path.** Past the check list above, the agent decides the launch's
composition (see [Per-agent launch composition](#per-agent-launch-composition)).
A launch's pane command starts with the agent's program:
`claudeProgram(cfg)` (`internal/spawn/launch.go`), `[launch] claude_path`
when set, else `claude` on `PATH`, or `codexProgram(cfg)`
(`internal/spawn/codexlaunch.go`), `[launch] codex_path` when set, else
`codex` on `PATH`. Fresh, reused and resumed Cursor launches use `composeCursorCommand`
(`cursorlaunch.go`) to select `[launch] cursor_path` when set, else `agent` on
`PATH`, and composes the internal pane gateway rather than a direct CLI.
Supported spawn, reuse and resume paths read their program at each launch
and the row stores none of these paths; see `internal/config` for the keys'
rules. `ComposeLaunch` and `ComposeRelaunch` call `launchAgentError`
first: a row whose agent is empty or unknown fails composition with a
wrapped `store.ErrRowAgentInvalid`, before anything is written,
pre-trusted, created in tmux, reset or moved to `pending` (the socket
directory, resolved before composition, may exist). **Must use:** program
selection for a launch goes through `claudeProgram` or `codexProgram`; Cursor argv goes through
`composeCursorCommand`, never a second copy of executable selection.

Pinned by `TestValidateOrder` (`internal/spawn/validate_test.go`),
`TestResolveMergesTemplate` (`internal/spawn/resolve_test.go`) and the
agent cases of the `pkg/api` spawn, resume and make-template tests; the
`epic-13-agents` Docker test plan (listed in `test/docker-epics.txt`)
runs the agent refusals and the `[launch]` path through the CLI with the
stand-in `claude`.

### Per-agent launch composition

Each agent has one composition in `internal/spawn`. Claude/Codex spawn,
reuse and resume launch through it: `ComposeLaunch` for a plain spawn and a
reuse, `ComposeRelaunch` for a resume. A Claude launch composes
`<claude> --settings <inline json> [args]` (`synthesizeSettings`,
`settings.go`; resume puts `--resume <id>` before the settings). A Codex
launch composes the program, the caller's own pass-through arguments and
agent-director's per-launch settings, all on the command line, from
`codexlaunch.go`, `codexsettings.go` and `codexargs.go`. Cursor
`ComposeLaunch` and `ComposeRelaunch` share `composeCursorCommand`, with resume
filtering saved selectors and carrying only the private latest load target
(see [Cursor gateway](#cursor-gateway-and-current-launch-binding)). A future agent
adds its composition at these two entry points (its program, its
argument check, its settings, its environment and its pre-trust) and
never assembles an argv elsewhere.

Cursor composition uses resolved `ExtraEnv` for fresh/reuse and saved row
`ExtraEnv` for resume. `ValidateCursorEnv` defends both entry points before
transport or mutation; directory/profile policy and per-create/runtime ambient
exclusion are owned by [Cursor environment authority](#cursor-gateway-and-current-launch-binding).

The Codex composition has these parts. Each is one function or table,
and the others call it.

- **Program selection.** `codexProgram(cfg)`, as for Claude's
  `claudeProgram`: `[launch] codex_path` as one unchanged argument, else
  `codex` found on the pane's `PATH`; read at each launch, never stored.
- **The argument check.** `CheckCodexArgs(args, questionToolOff)` is
  step 5 of spawn's check order (see [The agent: resolution, ownership
  and checks](#the-agent-resolution-ownership-and-checks)) and gives
  `ErrSpawnDeniedFlag` for the first refused argument. It and the
  composer read an argument list only through `ReadCodexArgs`, the one
  reader of what is an option, a value, a prompt word and the first `--`,
  so they cannot disagree. The refusals are two tables,
  `codexConfigRefusals` (`-c` keys at, above or under `hooks`,
  `tui.disable_paste_burst`, `features.hooks`, and, only while
  `disable_ask_user` is on, the two question-tool keys) and
  `codexFeatureRefusals` (`--disable hooks`, and the question-tool
  `--enable` while the setting is on), plus the Codex subcommand names
  (`codexSubcommands`) in command position and `--remote` and
  `--remote-auth-token-env`. An option form is refused even after the
  first `--` (the check reads options there too), while a subcommand
  name after it is only a prompt word and passes. `Validate` reads
  `Resolved.DisableAskUser`, the composer reads
  `cfg.Defaults.DisableAskUser`; both values come from the same loaded
  config. `resume` never calls the check.
- **One composer.** `composeCodexCommand` (spawn and reuse) and
  `composeCodexResumeCommand` (resume) both build the settings through
  `codexSettingsBlock` and place them with `codexArgvTail`: after the last
  pass-through argument before the first `--`, so everything from the
  `--` on stays the prompt, and after every pass-through option, so
  agent-director's settings win (Codex applies the last `-c` of a key and
  every `--enable` and `--disable` after every `-c`). A resume's argv is
  `<codex> resume <session id> [filtered args] <block> [-- prompt]`: nothing
  of agent-director's stands before `resume`. The block leaves out
  `--no-daemon`, `--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust` and
  `--enable write_stdin_approval` when the arguments already carry them
  before their first `--`, because Codex rejects a repeat of the first
  two.
- **The settings builder.** `CodexSettingsArgs` is pure: it takes the
  running binary's path, the installed path, the effective relay window,
  the two config settings, the folder and the pre-trust outcome, and
  returns the arguments in argv order. Its parts are the hook-entry
  builder (`codexEntries`: eight events, `codexHookEvents`, the help
  entry as group 1 of `SessionStart` and the deny group as group 1 of
  `PreToolUse`), the shell quoting of a path in a hook command
  (`codexQuotePath`) and the trust-hash computation (`codexHandlerHash`
  over `codexIdentityJSON`, which writes the identity JSON by hand
  because Go's `encoding/json` escapes characters Codex's does not).
  `hooks.state` carries one hash per handler, at its real group and
  handler position, so Codex lists every entry as trusted. The shell
  quoting and the hash are the parts a Codex release can break
  silently, so they are checked against data Codex itself produced (see
  [Hook-trust golden data](#hook-trust-golden-data-reusable-test-data)).
- **The question tool.** While `[defaults] disable_ask_user` is on, the
  block carries the deny group (`codexDenyCommand`, a plain shell command
  with matcher `request_user_input_async`, exit 2) and, last,
  `tools.experimental_request_user_input.enabled=false`. Nothing after
  that setting can turn the tool back on, and the argument check refuses
  the caller arguments that would.
- **`write_stdin_approval`.** Every launch carries
  `--enable write_stdin_approval`, for every launch of every row; a
  caller's `--disable write_stdin_approval` is not refused.
- **The launch environment.** `composeEnv` adds, for a Codex agent only,
  `AGENT_DIRECTOR_AGENT=codex` (`EnvAgent`, `EnvAgentCodex`; the
  `AGENT_DIRECTOR_` prefix is reserved, so `extra_env` cannot set it) and
  an empty `BASH_ENV`, which a `BASH_ENV` in `extra_env` overrides.
  `CODEX_HOME` is never set here: it comes only from `extra_env`.
- **The pre-trust outcome.** The folder trust and the hook-trust bypass
  are in the argv only on `ok`, so the outcome is decided during
  composition by `CodexPreTrust` (a pure function) and carried out of it
  (`ComposedLaunch.PreTrust`, `ComposedRelaunch.PreTrust`).
  `RunPreTrust` runs after composition succeeds: for Claude it is
  `PreTrust`, for Codex it reports the carried outcome (and prints the
  one warning for `failed`), so the outcome a caller reads is the one the
  argv was built for. See [Workspace-trust pre-write](#workspace-trust-pre-write).
- **No I/O.** Composition reads and writes no file, in a Codex folder or
  anywhere, takes no lock and makes no tmux call. Its only failure is a
  binary path that cannot be resolved (`executablePath`,
  `helpHookBinPath`), as for Claude's settings, so a composition failure
  writes nothing.

**Must use:** a launch of an agent goes through `ComposeLaunch` or
`ComposeRelaunch`, which call the agent's composition. A Codex argv comes
only from `composeCodexCommand` or `composeCodexResumeCommand`, and a
Codex hook command or trust hash only from `CodexSettingsArgs`'s
builders; never build an argv, a `-c` value, a quoted command or a hash
by hand, and never read a pass-through list with a second parser: use
`ReadCodexArgs`. A new Codex setting goes in the block before the
question-tool setting, which stays last. A new agent adds its program
selection, its argument check in `Validate`, its composer and its
pre-trust outcome at the same two entry points.

### Shared agent argument readers and resume extraction

`internal/spawn/claudeargs.go` and `codexargs.go` provide the pure,
non-validating readers `ReadClaudeArgs` and `ReadCodexArgs`. `ArgOption`
records the original `Index`, bare `Name`, `Canonical` name, full token
`Spelling`, decoded `Values`, detached `ValueIndices`, and byte bounds
`ClusterStart` / `ClusterEnd` for an option and its attached value in a
short cluster. `Known` distinguishes verified registrations from the
valueless fallback for unknown options. `After` marks Codex's policy
reading after `--`; those tokens are operands for extraction. Both readers
retain original positional and delimiter indices. Codex additionally
records the original `Command`, `SessionID` and `Prompt` positions, so
removal never guesses these roles from shifted argv indices.

Claude's `claudeOptionTable` (`claudeoptions.go`) contains all 126 root
registrations independently verified at 2.1.296, including the 122 at
2.1.280. Codex's value/flag tables and positional finalization were checked
independently at historical endpoints 0.156.0 and 0.162.1. Provenance,
complete endpoint tables,
embedded Commander traces, native Codex probes and upstream source hashes
are in the external probe's `b.ssz/probe/resume-parsers-20261013/findings.md`
and `claude-validator-review.json`, alongside `answers.md`. Update tables
from actual parsers at the pre-release check; runtime reads no agent help.
The 2026-10-13 prerelease checks used only installed native Codex 0.159.2
and Claude Code 2.1.296 and found no table or extraction correction. Claude's
embedded-parser traces use a registration adapter; native missing-value and
help probes independently check arities, but do not establish authenticated
cloud or session eligibility. These checks do not relabel the historical
captures as current runs; their sanitized evidence is in external
`b.ssz/prerelease/task1/` and `task2/`.

Required Claude values own even a dash-prefixed token or `--`; optional
values consume a following non-option token; required lists own their first
value and subsequent non-option tokens. Attached values keep their original
spelling, including the leading equals in `-r=S1`. Exact short registrations
such as `-d2e` precede cluster splitting. A value-taking short option owns
the remaining suffix: `-dc` is debug value `c`, `-nrocket` is name value
`rocket`; `-cd` is continue plus debug, and `-pc` is print plus continue.
`--model -c` and `--append-system-prompt --resume foo` retain their owned
values in the reader; spawn nevertheless refuses the latter's exact denied
long token. Spawn's `refuseClaudePrint` inspects the full original list,
including parsed clusters and exact long tokens owned as values, before any
extraction. Unknown options are treated as valueless; this policy does not
guarantee ownership or selector recognition for later agent options.

`resumeargs.go` owns the canonical selector sets:

| Set | Members |
| --- | --- |
| `ClaudeResumeArgs` | `--resume` (`-r`), `--continue` (`-c`), `--fork-session`, `--from-pr`, `--teleport`, `--resume-session-at`, `--resume-drops-turn`, `--rewind-files`, `--reply-on-resume`, `--cloud`, `--remote`, `--attach-serve` |
| `CodexResumeArgs` | command-position `resume` / `fork`, their `--last` / `--all`, and `--include-non-interactive` for `resume` only |
| `CursorResumeArgs` | `--resume` (optional chat id), `--continue`, first-command `resume`, `--new-session-id` (required value), verified at `2026.09.28-64d2043` |

Claude's `--session-id` creates a new session and is outside the selector
set. Codex command names in option values or prompt text are not selectors.
`--last` makes the first operand the prompt instead of a session id.
Codex extraction protects surviving prompt tokens behind an unowned `--`,
keeping each original token intact; it never joins or splits prompt text.
Cursor extraction uses `ReadCursorArgs`, preserving model/mode and recognized
required-value ownership even for refused sandbox/auth/header/exclusion
options, and literal operands after `--`. Required values own dashed tokens;
optional `--resume` consumes only a following non-dashed token. It assumes no
short selector aliases and leaves saved arguments unchanged. Its public
selector contract is owned by
[Cursor operation boundaries](caller-contract.md#cursor-operation-boundaries).

`ExtractResumeArgs(agent, args)` returns copied surviving `Args`, `Dropped`
original token spellings in argv order, and parsed `Removed` options.
It removes selectors and their owned values. For Claude, parsed-role
preservation requires every recognized required scalar or variadic option
in the original reading to have its required value. If any lacks one, even
